title: Good for deep sleepers who can’t make good decisions in the morning
body:
I’m a rlly heavy sleeper so my confused, groggy mind in the morning would always turn off my alarm in the morning or hit snooze. Sometimes I wouldn’t even hear the alarms and just continue sleeping. 

However, after downloading Alarmy, there has been literally no option to turn it off other than doing the activity, which literally requires me to get out of bed and do it within the time limit. I definitely recommend the QR code scanning feature or the ai treasure hunt to force u to get out of bed every morning. Moreover the alarm is extremely loud when at max volume.

This app has been so annoying it’s always compelled me to delete it in the morning, which I feel is a good thing HAHAHA. But ofc I  will try not to, and for the past.. 14 days I think? This app has actually helped me get out of bed within two minutes of waking up which is like CRAZY according to my standards.

title: great app with a lot of features but unreliable
body:
I really wanted to love this alarm app because it comes with some amazing features. The ability to scan a barcode or solve math questions to dismiss the alarm is super effective—it actually forces me to wake up and think instead of just snoozing it half-asleep. These features really helped me form better morning habits.

However, the biggest issue is that half the time, the alarm doesn’t even ring. It only shows a notification in the notification center that the alarm is going off, but there’s no sound at all. This has caused me to oversleep multiple times, which defeats the entire purpose of an alarm app.

If the developers can fix this major bug and ensure the alarm rings every time, this would easily be a 5-star app. Until then, it’s frustrating to rely on something that’s so inconsistent.

title: A miracle. (If it works)
body:
Update 27 Dec 2018: Apparently it was claimed that sometimes ios causes Alarmy to not ring when on silent mode, despite going through all necessary failsafes. But I've noticed considerable improvements as I don't really get the below issue often anymore, so bumping up another star for this great app!

Update 15 Oct 2018: not sure whether it's ios12 or alarmy but alarm doesn't work well when phone's on silent mode. AND YES I'VE READ THE FAQS. Still a decent app except I may get woken up sometimes by notifications nowadays (disabled DND permanently as well to avoid forgetting considering I wake up at different timing sometimes.) Oh Wells 

I have been late for almost 99% of my life for anything. 

Some of them includes:  weddings(not mine, yet), exams, bday parties, even important job interviews, and even though not everything is due to me not being able to walk up, most of these things happen early in the morning. And I ABHOR sleeping early. (I average 4 hours sleep everyday for at least 2 decades already)

To make matters worse, my brain gets used to the same sound very fast, and since I'm used to snooze (trust me if I disable snooze now you might as well kill me), it gets conditioned easily to turn off the alarm subconsciously, resulting in most alarm clocks, including iPhone to be useless in a matter of months (unless I keep changing the ring tone, but meh) 

So yeah, these two combined makes it a potent life destructing poison.

The above thus makes me the most credible person to review alarmy. And I gotta say its phenomenal how no one else have ever tot of this: alarmy shines when it comes to being stubborn af. Trust me it just won't go away! I've managed to figure out certain "bypasses" but this thing WILL stay on until you are truly off your bed. I once set an alarm with take a picture to disable and accidentally activated it while I was out.

There was nothing I could do to shut it off Sans uninstalling it. And I'm glad my brain has yet to reach that level of sentience. 

Until then this thing is a gem at helping me to be less late (Yeah that's how bad it is for me). My case is serious but alarmy is truly a godsend, second only to professional help. 

10 STARS!

title: Absolutely amazing. It was so much easier waking up until...
body:
(Problem is in the 4th paragraph if you have no time reading)

I’m a student who has stained my record permanently just because I have been late THAT many times. 

After downloading Alarmy for a whole solid month I wasn’t late for anything at all, not once, and I even started to wake up at 5 instead of 6 to workout before I went to school. My life really changed and all my friends thought I’d been cursed because they were used to seeing me arrive at school when half the day is over. 

HOWEVER, after a few months for some reason the alarm seemed to be getting softer and softer. I thought it was because of Low battery mode, or maybe the fact that my phone tended to get buried in my blankets sometimes which would muffle the sound, but I remembered that previously it was way louder and those two factors did not affect it at all. 

To clarify, there is a difference between how loud the alarm rings when it first rings and after I try to dismiss it. After I try to dismiss it, the alarm then starts to ring as loud as my phone can, so there’s no issue there. My problem lies with the loudness of the alarm when it first rings, before I press dismiss. 

It’s so soft that i can’t be woken up by it at all. My entire household and my neighbours used to be woken up by this demon of an alarm but now literally no one is. It’d just keep ringing for 6 hours or so, then my phone runs out of battery. 

Is there a way for me to change this? And if there isn’t a way, would it be possible to have an option for the initial ringing to sound as loud as the ringing after trying to dismiss the alarm? Thanks!

title: Alarmy: 1 | Insomnia: 0
body:
I’ve had insomnia my entire adult life. So if my nightly drug combo is on point, the stars align, and a butterfly doesn’t flap its wings in the Amazon, I sleep like the dead. 

The default iPhone alarm app is either too polite to disturb me, or it just doesn’t have the thrust I need to re-enter earth’s atmosphere. It’s also super helpful that Alarmy’s sounds are different from those of standard alarm apps (or any other kind of app, for that matter). I started with the aptly titled “End of the World,” and it worked like a charm, but there’s a bunch of other enticing options. 

Tl;dr: Get Alarmy. It WORKS!!

title: Loved/Love this App, But the Ads Have Gotten Insane
body:
I’ve never written an app review before, but I’m frustrated enough that here I am. I can’t state enough how helpful this app has been, it works incredibly well and has been one of the only ways I can wake up to an alarm! Genuinely life changing. 

HOWEVER, the ads have gotten increasingly incessant and it’s getting to the point where I can’t use the app :(. When I first got the app this year, the ads were minimal and acceptable. My main concern is the immediate pop up add after you complete a task. Like many people, immediately after I’ve woken up I’m still a bit confused/sleepy, and I keep mistaking the multiple very sketchy pop-up ads as another task to complete, or I try to close the ad but miss the tiny exit button. I’m scared I’ll get a virus by accidentally clicking one of these weird ads. 

Like I said before, I really appreciate this app, and want to continue using it, but the ads have gotten ridiculous. Please fix this.

title: Background Usage
body:
You have to make sure to close the app and not have it running in the background because it eats up your battery. I thought it was my battery that had gotten bad when my charge would drop significantly despite the lack of screen time, but when I saw what was eating up my battery, it turned out to be just this app.

It’s only mid-day and my setting already showed 9 hours of it running in the background. This is a common problem after doing some googling, and it’s honestly sketchy with how much data and battery it uses in the background. Whatever it could be, it’s just inconvenient and requires your phone to be plugged in just in case your phone loses all its battery overnight.

title: I hate it. That’s why I love it
body:
I never leave reviews

I absolutely hate this app in the morning— which is exactly what I need. It forces you up, even when you don’t want to. 

The barcode scanner is excellent! For those that don’t know, in order to stop the alarm, you have to scan a barcode of your choosing. That’s the only way to turn the alarm off. I scan the barcode on the back of my coffee container in my kitchen… now that I’m up, I might as well make some coffee and get the day started 🤷‍♂️

If you can’t be woken up, constantly hit snooze, turn your alarm off and fall back to sleep. THIS IS THE APP FOR YOU. 

Absolutely phenomenal

title: What. The Hell.
body:
This app is great 80% of the time. It has failed me a handful of times. Two of maybe four times has simply NOT gone off was for flights. I almost missed TWO FLIGHTS because of this app. It was just luck that I woke up and raced there in time. And I wake up and grab my phone and then—oh right! It’s supposed to be ringing! And it starts ringing when I’m already awake and have opened my phone.

And that’s just the fantastic part. It’s inundated with ads, it has all of these weird side ‘jobs’ it tries to do. Why is there a weird pet thing, and four different windows?? This is supposed to be an ALARM app, but over the past couple of years, it has tried to be EVERYTHING ELSE, TOO. And poorly. You can’t do everything well and this app proves it on the daily.

I’ve been using this for years and am sure I will keep using it out of habit. But I do not recommend getting hooked on it now if you have the opportunity not to start.

title: Works Great, Tons of Ads
body: This has been my go to alarm app since 2017. With all the different sounds and problem solving options available, it really worked for my case. However, since I’ve had the app for so long, I’ve been able to see its growth and change. And while it hasn’t changed much, the addition of ads and the amount added have increased greatly. This app used to be ad free and very clean. Now, with all the ads, it’s like the developers  tried to cram as much in as possible. It’s all along the sides, in your face, and even in areas where you don’t expect. For example, when you turn off your alarm, an ad appears with various options to click. You can either choose to open it (white lettering), choose to open it again (red lettering), or in the very bottom in small font choose to close it (grey lettering). They deceive you because the red lettering looks like the option to close the ad but in fact it’s another option to open the ad. What i’m getting at is that the app is so loaded with ads, it feels frustrating to use, especially when turning it off. It’s a bummer because I really liked this app.

title: Love your app, but have suggestion!
body:
Hey! I love this app it's really helped me wake up, but I've ran into an issue. I wake myself up with math equations but I realized something- my desire to keep sleeping has caused me to become really good and fast at solving the problems. I'd up the difficulty, but then i'd just get good at doing that half asleep. THAT GAVE ME AN IDEA!!

What if you added a FLASHCARD option? People could create custome flash cards and choose to be woken up answering a random flashcard question the user wrote in advance. The app could give multiple choice options or have the person write the term. That way, you wake up on time but if you don't, you get really good at what ever studies you're lacking in instead!! Either way you win!! If this was implemented it would be a life saver for me and many other students, so I hope you'll consider it! :)

title: Great app but BUT ADS😡
body:
I have been using this app for probably 3-4 years at this point and it’s great! I love all the options it gives for challenges, and I think it’s effective! My favorite is the scan barcode alarm challenge, because it forces me to get out of bed. 
BUT OH MY GOSH. THE ADS HAVE BECOME SO BAD. 

Sometimes it seems like the app is like 60% ads and 40% working app. I get that they are trying to force you to purchase premium but it makes me SO angry! 
Unfortunately, I have built my routine with this app. If someone asked me if I recommended it at this point, I would say no because the ads are just way too bad. On top of that, pro membership is so expensive for something that’s literally supposed to be an alarm clock. I don’t think I would mind as much if it was a one time fee, but it subscription feels absurd to me.

author: Genesee Jay

title: HEAVILY Shaming Users
body: I downloaded this app a long time ago and have loved it since then. As someone who struggles to wake up, it’s been a Godsend. I NEVER write reviews and haven’t written a positive one for that reason. However, this latest feature deeply disturbs me. When using the “Say Out Loud” setting, their newest game to open the alarm, I’m made to say sentences aloud that are demeaning and untrue. For example, despite hand selecting the 16 sentences I wanted used, I would be asked to say the same 4 phrases- notably “This is my fault, I am stupid”. I’m in graduate school. I work. I’m a caretaker. A dog mom. Planning a wedding. It’s incredibly hurtful that the first thing I say out loud about myself when waking up is that I am STUPID for being asleep and that it’s my fault, that I’m to blame. I’ve double checked- I don’t have these sentences checked off to use NOR are they even sentence options in the choices, so why are we getting such hateful messages? I’m using this app as a solution, and even though I don’t use that game anymore, I’m still about to delete the app. I don’t want to support a company using shame to wake people up, especially when there is false control over being able to select which sentences are used only for the user to receive the same 4 sentences over and over. I don’t have an issue with the out loud feature itself, I just think you should really look into what the responses are being given to users as this feels hurtful and honestly intentional on the companies part as this isn’t happening with Typing or other games. Do not download or use that setting if waking up and saying rude things about yourself is going to affect your day!

title: Saved my life dude.
body:
Bear with me this review might get long 
As a heavy sleeper who struggles with depression that causes me to resist getting out of bed, this alarm has saved my life. 
First, I love how effective the app is without needing to put any money in. Almost every feature is included on the free plan, which is very appreciated. 
The app does an amazing job at not only waking you up, but forcing you to get out of bed. My biggest problem with regular alarms is I just turn them off and go back to sleep. With Alarmy, you can set it up so the alarm will not disable unless you take a picture of something across the house. And it WORKS. You can’t cheat, either. (I’ve tried) the volume stays at maximum, no matter what adjustments you put on it. And, it’s not an exaggeration to say that the alarm never turns off. I dropped my phone behind my bed with the alarm on, it played loud the entire time I tried to grab it, which took like 30 minutes. 
There are a lot of other features besides the alarms which are useful for people who are trying to improve or understand sleep. You can track how long it takes you to wake up in the morning, and you can track how long you slept. All with one button. All for free. 
There are a lot more features which I haven’t even used. 

TLDR: this app is amazing and not a scam. All the good features are free. As a chronic over sleeper, I haven’t been late to school, practice, or work since downloading.

title: Spare yourselves
body:
I almost never write reviews but this one deserves it. Accidentally closed out so I’m writing this all over again. There are 2 main issues. 

First is that alarmy runs nonstop in the background. It used 42%, 21%, 35%, 27%, and 42% of my phone’s battery in the last five days. My phone’s battery health is currently 83% so it can use close to HALF of your battery in a single day. It requires that you leave background app refresh on to trigger alarms but more so to refresh all those juicy money-making ads which drain your battery. 

Second is that when you turn the alarm off on your lock screen it doesn’t actually turn it off. You have to open your phone and the app to then truly turn the alarm off. And this can break. It might not take you directly to the app around a third of the time. This got increasingly annoying over the 2-3 weeks I’ve used this app. 

I really don’t know how this app is so high rated. I tried alarmy because Apple’s alarm app likes to not trigger alarms randomly over several years. Personally, I’d rather miss an alarm than have a dead phone. Maybe if you pay the money things might get better but these 2 issues will likely remain. Spare yourselves.

title: Worked until it didn’t
body:
The app was consistent for about a week, but one morning I woke up 3.5 hours later than I was supposed to and 2.5 hours after my work shift started. I found that I must have accidentally hit the weather tab in my sleep, which for some reason completely muted/canceled the alarm.

There is no reason that accidentally clicking on a different tab in the same app should make the main purpose of the app fail, even on the free version. This app required a lot on my end, and even on full volume with silent mode off the alarm was decent at best. It woke me up, but I’m sure were I to continue with this app, the low volume of the app would lead to nights where I simply sleep through it.

I will not be continuing with this app. There’s zero reason I should have to pay for a consistent alarm app in the year 2026, and the free version clearly isn’t consistent enough for me to continue to trust it.

title: Ads
body: Wrote a review a while ago but had to come back because it’s still such an issue. I’ve been using this app for over five years and these ads are ridiculous. Going from an app that simply worked as an alarm clock to one that is constantly trying to market a product to you takes away from its purpose entirely. Not to mention, these ads are maliciously placed, specifically in small, easy to click places that you will not see when tired and waking up in the morning. It feels like trying to get rid of a popup ad on a game that will not go away no matter how hard you try. It might not seem like a big deal to new downloaders, but this addition has made my experience significantly worse, especially as I used to use the version without ads. I do not understand why an app would want to prey on its own users like this. I am disappointed.

title: Image privacy policy?
body:
I think the alarm is great and super helpful for waking up. However, my major concern with this app, and why I ultimately will be deleting it, is the household object search (which I find to be the most effective way to wake up). Alarmy provides NO details I’ve been able to find on the data storage and privacy of these images. Alarmy is getting a daily stream of images from inside my home, and has no details on where the image is being evaluated (on my phone vs in the cloud), whether the image is saved or not, and whether advertisers might one day be given information from these images. I would love to continue supporting Alarmy but it’s very troubling that these concerns aren’t proactively addressed by the company.

I don’t find the other “missions” effective so unfortunately switching to those with more limited permissions is not an option.

title: Chronic oversleeping fixed immediately

I’ve been a chronic over sleeper my entire life. It’s caused me to be late to or completely miss school, work, meetings, and appointments. I’d have very short-term success throughout the years in trying to change my sleep schedule to become a morning person.

The amount of value I have received from this app is hard to quantify. I have literally overcome being a late sleeper/riser to waking up at 6:45 AM sharp every single day (weekends included). 

I’ve set my alarms to require me to perform 60 bodyweight squats in order to turn off. 

That should wake anybody up. 

I would recommend Alarmy to my dad‘s sister‘s uncle‘s dog’s boyfriend.

title: The only alarm app now that can do what I need
body:
It’s tragic how this is the only app that has been able to do what I need in order to actually wake up and not instantly go back to sleep in a negative mood. It’s pretty good at its main goal, I like how I can put any picture or video as a screen for the alarm I just wish I could actually see it when the phone is locked instead of a blank screen and I have no idea if it’s supposed to work or not because it never has with several different things I’ve tried. The best part about the app is the ability to put an entire song as an alarm from your files and it is currently the only app now for Iphone that I can find that does that for “free” Yeah the ads are “questionable” to say the least sometimes like I definitely don’t support some of the things I’ve seen  but it’s kinda hard to avoid and tragically horrible people still have free speech so what can I do besides spread the word to stay educated. The pop ups are annoying but I guess they need to pay for the app somehow, just wish they used the on screen ads only and didn’t have pop ups that make me accidentally click them. 
My biggest problem is that I HAVE to have the app open always or it’ll change all my audio to be the default triggering audio and I have to readd every single file, that has happened twice and I have no idea how to avoid it when I unconsciously close apps sometimes or reopen them to refresh them so it’s just inevitable. Also several times when trying to add a personal sound file or delete and readd one the app completely freezes and I have to reopen it and try again. I don’t really use the other features of the app so I can’t accurately rate them but I did try a few small ones; The tarot cards are cool and I enjoy them when I remember they exist, the quotes are a good addition just some of them seem random and I don’t know how they could seem like uplifting quotes but who knows all words could be subjective and the last thing I tried was the little pet which I find unnecessary but cute if you want it, I just sort of wish I could hide it from that screen because I don’t want a little egg telling me to feed it when I don’t care but whatever that’s the least of my concern. It’s a good concept but it amazes me just how many of these kinds of apps can’t simply do the thing easily without all these issues I have tried over 10 apps by now and this one is somehow the best one on apples app store, wish I could download android apps and stuff but no everything is a rivalry and difficult so this is it for me. If you really struggle with sleep I recommend this app but if you just want to try a different app or want audio longer than 30 seconds I honestly say it might not be worth all the issues. If you don’t mind dealing with all the problems and having to keep all your audio still accessible in your phones files then try it.

title: This app is a good option for those who are heavy sleepers, have IH or Narcolepsy!
body: As someone with Hypersomnia (the opposite of insomnia, think Narcolepsy) this app has been very helpful to me. There are a large variety of things you can choose to have to have to do in order to turn your alarm off, pretty much all of these options require you to have to start using your brain — making it harder to just hit snooze or tap dismiss. Additionally, there are options that require you to physically move which are the most helpful ones for me. Particularly the option where you have to scan a barcode of a certain item you’ve previously chosen to turn off the alarm. I choose to do something across the room or in another room near by. Like any app, it does have its quirks, but this is honestly the best alarm app I’ve found so far. The premium version is a plus, but you don’t NEED it, the baseline features are good, too. If you have Narcolepsy or IH/Hypersomnia, as someone who’s used this app for the past year, I would recommend this app!

title: PLEASE HELP 😭
body:
I’ve loved this app for years. 
I downloaded it because I had a career where my start times varied wildly from day to day. I needed an alarm I couldn’t easily ignore and Alarmy checked all the boxes. The updates have historically brought better features time and time again. Every time I hear someone say they slept through their alarm I recommend Alarmy. 
That all just changed. 
I hadn’t used the app in a couple weeks as I was on vacation and didn’t have to get up until I felt like it. 
Today I had a dentist appointment I could not miss. I opened the app last night and immediately it hung up on the loading screen. I shut it down, cleared the app from my operations, and tried to open it again. 
No luck. 

I rebooted my phone and opened the app again. 
No luck. 

I guessed there may have been an update. There was. I updated and tried to open the app again. 
Again it hung up on load. 

I deleted the app from my phone and reinstalled it. 
This time I was able to get through initial setup and permissions, although it forced me to accept app tracking which was disappointing. It said I could change it later in settings, so I accepted tracking (under duress) I love this app. 

It allowed me to set just ONE alarm before it hung up again. 

When it went off this morning, it got hung up again. It didn’t let me open to the dismal page where I normally solve math problems (a feature I absolutely love because it’s very hard to go back to sleep after having warmed my brain up with maths)
Instead, it immediately silenced the alarm and left a notification stating that the alarm was going off. If I clicked the notification, it opened the loading screen and once again got hung up. 
Each time it gets hung up, the loading screen appears for about 45 seconds before it just disappears. 

I’m using an iPhone 15 pro running iOS 26.4.2

Please tell me if there is a fix, or if I’m overlooking something. I’m confident you’ll help take care of my problems using this app because it’s had such a strong track record. 

Thank you and have a wonderful day. 
~sincerely but panicking 
E. Keebler

title: Charged lifetime subscription half awake
body: I am very disappointed at the recent changes to this app that I have used for over two years now. The new user interface and changes to the app have made the subscriptions pop up predatory.  I was trying to finish a math challenge and was barely awake, as I was trying to turn off the next alarm because I ran out of time falling back asleep, the app popped up the subscriptions option as the next alarm went off and with my eyes closed I hit the lock button to snooze the alarm and the app SUBSCRIBED ME FOR 167$ for a lifetime when I was BARELY awake. I do not have money now to pay an important bill due today, and am broke now till this appeal return goes through in 48 hours. I am extremely disappointed and livid that an app that I’ve enjoyed for free and never had a problem with when I’ve had it, has now done such a thing as to take advantage of the users who are trying to wake up and likely am not the only person this is happening to. I want to continue using the app for free but even if I get a refund the UX has become terrible and it’s setup now to take advantage of those on the free version. I’m appalled and I did not want to start my day like this especially when finances are hard right now.

title: Amazing alarm, Will embarrass you
body: Amazing alarm, ensures you can’t just hit snooze. Also ensures to humiliate you should you ever leave one on. “Just lower the volume” they’ve thought of that. For some god forsaken reason this app is capable of cranking the volume back up faster than you can manually lower it, even if you’re practically strangling the down button out of desperation, it will instantly raise it back 3/4th of the max and ignores your input. Additionally if you’re listening to music in your headphones, so is everyone in a mile wide radius. So pray it’s not anything embarrassing. Even if you’re ready, phone in hand, and click it as soon as the alarm activates it takes a few seconds for the app to open and load and then open the alarm itself, and in that 10-20 seconds it will be blaring like an tornado siren. And then you’ll have to explain why you need to complete a puzzle in the middle of a lecture hall or office. Best alarm ever, I hate it. (if they just allowed you to be able to silence it while holding down the volume, or even delay raising the volume back up for 10 seconds to grant you enough time to start the puzzle then it would be close to perfect…… please)

title: Buggy
body:
I really wanted to love this app because the features and overall design are great, and it’s very easy to use. Unfortunately, it’s way too buggy to rely on.

I have an alarm set 5 days a week for work, and at least once a week, the alarm will go off with NO sound. My phone is fully updated and not on silent, so there’s no reason this should be happening. I am always late to work because of this.

I’ve tried reinstalling the app and restarting my phone. I’ve also contacted the developers multiple times, and the response is always the same: “sorry, we’ll work on it,” but nothing ever actually gets fixed.

An alarm app that doesn’t reliably make sound defeats its entire purpose. Until this is fixed, I can’t recommend using it at all.

title: Missions such as QR codes no longer working
body:
I love this this app and have used this alarm faithfully for years, I have recommended the app to many people, and I’m a premium member. However  recently I’ve noticed that the app’s sensors have been off. (For the record, I have an iPhone 17 Pro Max and I keep the app up to date.) It started with the stepping sensors, not tracking steps I took. Then the squat sensor stopped working. As of this morning, the barcode/QR code mission isn’t working. (I tried scanning the code more than five times in the same brightly lit space I always do, and it just wouldn’t recognize the code. Barcode scanning is pretty fundamental and basic. Many apps use it successfully. 

The gradual wake up, wake up checking, ability to choose a variety of noises for the alarm, such as birds chirping, are all still great features. But the sensing that made the missions feasible is failing and I am very disappointed and don’t know why.

body: After my first use, this is the best app. This app literally has every safety in place for everything I’ve done in the past to shut off my alarm. It won’t let you uninstall the app, shut down your phone, and it also has a back reminder to make sure you’re actually up which will trigger another alarm if you don’t acknowledge that you’re awake. That doesn’t include the “missions” set in place to ensure I’m waking up. Overkill? No. I consider it necessary for someone like me who sleeps through 10 alarms in the morning, and I’ve been doing that practically my whole adult life (approx. 18 years). title: спасибо за будильник <3
body:
когда я просыпаюсь рано утром, и слышу свой будильник я его ненавижу всем сердцем, но если я его выключу и не сделаю задание то он будет звенеть дальше , и поэтому мне приходится вставать и искать кью ар коды либо же решать примеры и тд, но после первого же задания я устаю и думаю о том что уже проснулась, ложусь на кровать и со спокойной душой выключаю все остальные будильники и так же благополучно засыпаю, а если быть честной приложение и в правду помогает вставать, но уши привыкают к постоянному звонку по утрам , из за чего мелодию нужно менять, мозг привыкает выполнять задание и ложится спать, но на этот случай меня будит сестра, хотя я сама еще не придумала тактику просыпаться вовремя и не иметь привычку засыпать после звонов будильника, так что я этим всем хочу сказать.. 
1. пожалуйста, не делайте все платным, я так привыкла к этому приложению и желания платить еще за что либо вообще нет, так же как и искать новое приложение
2. добавьте побольше новых красивых рингтонов на будильники, просто «wake up princess» и так далее не очень хорошая идея будильника
3. можно ли как то сделать чтобы я делала задания на заблокированном экране, утром сложновато скукурузить морду которая у тебя обычно для фейс айди, да и плюсом я калькулятором пользуюсь когда лень примеры решать
но приложение и в правду хорошее.. намного лучше обычного будильника, я думаю мне тоже нужно постараться восстановить режим и иметь мотивацию вставать утром, спасибо вам за приложение, надеюсь вы прислушаетесь к моему совету🩷

title: Complete Lifesaver
body: I am awful at waking up for alarms. I sleep through them, I don’t even wake up and snooze. I fully had to buy myself one of those shocking alarm watches which still don’t work if I set them too early because I’ll just take it off and go back to sleep. This app wakes me up. I have to get up very early to get to work, and I have never been late on a day I set the alarm. Being able to set multiple alarms, how loud it is, the different checks, the wake up reminders, even the weather alerts are so incredibly helpful. Also the way you can turn off the alarm and then set it to only turn off is so helpful. If I wake up early, I can turn off the rest of the alarms for the day, and then don’t have to remember to set them again at night. When I got a new phone this was literally one of the first apps I redownloaded. I love this app so much.

title: TERRIBLE FUNCTIONALITY
body:
So from time to time this app works great. 

Other times, it fails to ring, or skips alarms. It auto shuts off sometimes. And then sometimes it starts going off nonstop. I discovered if it auto shuts off and later in the day I connect my iPhone to an aux/charger my phone resumes the alarm for a 30 seconds. Yikes. 

This app has saved me from being late to work. On the other hand, it has also doomed me.


Edit (2026):
If you close the app, you get a notification stating your alarms won’t go off. This is a lie.

Closing the app does one of two things:
1- won’t ring. 
2- Will ring anyway
Regardless, sometimes the app won’t work even when open.

I have stopped relying on this app to reliably work. I have people wake me up instead because it refuses to ring. What is the point of getting premium for half baked functionality.

title: Not reliable
body:
The idea of this app is really great. The tasks that force you to wake up and solve something before turning off the alarm are very helpful, especially for people who turn off alarms in their sleep.

However, the app does not work consistently. Sometimes it works perfectly, but other times it does not. Even when all recommended settings are enabled, the alarm does not always work correctly. About once a month the alarm simply does not go off, which is a serious problem for an alarm clock app.

The concept of the app is excellent, but reliability needs to be improved because people depend on it to wake up on time.

title: Invasive Ads Killed Browser
body: I want to like this app—the alarms themselves work fantastically—but the ads have gotten far too invasive over the last few months. They recently added a “continue snooze with ads” feature that I wasn’t notified of until hitting it by mistake one morning, and the subsequent advertisement jumped to my browser and started a spammy “call now!!” popup loop that crashed it and ruined all of my tab history. There should be a way to opt out of this feature without getting rid of snooze entirely, or at the very least making it so the ads stay confined to the app instead of wormimg their way into other parts of my phone. This should be an Alarm app, not malware.

body: I subconsciously turn my alarms off EVERY morning, this fixed that! I have to say I thought this app would only work for people who live alone. author: LaraeAugust

title: Lost its teeth
body:
I’ve been using this app for years, but they’ve made some recent changes I’m not happy with. It used to not matter if you closed the app or turned off your phone, the alarm would still ring. Now, if you close the app, the alarm turns off. If you reopen the app, the alarm will ring but at the beginning of the snooze cycle. So guess who’s been closing and reopening the app and sleeping through those unlimited snoozes for half an hour?
The other thing I’m upset about is that they’ve added a feature you cannot disable where you get extra snoozes if you agree to watch ads. The ads can be muted, and if you mute your phone they will automatically be silent. Whoever is paying for ads on this app should take their business elsewhere, because people are literally sleeping through them.

This has been my favorite alarm for years. But I think it’s time to find another.

title: Couldn’t get out of bed until I got this.
body:
For context, I struggle with severe depression and anxiety as well as chronic fatigue. I was just using the default Apple alarm app and I kept waking up late or sleeping through it which caused me to miss class and work. 
I heard about this app, so I gave it a try, and it’s made a world of difference. I’m consistently waking up on time, getting out of bed when I need to, and not falling back asleep after hitting snooze. I know this sounds like an exaggeration, but it’s genuinely been so helpful and meaningful to feel like I have control and security in getting up. 
The features are also great. I like the variety of sounds I can choose from as well as the tasks I can do. I like to do a few math problems, then scan one part of my morning routine so I have to get up. I love that I can fine tune the tasks, snooze features, pretty much everything about the alarm. Fantastic app, very user friendly, and absolutely worth the low price. I highly recommend for anyone but especially if getting up feels impossible.

title: Wonderful app, but..
body:
This app works well! Even though it takes me 6 to 10 minutes to finally wake up and turn off the alarm, it does its job. I'm giving this a 4-star rating primarily because of the wide variety of alarms, although many of them are not very effective. For me, listening to a song as an alarm would likely cause me to sleep through it, as it would just blend into my dream. That's where the issue arises—many of the alarms are songs. While there are some more annoying alarms available, I wouldn’t use something like a fire alarm to wake me up. 

The only effective alarm I’ve found so far is “Orkney.” It’s not too jarring to wake up to, but it's just loud enough to get me to turn it off within 5 to 8 minutes. Yes, you can create your own alarms by either recording one or using Apple Music, but again, music doesn’t help me wake up, personally. 

I appreciate the addition of the missions feature! It’s a great way to ensure you get up and don’t fall back asleep. That part of the app is a 5-star rating! Overall, this application is really useful and helps me wake up on time. I highly recommend getting this app!

Edit: this app is HORRIBLE for your battery!! My phone was 50%, when I woke up, it was 12%! I went to my settings and it said that 86% of my background activity was from this app!! It drains your battery extremely fast!

Edit 2: I have just redownloaded this app near January. Now the usage of the battery is maximum of 5-12% thank you for fixing this!! Get this app!!

title: Works really well, too well
body:
Time and time again, Apple’s built-in alarm betrayed me with its phantom rings alarms that swore they went off while I peacefully slept through my 8 a.m. lectures. Desperate and academically endangered, I turned to Alarmy. At first, it seemed harmless: different alarm sounds, challenges, options meant to “help” you wake up. What I didn’t realize is that this app is not an alarm, it is a biblical event. This is not a pocket fire alarm. This is the closest thing to the Rapture I have ever personally experienced. Because as I sat
in a dead-silent classroom of about 60 people when suddenly my pocket unleashed what can only be described as 12 trumpets of judgment. Every head snapped in my direction. Panic set in. But past-me, knowing present-me is a certified sloth, had set precautions—rules that said the alarm WILL NOT turn off unless I complete the challenge. So there I am, aggressively digging through my pockets, shaking my phone for what seemed to be the longest 10 seconds of my life, while the alarm—by my own design—refused to stop. I am a product of my own necessity. I was already awake, but my God, I wish I wasn’t. If you use this app, understand this: you will get the results you want. But it is by God’s mercy, your body will eventually learn to wake up before the sound permanently gives you war-like flashbacks. You’ll start questioning whether the real alarm was the sound itself… or the primal fear it unlocked within you. Expect a 5-second cardiac arrest to start your day. Set wisely. Otherwise, you will inevitably hope that it was Devine intervention deciding it’s your time.

Overall: great alarm.
8/10.

This glitch seems to pop up about twice a year, and it’s always right after a new update. I will suddenly find myself late to work after the app’s snooze button decides to stop working. title: Great for waking up, not so much for mid day alarms.
body:
Got this app for waking myself up in the morning, and it works great. Loud alarm, annoying options, and math to wake your brain up. 
But, I was also looking for an alarm that would play through my head phones mid day, just quick alarms when I need a reminder. Google said this app would work rather than the built in alarm and I was like “cool I already got it”. I tested the sound and it seemed to play through my head phones then…. Embarrassment. Mid day in the lobby full of people, the alarm went off full volume in front of everyone. And to make matters worse, unlike my built it alarm, IT STARTED PLAYING MY YOUTUBE VIDEO AT THE SAME TIME FULL BLAST!! People were staring, I tried to swipe up on the alarm and at least pause the video, but each time the alarm blared less than a second later, reblasting the video. Only way was to try and switch to alarmy and shut it off, which took longer than normally would because I was flustered, startled, and focused on something else before hand. THANK GODS I wasn’t in the library.💀💀

When you close the app on your phone OR leave it open to this screen the alarms literally just WILL NOT GO OFF. And I’m the type of person who sets multiple alarms in one morning, so I have had MANY experiences of the screen not switching back for whatever reason (i was sleepy and missed the button to close it, forgot entirely, etc.) and sleeping in. I don’t know if these issues resolve themselves if you buy premium, but if even THAT’s the case, it’s still b.s. that the free version is as buggy as it is. It works great when it actually WORKS, but generally, if you’re looking for something reliable, don’t go for this.

title: The Bulletproof Alarm
body:
I don’t usually write reviews- but for Alarmy I really had to. 

I live with chronic depression and pretty severe ADHD. I’ve always had issues getting to sleep and consequently have always had issues waking up. It was getting to the point where I felt like I was going to lose my job. 
I had tried alarm clocks for people who are hard of hearing, setting my alarm clock across the room, multiple alarm clocks, different tones, etc. Nothing worked because it’s like I was able to sleep through turning each of them off. 
Alarmy’s math questions have been my saving grace. I HAVE to wake up enough to think to get the alarm to stop yelling at me lol.  
I couldn’t recommend this app enough. I can change the alarm tones any time I want with ease, I can change if it’s a gentle wake up or not, and I can change how many times it’ll allow me snooze, and whether or not I want the alarm to CONTINUE until I complete the challenge or whether it pauses WHILE I am completing the challenge which has allowed me to FINALLY fine tune an alarm that is sleep-proof for me. 
I wake up every time. I couldn’t be more grateful that this app is available in a free version for people like me. 
Whoever made Alarmy originally and whoever the dev team is that maintains it- sincerely, thank you from the bottom of my heart.

title: Serious Privacy and Data Concerns
body:
This app used over 20GB of mobile data in a very short period of time, which is completely abnormal for the way I use it. There is no feature that should require that much data, so this is extremely concerning.

I’m not sure what is causing such an excessive data usage, but no other app on my phone has ever consumed that much without a clear explanation.

The developers really need to investigate this behavior, because it raises serious questions about the app’s internal functioning and its respect for user privacy and security.

Until this is clarified, I cannot recommend this app.

title: Meaningfully Improved My Sleep and Life
body:
I originally used this on Android, and while the Apple version is a bit less intuitive due to all of Apples restrictions on what Apps can do, this is still one of the most important apps on my phone. I used to spend the last two hours of my sleep snoozing my alarms and getting bad, interrupted sleep. It turns out not having an option to snooze does one of two things. I either wake up on time, and get up, or I wake up enough to make a conscious, well considered decision about how much more sleep I need, then I set my alarm for an hour or two later.

In my memory, I’ve never been compelled to leave a review about an app before but this is one of the few that has meaningfully improved my life.

title: BEST THING EVER
body: When my normal alarm clock stopped working (I have an iPhone 15 this happened months ago) I needed a new solution. I first noticed it when I would wake up for school and kept waking up late thinking I was crazy for not hearing my alarm. I would set an alarm and watch it barely make a sound when going off. I’ve tried everything to make it louder and back to normal, but from what I’ve found along with many others with this problem, there’s no solution. I came across this app thinking it wouldn’t be good, it’s the best alarm app ever. Way better than my old one, I wish I would’ve switched sooner. It’s supper loud, perfect for heavy sleepers, different sounds and vibrations that I actually like, easy to set quick timers, easy to have routine alarms set or pill reminders, and even has a background and games for when you wake up. They have brain games to help get your brain functioning, having different ones to suit whatever you like. And the wallpapers are so cute and definitely a must now, I love waking up to a cat or a cute quote. There’s even a sleep tracker that shows how many hours you sleep and gives reports as well as snoring and noise while you sleep. I haven’t explored much of those though. This is a must have, whatever alarm or clock app you have you need to replace. I wish more people knew about this app.

title: I DIDNT GET FIRED
body: I normally dont do reviews cause i feel like they are pointless, especially for apps. But hopefully this can help someone like the app has helped me. Since highschool (im currently 25) I ALWAYS sleep through my alarms, especially through college. I would set 20 alarms, highest setting and still somehow sleep through them, or worse wake up half sleep to turn it off then go back to bed. As of recently, I got a job that I actually like and the biggest problem was my attendance because i was always late, and its hard explaining it to people because i come off lazy and unreliable. But really I would beat myself up about it every time I would be so upset with myself, and it felt like there was nothing I could do. Until one day I got a final warning at work and I knew I needed to try something new because I couldnt risk my livlihood, i was scrolling on reddit for solutions and someone recommended Alarmy. I swear to you, every day since i downloaded the app I am now EARLY every day and literally saved my job. I ended up getting the year subscription and is the best purchase I have made (aside from my car lol) in my adult years. Thank you, i dont know who created this app but you are the reason I still have a job to provide for my son as a single mom.Thank you for understanding me without knowing me.

title: Not The App It Used To Be
body: Alarmy used to be a great app for years but in the last couple months it has completely gone down hill. It’s clear whoever runs it now is only interested in profit and it has completely ruined the simplicity and usefulness of the app because of it. The main reason I started using Alarmy was because I had a habit of shutting off my alarms and going back to sleep without really realizing it. I started to use the barcode feature which would keep alarming every minute until you physically get up to scan your code and turn it off. However, over the course of many updates (read: added features you need to pay for), the barcode alarm is easily dismissed or bypassed without scanning anything. I’m sure many other features are affected too, but this is what I used it for most. I will be looking for an alternative app immediately.

title: Was great until it ignored alarm changes
body: So I’ve been using Alarmy for almost a year. It worked great up until this morning. I have a hunch it’s what happened before to me in the past but this morning I was able to confirm it. So usually my alarm is set for 830. I had to wake up earlier than that this morning so last night i changed the alarm to 730. Went to sleep and my Alarmy decided it didn’t want to respect the changes I made to my alarm and still went off at 830. Thinking I was just going crazy I went on the app to make sure it was set at 730. It was, pressed on my sleep report and the app said the first alarm went off at 826, an entire hour later than I needed to wake up. I thought this whole time I was just sleeping through my alarms but that’s not the case, Alarmy just isn’t working properly. This app would have 5 stars from me but it can’t even function properly at the most basic level of an alarm app: going off when you set it to go off. I hope this issue is worked out because it’s a nice app despite this flaw but it’s seriously making me consider another app. I can’t trust an alarm app that picks and chooses when it wants to go off.

title: Possessed Alarm That WILL Get You Up
body: For those of us who are perennially exhausted or fear oversleeping, this app is the clanging, possessed alarm that will wake you up, especially when you enable one of its CHALLENGE features. Pick your poison and difficulty level to shut off the ringing: 3 physical challenges, 3 selfies, 3 math problems (I do level 3 though I have a minor in Advanced Mathematics). It doesn’t sound so bad except…these are decently timed. Better get your brain going if you want to shut off the phone with something other than a hammer. Good news though. You can hit the snooze button up to 3 times…for the cost of watching one ad for each snooze. Still though, I find I like this thing better than the screeching bedside alarm. It’s reliant and while the app must have been forged in hellfire, it’s better at waking me up in a way that gets my mind clicking without being angry…unless I forget about setting a later alarm and cannot get it to turn off during a work meeting. 5 out of 5 for an alarm that does what it should,

title: Pricey but…
body: No one should be charging half the price of a streaming service for just an alarm. That’s ridiculous. But…a message to its competitors, they’re doing something right, because I don’t have the fear that it’s going to ring and then suddenly stop, not ring at all, or be easily circumvented to my persistent half asleep actions. I stopped using Alarmy because it was excessive to pay what they’re asking, and the Ads were somehow very annoying despite how little you’d interact with an alarm app. Yet after trying another wanna-be alarm app that was very convincing and similar….i woke up an hour after the appointment I was suppose to go to with no indication of any alarm going off. I could sleep through a train, but if you’re fearless enough to set some more drastic settings and ringers they offer than that’s like getting hit by one.  I’ve used it for years now and I’d say it gets a 9/10 for reliability. Missing 1 point for 1 or 2 occasions I can’t  account for where it didn’t go off, but that could’ve been user error. Note: don’t set your alarms when you’re already falling asleep. If it doesn’t wake you, it’s probably your own fault. 1/10 for price. I mean cmon. That’s ridiculous, but like I said, it’s not that they have a lot of real competition on what they have locked in.

title: Great at waking me up. When it actually goes off.
body:
The alarms are very loud, good for making me who is a heavy sleeper actually wake up at a reasonable hour. Wish there were alarms for every other weekday but whatever

However the app sometimes just- doesn’t work??? Sometimes even if I have the app open and my volume up, the alarm won’t go off. It’s a very small chance but I can’t really risk that.

Another issue with it is that the alarm DEVOURS your battery so you’re forced to leave your phone charging all night, and sometimes if you hit snooze a lot, it’ll cause my phone to get extremely hot and slow to the point of struggling to turn it off

I’ve also had suspicions that the ads on this app are scams? Sometimes when my phone is flipped screen up I’ll wake up to scam websites on my browser that I obviously didn’t open, but I have no proof it’s Alarmy so I’d take this with a huge grain of salt

But yeah, good when it works, garbage when it doesn’t

title: Ads stop alarms
body: So I normally am VERY happy with the quality of this app. I’ve been using it for multiple years, and have been very satisfied with the service. However, I recently started experiencing a bug that has led me to miss my alarm multiple times due to the ad blocking the alarm. Typically, I set the alarm at a specific time, and it rings to wake me up. Recently, I’ve set up the alarm, woke up on my own after the alarm time, unlocked my phone, and was greeted by an ad in the alarm app. Once I clicked the app away, the alarm immediately began to work but without any sound. I am not sure if this is an IPhone or the app issue, but it has led me to miss multiple important events. I am really disappointed as this was one of the most reliable alarm apps I used, and I can no longer trust its quality, thus, I have to find a new app to switch to.

title: Great app but bad business practices
body:
I have used Alarmy for over a year and I really like it. The barcode scan feature is a lifesaver. Before using this app, I almost lost my job because the default alarm failed me. 

Today I received a pop-up offering 78% off for one year of the pro plan for a total of $35. It seemed like a great deal, but the pop-up did not explain what features the pro plan includes. When I tried to close it to check, it said I would lose the discount if I left the screen. That felt manipulative because they are trying to rush into buying without telling me what I’m even getting. title: Works, but with a few glitches.
body:
Getting up in the morning is very difficult for me. And I started a new job that has me up quite early many mornings now. These alarms are the best way to get me up and out of bed without disturbing my husbands sleep. I highly recommend the photograph one since I just take a photo of something particular in my bathroom, the first place I need to go to start getting ready in the morning. I also appreciate the variety of ring, volume, and snooze options available. 
The only issue has been I’ve had a couple glitches come up that only get found when the alarm is going off. Last week the alarm just didn’t go off at all. I was nearly late for work. Yesterday an earlier alarm went off when it wasn’t scheduled for that day of the week. And this morning my alarm which has been the same settings since I made it, suddenly had the spoken weather report option turned on. I woke up to a loud robotic voice telling me today’s weather instead of the gentle music I set the alarm to use. 

All of these incidents have been very disorienting first thing in the morning which is something that sets me up with a bad mood for the day. 

I will keep using the app. But I am frustrated by the glitches.

I have really bad sleep issues. All the experts say to wake at the same time to help reset it, but I sleep through all alarms. I usually wake up just enough to shut it off, then fall back asleep. Despite my resolve the night before my sleepy morning self is stubborn as a mule and I am constantly oversleeping with what should be “just 10 more minutes.” 

Alarmy has helped me wake up enough in those groggy moments to force myself out of bed. I adapt to almost any alarm in a few days, and that’s no different for these. I’ve slept through them before even at max settings, but if I do wake then the challenges tend to keep me awake. If I find myself solving them too quickly I can modify them, so I always have some new roadblock to turning off the noise that usually I am awake enough to start my day. This app is literally the only thing that has worked for more than a week. Amazing work, well worth it.

title: Great app, and the team listens to feedback!
body: I have been using this app for several years, and it has been great. I have problems with regular alarms, as I often dismiss them in my sleep. Even when people call me to wake me up or wake me up in person, my sleep walking and talking often prevents me from actually waking up. The persistence of the alarms from this app, combined with the memory game which I assign to turn off each alarm, is one of the only things that can wake me up when I don’t want to be woken up 😅. Also, the team seems to truly care about the app experience for their users. In a recent update, the memory game mission was changed in a way that made it much harder for me to compete with my vision issues. I contacted the team about this, and within a week I received a response that said they would fix the issue for the next released update. Good to see a development team so focused on improving user experience. 10/10 would recommend the app.

title: Great wake up! EDITED
body:
EDIT 9/24/25: alarms are all working perfectly and have been for a long time now! Last thing I do before going to bed is open the Alarmy app. TBH I don’t even switch my ringer on anymore. As long as the app is open, it works. Must’ve been updated. The phone can be locked, but the app must be open. I do have a 2nd alarm as backup for hard days or if the 1st one does glitch, but I normally have to skip it since I’m already awake! I am still using the memory game every day. I have it at a harder level now. This app has been waking me up for work every day! My sleeping self hates it, but I’ve never been so on time in my life. Thank you!! 

EDIT 10/2024: recently, my Alarmy alarms have not been working as they should. They do not go off at all some days! Or if I fall asleep looking at the memory puzzle, it turns off the alarm instead of ringing or snoozing. I turned my ringer on and keep the app in the background as the help pages say. But this doesn’t help. It just means my notifications go off all night instead. I don’t understand why the app worked for months and then decided not to work. Is this  bad update? 

ORIGINAL: I struggle to wake up. I always have. With Alarmy, I have not slept through my alarms a single time in months!!! I still set a few alarms with a few different challenges, because I’m a tough case. But it works! I wish more features were free as they would make switching up alarms easier. But I’ll probably pay if my body starts getting used to these. I love how customizable the challenges are and how persistent the alarm is! Great app for those of us who can’t fall asleep and can’t wake up.

title: Just ok, novelty wears off
body:
I’ve been using this as my primary alarm for the past few years. Alarmy excels in giving a variety of unique wake up options you won’t find in your default alarm clock app. 

Alarmy’s weaknesses- they partner with really weird/sketchy advertisers. I often have accidentally clicked an ad link on the app in my semi-catatonic state of waking up & it’s the kind that takes you to a “security breach scan” spoof- I.e., some sort of scam/social engineering front trying to get you to think your phone is infected. Seriously? I’ll be ok, but what about the person who might actually get duped/scammed because of a nefarious “ad” you allowed in the app?

Secondly, Alarmy’s efficacy and star wanes with time. We are human- we adjust/adapt. So nowadays, I snooze multiple times and right away nowadays because I know I will have to solve a math problem if I choose to wake up and I’m not yet willing/ready to. So yes, my body and mind became and  jaded to this app.

The ads are the worst, but they also keep changing the interface of the different ‘games’ you play to wake up in the morning. It’s infuriating. The app is already made to make it annoying to wake up, now I’m groggy, it’s pitch black, and the interface has changed the 3rd time in the last few months and in my half awake state I have to figure out how to even START to turn off my alarm. It’s just infuriating. Oh, and the ads have gotten REALLY bad.

title: Amazing!
body: I had such a hard time waking up successfully each morning at six and Alarmy made all the difference. They have good ring sounds and can use your own too. Plus a vibration and a beautiful or cute wallpaper for all of your alarms. But my favorite part is that Alarmy has many different "missions" for you to do when your alarm goes off to fully wake you up. From waking up your mind by doing a crazy math problem to squatting ten times, they have it all. I also love that they provide how many hours until that time you set for an alarm so you know how long your sleeping. Anyways, I've been using this app for eight months now and I LOVE it so much!

title: Doesn’t work half the time after update
body:
Loved it, I’ve used it for years now actually. Updated the app and now it doesn’t work half the time. Lets me dismiss alarms without doing the missions, doesn’t even ask, despite the fact that I have them set. This only happens half the time though, so sometimes it does the missions and other times it randomly doesn’t. 

Obviously this is unreliable and defeats the point of why I use the app. Nearly didn’t wake up today for an important meeting because the alarm was dismissed without popping up with the missions, so I won’t be using it anymore.

And it’s not that I did the missions half-asleep, I have alarms set for during the day when I’m awake, and those too will randomly not require missions to dismiss the alarm. I even checked after that I enabled them on those alarms
 and I did. 

Good app when it worked, but I’ll have to switch to something else now because obviously when I’m relying on these alarms, I'm looking for reliability. It’s unfortunate because I have used it nearly everyday for years.

title: I’ve Used This App For Years!
body:
I’ve used this app for roughly 5 years now. It worked great for me, and then I noticed something looking at my battery usage in my iPhone settings. 

This app was using nearly 50%,  FIFTY PERCENT!, of all of my battery on my iPhone. I started closing it out and my battery life greatly improved. That is how much data this app is collecting constantly. If this app is open in the background of my phone my battery life is extremely shorter. 

I started to realize I can close the app out in the background and my alarms would still go off, even though it warns you that your alarms might not go off. I used this method and everything seemed better. My battery life vastly improved. Then I noticed that my alarms now weren’t going off all the time now either.

Moral of the story:
This app absolutely DRAINS your battery life with how much data it is sending to China without your knowledge (not hyperbole, check your battery usage in your phone setting) if you prevent that, your alarms become unreliable. 

Would have only given it 1 star but I did use it for years.

title: Media playback volume big
body:
New bug:

It’s very hearing-unsafe. My elderly parent’s hearing is bad, so I’m very cognizant of how exposures like this add up over a lifetime. I’m constantly using noise canceling on my AirPods Pro and Max, and earplugs when not using them. Please fix this! To help with troubleshooting, if I I snooze via pushing the notification (but not popping into it) it doesn’t steal media focus, so it doesn’t occur. 

Old bug: 
I got the camera permissions pop up, accepted, and get the box with instructions and the graphic showing where to scan. But it can’t see the image from my camera. Camera works fine otherwise.  It required rebooting to work. This wasn’t in the FAQ.

title: Love it
body:
Entrepreneur here with ADHD and major sleep problems. I was on meds for both at one point. It took me 100mg of the sleep meds to fall asleep on time. But, I’d either sleep wayyy too late, or be insanely groggy in the morning. Falling asleep at my desk for the first two hours of the day. 

Apple alarms 90% of the time don’t wake me up. I don’t always sleep much, so I need something intense. 

Alarmy gets me up (for the most part) every day. You have challenges of your choosing to solve/complete. You can pay for the subscription (I do) and make it extra loud, and overall a major inconvenience (in a good way 😂) that forces you to work a little. Gets the brain fired up some and allows you to make the decision - Get to work or go back to bed. That part is on you. 

I love it, my girlfriend hates it. Not a morning person 😂😂

Highly recommend!

title: These ads are getting ridiculous
body:

Now that they’ve implemented the full screen pop up as soon as the mission is completed, I have to find a different app. It’s so frustrating - and almost dystopian - for the first thing I see in a day to be an ad for Amazon. Not to mention, the click off is small, and it’s really easy to accidentally click on the ad and be redirected when you’re tired and not really looking.

Developers/ad team, this should be a priority for you. I’ve seen many other users say the same thing. This is a really dumb way to lose people when you can embed ads elsewhere more intuitively (sleep report?), or focus on attracting more users than farming us for every possible cent of ad revenue.

This payment goes to Alarmy which is not good considering the high cost of subscription already. It would be more bearable if you could choose from several charities for the penalty money to go to. 

Less bad: The battery drain when you have an alarm set is severe. I find it simple to get around this by not having a daily alarm set and instead use the one time option and turn the alarm on before bed (instead of it being set on all day).

Good: The photo mission where you take a picture of an object to set up and must then match up the camera to that picture in order to turn off the alarm. Missions in general. Gentle wakeup where the alarm increases gradually in volume.

Review of paid version June 22nd 2025

title: Love but needs countdown timer
body:
I love Alarmy, but really wish it had a countdown timer feature. As someone with ADHD, I often need timers that start “X minutes from now” for things like laundry, eating, or getting started on tasks. Other apps offer this, but Alarmy’s features (missions, nag mode, snooze lock) would make it way more effective.

It’d be great to have saved timer presets, labels, and one-tap start from the home screen or widget. Hope you’ll consider adding it!

⸻

title: A lot to like…. And a lot of ads…
body:
There’s a lot I really do like about this app. But the ads have gotten so insanely obnoxious, they’re everywhere, they seem designed to be easily accidentally clicked, and feel so intrusive.

Normally, for an app like this, I would have absolutely no issue paying for the premium version to get rid of ads and unlock the extra features. EXCEPT THIS IS AN ALARM CLOCK APP THAT WANTS $7.99 PER MONTH - PER MONTH. AN ALARM CLOCK APP THAT WANTS A MONTHLY SUBSCRIPTION OF $7.99

That. Is. Insane. I am desperately looking for an alternative that has similar features and a non-INSANE pricing scheme. I have no idea how they even justify this. $7.99/year? Sure, I guess - if they are actively developing and updating it to ensure functionality, add features, etc. But $7.99/month is so absolutely insane. It’s an alarm clock app.

Not only that but I’m noticing Apple has this flagged for tracking. I guess that makes sense if they’re running targeted ads. But all in all this just leaves a bad taste in my mouth. Again - it’s an alarm clock app. You don’t need my personal info or $7.99 a month to keep an app’s development funded.

title: A once great app that has consistently gone downhill
body: I have held a premium subscription to Alarmy for several years now, this app has been life changing in the past and I used to be a very big fan of it. That said over the past few months this app has become extremely unreliable. The amount of times I have waken up late recently only to find my phone not making a sound and that Alarmy has refused to go off is beyond ridiculous. Yes do not disturb us off, yes my ringer is on, yes the app is open in the background, and yes I do not have screen time restrictions on it. I have checked my settings multiple times and they are all correct, sometimes the app does work and it’s great when it does. But not all the time does it work anymore. An app like this has no excuse to simply not work especially when I pay a not so cheap subscription for it. This used to be an amazing app but they have forgot their core values of being the best most consistent alarm app on the market and have rolled out features that seem to be driven by profit rather than to stick to the core values of an alarm, which is making a noise when I tell it to.

title: Super unreliable app, used to be great
body:
I loved Alarmy and used to use it religiously a couple of years ago, including as a premium member. But in recent months, the app is extremely unreliable. Even just this morning (hence why I'm writing), it went off at 6:51AM despite being set to 6:00AM and ONLY went off once I touched my phone. I was already awake because this has been a consistent occurrence. I thought I was setting the wrong times, but no; the alarm just doesn't work anymore. Their solutions (ie. keep alarmy in background AND turn off silent mode and focus mode) don't actually solve the problem and aren't sustainable/practical. Shame. 

The app itself is a great concept and I still love the idea of needing to complete a mission to shut off your alarm, but if you're looking for an alarm that keeps you accountable AND rings when it's supposed to, Alarmy is no longer the best option. It's unfortunate because, even at the free level, this app used to be incredibly. Hope they can return to that.

title: Only thing that can get me up
body: As a chronic oversleeper and someone who has an endless list of alarms in my clock app just for waking up, I have tried numerous strategies. Getting enough sleep helps, sunlight too. I’ve tried setting different alarm tones so I don’t get used to it. Alas it still happens. I still sleep through class and often I don’t even feel like the one pressing stop. Like that’s unconscious me who has no regard for the consequences. Anyway this is all to say that this app forces the decision back into my hands. It’s not a cure all, but it wakes you up and stimulates your brain enough that it’s actually you. If I sleep in it’s because I choose to get back into bed after getting out and sobering up from sleep. You can make it as difficult as you want to incentivize you not to go back to sleep. Just make sure you don’t accidentally leave an alarm on after since they’re hard to turn off if it goes off in class, which is typically a pro but can be a con with user error. You can always resort to deleting it. My tips: if you resort to deleting it rather than waking up, disable deleting in parental controls on your phone to make that just as difficult. I like to use voice alarms because my mind doesn’t register that as an alarm noise. Also the picture mode can be a little finicky so I’d stick with QR codes personally unless you can guarantee lightning conditions and such.

title: Almost Too Good
body:
This is arguably the best subscription I pay for. Having ADHD makes waking up and staying awake the hardest part of my day. Alarmy’s activities force you to get up and do so with urgency. The most effective one for me is the QR code scanner. As I write this, I’m having to drive back home from my work office so I can scan the code I chose and turn my alarm off! I’m a little annoyed to be sure, but that’s the point of an alarm clock, annoying you enough that you get out of bed. 

I recommend Alarmy to anyone interested in an alarm app, and especially to any of those people who are neurodivergent like me.

title: College student: this app set me on a good path
body: I love sleeping in. I believed I needed around 10 hours of sleep to even operate. Then I downloaded this app, set an alarm with the math challenges, and started plugging my phone in across the room rather than next to my bed. Now, by the time I’m able to shut off my alarm, I’m basically fully awake and my cognition has been tested to start the day. I’ve become significantly faster at mental math. I’m a neuroscience grad student and this app has amplified my cognitive efficiency in a way no method we’ve studied ever has. I’m a bit of a niche case in that most stimulants have major adverse effects on me, so coffee and most medication to boost awareness and focus usually doesn’t do the trick. But this free app does. I’ve recommended this method to my friends in med school who are fighting similar battles and I hope they have similar results. Brilliant app that I’d like to run a study on one day.

title: I wish it had a few more features but overall good.
body: I pay for premium because personally a single challenge will not wake me up and I like some of the premium exclusive challenges like the photo matching. I like Alarmy and it works well, especially the wake-up check feature. I also like the morning reports, where it shows you how long it took you to wake up each morning, time from first alarm ring to last challenge completion, etc. You get a morning score based on those things. I do really wish it had an edit feature for these logs though because I often leave on a “just in case” alarm that’s set for significantly later than the rest of them, sometimes hours, and when it goes off, my wake up score will go from ex. 97 to 44 because the app thinks I’ve taken multiple hours to wake up. It’s pretty annoying because I’d like to be able to compare days where I use certain challenges, certain alarm sounds, etc to see if it affects how long it takes me to wake up but it becomes impossible to do so. A Face ID lock would be good too, because sometimes half-asleep partners will turn your alarm off for you…

title: Most affective alarm ever
body: I have a habit of turning off alarms in my sleep. I downloaded this app because I saw you could set the alarm to make you get up and scan a QR/Barcode with your phone for it to turn off. Thus, I did this and set it so that I have to scan my deodorant bottle that is across the room. I kid you not, this alarm awakens the actual fear of god within me and gets my butt out of bed every day. The alarm starts off quiet and then gets loud gradually (but quickly). This gives me about 5-10 seconds before I lose my mind from the alarm. Also, even if I click the button like I’m going to scan the barcode without actually doing it the alarm will turn back on until I actually do it.  I hate when my alarm goes off now but boy oh boy do I wake up. It was a little difficult to set up just because there are so many possible customizations and there aren’t many alarm sounds to choose from but it does what it needs to do for me. 10/10 would recommend but not if you aren’t prepared to be mad at yourself for the abrupt awakening.

Edit: I was urged to reach out to support about this, and received a very helpful reply from June. It detailed how the Alarmy team has been battling some challenges that newer iOS versions present with regards to battery life. Learning that it isn't a degradation of product, but instead a caveat of the platform, makes me feel that this app does deserve the 5 stars I wanted to give it.

title: Great Cross-Platform App with Excellent Support & Features
body:
Alarmy is a fantastic app with innovative features that make waking up much easier. I especially appreciate the ability to route alarms through Bluetooth headphones, which helps avoid disturbing others.

One of the standout aspects of Alarmy is its excellent support for both iOS and Android. As someone who uses the app across multiple devices on both platforms, I appreciate its seamless experience and reliability.

I also highly recommend the premium features, which add even more value. Features like customized alarm missions, step-based wake-ups, and advanced alarm settings make waking up much more effective. If you’re looking for a smarter way to start your day, the premium version is definitely worth considering.

Additionally, I recently reached out to support regarding an issue, and I was impressed by their responsiveness and willingness to assist. Their customer service team, particularly June, was very helpful in addressing my concerns, which speaks volumes about their dedication to users.

Overall, Alarmy remains a well-designed and effective alarm app. I’d love to see a Lock Screen widget added for even greater convenience. Thanks to the team for their support!

title: Alarmy is the best Alarm app!
body: I’ve been using Alarmy for about two weeks and I already love it! It’s super easy to set your alarms, it has nice alarm sounds, and you have missions like having to type something or get up and take a picture of something to make sure you’re awake! Also it has other features too! Yes, some of them you do have to pay for, but the free ones are equally as cool! My favorite is that you can customize the background of the alarm when it rings and pops up on your phone, and that you can “track” your sleep. You can see how long you’ve been sleeping, if you snored ,(and if you did you can hear a clip of it), and if you moved around in your sleep. Also, I forgot to mention, for the alarm it *does* make sure you’re awake if you add a mission. You get three snoozes, but after that it won’t stop ringing till you do the mission or find a kinda complicated way to turn it off in case it’s glitching or you have to take a picture of something you don’t have anymore for the mission, in which case you’re already pretty much awake. Also, it progressively gets louder the longer it takes you to wake up, and you can even record your own alarm sound or put one of your favorite songs as it! That’s pretty much all I have to say about Alarmy, but I love it and one hundred percent recommend it!
