This app has almost lost me my job several times. Even if I weren’t paying for premium, having an alarm app that doesn’t go off unless the phone is unlocked is the most absurdly disgusting feature a manufacturer could build into such a thing, because it absolutely negates its own necessity. If someone were awake to have their phone active, would they need an alarm??? To potentially cause serious problems for someone unless they pay for premium is criminal in and of itself. But to charge someone $70 for an app that STILL won’t works unless the app is OPEN all night long is so blatantly idiotic that it’s almost laughable. Thanks for essentially stealing my money.

title: Alarmy gave me my independence back!
body: I never usually submit a review or testimonial, but this is the exception because I wanted to share how Alarmy had positively changed my life. My entire life I have struggled waking up on my own, I am an extremely heavy sleeper and sleep through just about any alarm previously, and in my sleep somehow have turned off alarms when I didn’t sleep through it. I always needed someone else to be responsible for making sure I got up out of bed and it meant that I was not fully independent. I was always afraid of being able to hold a job because I was afraid I would sleep through my alarms or someone wouldn’t successfully wake me up. I have tried many other types of alarms to find a solution and came up short, until Alarmy. At first the idea of paying a subscription for an Alarm app seemed silly, especially because I had little hope that it would work for me since nothing else had. However with the free trial I decided I would give it a try, since I had seen great reviews as well. And I’m so glad I did, because it immediately worked for me, the settings I thought would work best for me actually did, and it forced me to wake up fully out of my sleep to turn it off instead of doing so in my mostly-asleep fashion that I did before. I set it so it got louder and louder to where I could not just ignore it. Because it does not shut off, and it turns into the loudest alarm I could possibly have on my phone. It immediately started rewiring my brain so where most days it starts and I am up in seconds unlocking it, so it never even gets that loud, and I am already up and doing things instead of fighting the urge to lay my head back down. I now have no fear of not waking up on time or holding a job, my family does not have to deal with the burden of being responsible for me being awake, and I have full independence for the first time in my life. I have absolutely no issue paying a few dollars a month to keep that independence, and it has done wonders for my quality of life. Because of this I felt the need to share my success story. Thank you to the developers of this app! Thanks Alarmy! -Lauren Simmons

title: Awesome!!
body:
The app just told me I’ve been using it for 100 days now and if I wanted to write a review so I thought why not.

It’s usually soooo hard for me to get up. I would set 15-20+ alarms on my phone plus set my Alexa to go off to wake me up. But I would usually either turn off the ones on my phone while I was still 1/2 asleep or I would just keep pressing snooze every time until it was an hour later.

I DL this app and have been using it while also still using my phone alarms, It’s awesome! There’s all kinds of different settings and you can really customize it however you think will really work for you. 
I really like how you can pick an alarm sound they offer or one from your Apple Music library, so I have a couple from my library I picked and have it set on random so every time the alarm goes off it’s one of the songs I chose. There’s a few “tasks” you can choose from, things you have to complete to make the alarm stop. I haven’t tried all of them, but the ones I currently am using and like is one where you have to physically shake your phone a certain number of times and then one where it shows colored boxes in a grid and you have to remember where they were and click on an empty grid where the boxes were (like a memory test thing). I think my favorite feature though is the “wake up check”. You can set it for however many minutes after your alarm goes off and you complete the tasks, and then to complete the wake up check you have to type out this short paragraph exactly how it’s written. If you don’t complete that, then however many minutes you set the wake up check for, your alarm will go off again and you have to complete the tasks all over again too. Really helpful for someone like me who will wake up to an alarm but would totally go back asleep again.

Since I’ve started using it I’ll set my phone alarm to ring once or twice, then set this alarm to ring then set just a couple more of my phone alarms just incase. But I usually turn those off because I’m awake by the time this alarm goes off and I have to do the tasks + wake up check. 

This alarm has been so helpful to me and I’m very happy I found it! I would definitely recommend it to anyone who struggles with waking up to a normal alarm or has issues with setting alarms then turning them off and sleeping more  (like I did). 
Also my bad for my super long review lol.

When I finally did wake up my phone was incredibly glitchy/laggy to the point I couldn't even get the whole minigame in the app to go. And when I left the app it kept spamming my phone with notifications making it worse. I eventually had to just delete it because it was so bad, I couldn't do anything about it.

Even afterwards my phone acted incredibly glitchy, taking forever to open an app or a huge delay when typing. It luckily subsided when I restarted my phone but I can't risk something like that happening again and doing actual damage to my phone. I'm just going to buy one of those bed shaker alarms instead.
If you are the type of person who is able to sleep through even these alarms beware because it could cause your phone damage from overheating!

title: Quite literally changed my life!
body:
This app quite literally changed my life! I love mornings, and never had an issue actually hearing the alarm, but I, in my sleep state, would always, and will always, snooze. For eternity. There is no getting me up. It’s actually kind of scary. It’s not enjoyable to drift in and out of half sleep until you’re more groggy than if you would have just gotten up.

I set the snooze max to 3 times, at five minutes per snooze. On the last one, I must get up, no questions asked, to scan a bar code in my kitchen. From there I can then stay up by feeding my cats, doing my skincare and writing in my gratitude journal, etc. it’s wonderful. And gets easier.

My alarm usually goes off between 5AM and 7AM, besides the one night per week that I bartend late. I’m not a night person so that has been sad for me but Alarmy has kept me on track for the rest of the week, which I try to go to sleep by 9PM.

THANK YOU ALARMY for helping me feel like myself and have it together♥️

title: Make Alarmy Great Again
body:
So I use to have this all back in college when I owned an android because I have a serious problem with waking up and missed multiple exams from it.

When I found this app it quite literally saved me and and was a huge help towards graduating.

Didn’t use it for a while because I’m self employed and don’t have to wake up at any particular time, but recently I started sleeping till 4pm oversleeping the Apple alarm or maybe turning it off unconsciously so I decided to give Alarmy another try.

First off the IOS version is not near as effective. I normally do 7 math problems on hard mode and that worked like a charm, until I realized you can just delete the app rather than solving multiple hard math problems, and now I wake up late every afternoon realizing I deleted the app subconsciously while in deep sleep. I imagine this is probably not the developers fault but more of a restriction that Apple puts on apps. But the android version was not deletable and you also couldn’t even turn off your phone as I learned when it went off during a lecture and I had the barcode set to can of chicken noodle soup at my house so I had to run out of class 😂 if it’s possible you should implement this on the iPhone version because it stopped working for me once I realized the cheat around it.

But the reason for my two star review comes from your absolutely stupid subscription plan. You expect me to pay $60 a year for premium features? I could buy 5 alarm clocks from Amazon every year for that same price. That’s absolutely absurd. I would have no problem paying a ONE TIME fee of $20 for this but subscription culture is the biggest scam in the world rn and you guys are clearly exploiting it. Netflix for a year is the same price I mean cmon that’s absurd.

Change the premium to a one time payment of $20ish range, and update it so that I can’t just delete the app in my sleep to turn off the alarm and I’ll gladly pay the one time fee and continue using Alarmy. Otherwise I think my $60 would be better off buying 5 physical alarm clocks every year until I have so many that i have to walke around the whole house to turn them off 

I’m sure this comment will never be seen by you guys but if it is seriously think about the fact that you are charging $60 annually for a subscription. That’s legitimately a scam. Either make it a one time payment or like $1 a year or a one time payment. Quite literally Netflix is the same price.

And also make it so you can’t just delete the app to turn it off because any really troubled waker uppers like me will just delete the app while they are asleep

title: Zoe’s Un-Alarmy-ing Rant: Hard Pass on the Paywall
body:
Oh boy, where do I even start with Alarmy, the app that used to be my reliable, not-annoying wake-up call? Yeah, emphasis on used to be. Once upon a time, it was a neat little freemium deal. You’d set your alarm, shake your phone a little, and boom, you’re awake. Easy peasy, right? But noooo, some corporate genius decided that freemium wasn’t enough. Now, it’s a 7-day trialware! Seven days to test my patience before slapping me with a paywall higher than Gavin’s sense of heroism.

First of all, who wakes up in seven days? Zombies from The Ring, maybe. But us mere mortals? I’m still trying to hit the snooze button with my face half the time. Seven days is barely enough to figure out if the app is actually worth using. And don’t even get me started on the premium features, like, “Oh, look at us, we can force you to take a picture of your sink to turn off the alarm.” Wow, revolutionary. Because that’s what I want to do first thing in the morning—stare into my dirty dishes before I’ve had my coffee.

You know what else is a great wake-up call? Losing your pancakes because the delivery guy forgot where you live. Happens every time. So thanks, Alarmy, but I’ll stick to the free version while it lasts and just pray the pancakes get here before you charge me for the privilege of turning off my alarm.

TL;DR: Alarmy? More like “Alarm-y Gonna Make Me Pay?” Hard pass.

Like my snark? You’ll love Zoe in Snack Powered Mage, available now on webnovel dot com.

title: Too many notifications
body:
I downloaded this to help me wake up for an early morning flight, so I used it Monday into Tuesday morning. Worked great! I was excited to experiment more and see all the features. Tuesday night to Wednesday morning, I did not use it as I wanted to sleep in after such an early start to my day. Just now, Wednesday morning at 10am, I notice that I have acquired 40 MISSED NOTIFICATIONS FROM THE APP. I’ve had the app literally less than 48 hours and I have 40 notifications. No thanks. It seemed to have good features, but I just cannot believe the overwhelming number, hence taking it down to 3 stars.

To anyone reading, it does have a free and paid version. The recordings it takes while you sleep talk or snore or whatever are a paid feature however. The basic free is the alarm, a few customization options for alarms and challenges for waking up, different alarm sounds, a decent array for a free app imo, and you can see your sleep reports like how long you spent in different sleep stages.

title: Saved me from getting fired
body:
I’ve had the same job for over a year and about a month ago I had a meeting with my manager about a last chance agreement. Basically, I signed a contract that stated that if I was late one more time my job would end, this was a long time coming and I had received multiple last chances before this. However, this was the last chance I would get and the stars had to align for me to get even this. Since receiving the last chance agreement I spent 15 hours the next weekend building a custom made alarm clock unsuccessfully due to damaged sensor components. I resorted to trying this app which came highly rated from the internet (reddit) and I have yet to be fired! The only improvement I can currently think of would be having the option to have the alarm be a random bar code, that way you would actually have to think about where you need to go in order to dismiss the alarm. 

Thanks Alarmy!

EDIT: I got fired because this app didn’t wake me up. I also went to be to late but still. I have moved on to Pavlok combined with paying an absurd amount now for this app. The one thing I notice is that this app drains my phones battery a ton during the day. It makes my 14 pro max die faster than my 13 even though I keep the 14 pro max in my pocket and use the 13 for most things. Looking at the battery usage, this app takes up most of the usage when there is only a little active screen time. It’s crazy. I tried disabling all its background stuff and it still does it. title: Missing features
body:
The only app that I hate but don’t want to remove haha. Its so annoying (in the setup I have, it doesn’t have to be unless you want it to be) which is why it works. I only have 2 issues keeping me from a 5 star review. 

First of all, I used to use one of my own tunes (that is not released on apple music yet) as my alarm sound, but currently there is no way to use an existing audio file from your phone’s files as an alarm. You have to record directly through the app’s built in “record” section, making it impossible for me to use my old alarm sound unless I record the final mix in the app, SIGNIFICANTLY decreasing the quality. Very unfortunate.

Second, being able to set up multiple missions in one alarm is great, but they all use the same timer. Believe it or not, it actually takes me LONGER to get out of bed, walk across the room, and scan a barcode (AMAZING feature by the way) than it takes me to solve some simple algebra. For now, I set up a buffer, using the shake mission on easy as a prequel to the QR code so that I can periodically shake my phone while getting out of bed and walking over to the barcode so I don’t run out of time, but I frequently forget to do so and end up having to restart from the beginning, which is very annoying.

All things considered, this app is very well put together and I would love to continue using it, but its really limiting right now. Thanks for all the hard work you have put into this app, it really shows. It just needs a LITTLE bit more love, and I’m sure it would be great.

Thanks, Ike.

title: Apple ruined everything
body:
I was recommended this app by my therapist, and it worked like a charm; I set it up so I needed to scan the barcode on the back of my drum practice notebook so I would actually practice the instrument more consistently. And it did help me with that!

Today I transitioned from an iPhone SE 2 to an iPhone 15/16/whatever the newest thing was.

The camera can’t read the barcode anymore. It’s blurry when I move the barcode close enough to fill the scanner rectangle, and only appears sharp and legible when the barcode is too far away to be read either. 

I knew the “Look at our three cameras!!” thing was a terrible idea from the start. I can’t zoom in or out of the scanner or refocus it, so the alarm has been going off for two goddamn hours.

It’s not your fault. I’m warning you, because you should probably try and bugfix this before Apple’s bootlickers and Always-Buy-Newest-Instantly folks come in, blame it on you, and smash your reputation into the ground.

TL;DR
The app’s great if your phone is functional. Apple’s phones are not functional.

title: DO NOT, use the sleep analyzer!
body: The alarm clock is GREAT! The sleep analyzer is of no use to ANYBODY! So, the alarm clock is GREAT at getting me up in the morning! I LOVE IT! That is where this wonderful app shines! As for the sleep analyzer, I've used it for two nights. The first night it said my sleep quality was 48, which is understandable, because I didn't go to bed until 2:30 in the morning, and woke up at 9:05 in the morning. I used the sleep analyzer again last night, and on the sleep quality score it says "UPCOMING!" It's been that way for over two hours since I woke up! So it did not record DOODLEY SQUAT as far as sleep quality! I won't be using that thing anymore! It's clearly not doing what It should do! And I recorded a good amount of sleep, but it didn't give me the data I wanted! So they need to improve the sleep analyzer, and then againagain, I don't know why it's even there, because you're not going to get accurate data unless You're hooked up to monitoring equipment like an ECG monitor, a Pulse Oximeter, EMG Electrodes, EEG Electrodes, Respiratory monitoring electrodes, and of course the snore monitor, and I suggest an End Tidal CO2 monitor! IN ESSENCE, IF YOU NEED SLEEP ANALYZI, GET A POLYSOMNOGRAM, AKA A SLEEP STUDY! I've had several of them, and It's not bad at all! Don't try to rely on an iPhone Based sleep analyzer! Those are a joke! Well, at least this one in "ALARMY," is! But, the ALARMS ARE WONDERFUL! I set it to the Loud alarms, and ure enough, it gets me out of bed in the morning! So, I'm not saying don't use the app. I'm just telling you that you shouldn't use the sleep analyzer, but you ABSOLUTELY SHOULD USE THE ALARM FUNCTION!

When they ask you for feedback they will setup google chat's but it is not on your schedule and you are just expected to just show up to the google chat. author: RVJStudio

title: This is genius!
body:
I never write app reviews, but this one deserves accolades. 

My 17 year old son cannot for the life of him wake up to alarms. We have tried a variety of alarm clocks, Alexa alarms, sunrise alarms. He just turns them off and goes back to sleep, and often doesn’t even remember doing it. However, since this is a skill critical to both college and life, not to mention a smooth and kind morning at my house, I am desperate to help him figure it out. 

Alas when I saw this app discussed on the Today Show, I decided to give it a try. It is amazing! There are so many different options on the missions you set, the alarm sound, and how many snoozes you want to allow. 

My son has realized he needs both a mental wake up (he’s chosen the puzzle) and a physical wakeup (he’s chosen a certain number of steps). He’s also determined he can’t have any snoozes, because he just falls more deeply back asleep. After a couple of weeks of experimenting with the app, some resulting in successful waking up and others not, I decided to pay for the full version. To me if this works in the long term, it is completely worth the price! This has allowed him to add in multiple missions and now he seems to be waking up. This is amazing and has changed the dynamic of mornings at my house! Instead of him waking to me yelling at him for the fifth time to wake up, he gets to do everything quietly on his terms. I will continue to monitor him this school year, and I will update if it changes my review. But I expect any failures will be due to him not recognizing the best settings for himself. He can always add more to extend the time he engages in order to fully wake up. 

The only negative with the app is that it MUST be open in order to ring audibly while the phone is in silent or sleep mode. He just sets it at night then keeps the app open. But I’ve had him set a separate emergency alarm just in case (even though he will probably just turn that one off!). 

I suspect whoever developed this app either couldn’t wake up themselves, or lived with someone who couldn’t, because the features are ingenius at predicting all the ways people will circumvent alarms! Definitely try this if standard alarms aren’t doing the trick for you. 

Also, I have never let my kids have their phones in their rooms at night, so this has been the “reward” for waking up. Good practice before college! Alternatively, if it’s for a younger kid you could move the phone into their room either very late or very early when they’re still sleeping.

title: Doesn’t work half the time
body:
I have been using this app since 2018 and in the last 2-3 years I regularly am having problems with it simply not making any sound when it goes off. I will wake up on my own 30 minutes to an hour after I needed to get up, and the Alarmy app notification is going off, and about 50% of the time my phone is vibrating, but absolutely zero sound is happening. 

My phone’s volume and ringer are turned all the way up, Alarmy is the last app I open before I go to sleep (and I leave it open when I lock my phone), I have it as an allowed app in all of my focus modes (though, this morning it was not set to go off in a focus mode at all, and still went off silently), the app is up to date, alarms have sounds and missions attached to them. 

I am fully at a loss for what to do other than use another app, which isn’t ideal because when Alarmy works, it works, and is the best, but it’s just been not going off 2-3 days a week lately (at 2 this week so far). I feel like this all started when I had to uninstall the app from my phone because it went off on a run 2 miles from my house and I had no other way to get it to stop, - when I re-downloaded it and logged back in, the entire app was different, including a lot of the settings, so idk if I was originally somehow grandfathered in to a better app and then lost that when I uninstalled (or I just hadn’t been updating regularly, and doing so messed it up) but it’s very frustrating.

title: Saved my mornings (and less intrusive to family)!
body:
I have been struggling to wake up to things for years and years. I’ve tried moving the alarm clock away from my bed, multiple alarms, obnoxious sounds, and nothing’s ever kept me awake and alert enough to actually start my morning consistently, but since downloading this app, I’ve gotten so much better!

I initially turned down the idea of these mission alarm apps because I thought I would have to walk around the house with an alarm blaring for all the family to hear, but that’s not how this works. The alarm is completely silent as long as you’re interacting with the missions you’ve set for yourself, making it LESS intrusive than traditional alarms. Doing mental activities that they offer forces my brain to wake up enough to ask why I want to get up, and you can set physical activities that require you actually get out of bed before the alarm can be dismissed fully.

The developers have safeguarded against almost every possible way to dismiss it without completing the preset missions.

Of course, I’ve come to learn that just because I can make myself wake up doesn’t mean I don’t need the sleep I was getting by sleeping in before, but this app frees me to make those choices and plan and not be at the mercy of my unpredictable sleep schedule. I subscribed to the paid plan within the first week, although a lot is offered for free. I would definitely recommend this to anyone who can’t get control over their mornings!

title: If your Alarmy is only vibrating…
body:
If your Alarmy app is ONLY vibrating when it rings then you have it sitting in the background and not leaving it up on the screen and then locking the screen. 
You have to be able to open/unlock your phone and the app be open on the screen when you unlock for the alarm to ring. I have been using Alarmy for probably 6 years (off and on) and have only ever had it not ring (just vibrate) when I’ve had it open in the background but not on the screen when I locked it. 
This is only being written because I read a few people were having this issue. 
So open the app, set alarm , LEAVE IT open ON YOUR SCREEN & LOCK YOUR PHONE, plug in to charge. I can GUARANTEE YOU that it will sound every single time. UNLESS you’re setting the alarm to go off before your focus is turning off in the morning. Or you could add Alarmy to your allowed apps to get notifications from. (That’s what I do just in case.)

title: Download at your own risk
body: I downloaded this app a while ago because the regular Apple alarms are buggy and don’t work. At first it was good, solved my issue. However, once the app began being updated to include premium features, I started experiencing issues. I’ve had many mornings where my alarms did not work (despite having my phone ringer on, volume all the way up, and updated to the newest versions of the app). I would open the app after the alarms not working and the slider would be blue (so it looks like the alarm is still set) but the top of the screen would say there’s no upcoming alarms. I reported all these occurrences to customer support, all their answer is to update the newest version of the app (which my phone already automatically does). The last instance I reported this back in April, I’ve gotten no correspondence until today (except a couple emails saying give us more time). What I got today was a non-solution: I was told to report the issue again (plus the standard update the app). I waited over a month and I’m being told to report the issue again!?  I’m wondering if there’s even a human reading and responding to the issues or if there’s just standard copy and paste responses. I’ve had to purchase an actual alarm clock because of how unreliable this app has become.  Because of the failing alarms, I’ve been late for/completely missed classes, meetings, and other appointments. DON’T DOWNLOAD THIS APP UNLESS YOU WANT TO GAMBLE WITH YOUR ALARMS, BUY AN ACTUAL ALARM CLOCK.

title: Horrible Battery Drain
body:
I used to use this in college and have gone back to using it for work years later. It works well (though I do wish we could organize alarms into folders). However, I have deleted the app because of this single genuinely frustrating problem: it drains my phone from 100% to 20% in 4 hours. 

I charge my phone to 100% overnight. I wake up to my alarm(s) and then go to work. It is still near full charge when I get to work. I do not use my phone AT ALL for four hours until my lunch. My phone is at 20% at lunch and dead by the end of my shift. It’s also incredibly hot.

I looked at my battery usage and there is no other app using battery except for Alarmy at 90-100% usage. This only started happening recently but the app has become unusable since I have not figured out why it’s been happening or how to fix it. Alarms are not going off while I’m at work - they’ve all been deactivated when I wake up. At first, I thought it was me leaving my flashlight on accidentally or leaving a show or music playing in the background for my whole shift. But now I’m sure it’s Alarmy because this problem ceased when I deleted the app. 

I want to continue loving this app - iOS native alarm clock is absolute garbage. But I don’t want to have to deal with this issue and I don’t want to have to troubleshoot for said issue that shouldn’t be happening at all.

Devs, I know you work hard on this app and I’m just upset at the situation - not you guys. For all I know, it could just be a problem with my phone. It’s unfortunate :(

title: It is broken now
body:
1st review: I am doing perfect squats but it only counts like 1 out of every 10. I’ve just updated my iPhone and it’s still doing it. Please let me know once this has been fixed and I’ll fix my review because before it was great

2nd review: Extremely unreliable, they’d MUCH rather make profits than help and or fix their app. I agree with another reviewer that said the people working for/with Alarmy should be IQ tested.
I have been paying for this app for about 2 years now. No matter what version I am on it will glitch in many ways. Either the alarm with not work or it will not work properly. Sometimes it’ll literally just vibrate (no matter the settings), sometimes it’ll just stop doing anything after 1 snooze and the list goes on and on

I have never been able to access more than about 20 songs in my music library even though I have like 1,000? Also a song that will work today will stop working sometime in the future (could be tomorrow, could be a week from now, etc)

I’ve contacted customer service numerous times via email cause you cannot call (I really don’t like emails overall, waste of time - calling is much faster & overall more efficient) and notified them about such issues which sometimes would get resolved but ALWAYS it’d be temporarily (like, literally maybe for 1 or 2 alarms) it’s pretty wild that you pay for an app and if doesn’t work. I am not a penny pincher by any means, I work very hard and do well for myself - however I DO NOT like paying for services that I simply do not get so I’ve asked for them to give me extra months or SOME form of reimbursement and they never do. At the end of the day it is ALL about the “almighty” $ to Alarmy, which is gross.

You are better off using an alarm clock that CANNOT connect to the internet. I really don’t like how there’s this huge push to make everything attached to the internet and furthermore it seems more and more companies want you to pay for everything all of the time. I’ve seen where other users were rightfully upset they had their “lifetime” membership taken from them. This shouldn’t be a thing. You should honor your original users and let them be grandfathered in.

Very worth nothing that I have used this app on several iPhones including 2 iPhone 15 Pro Max’ and with every iPhone (wether latest update on iPhone and or the app) I get basically the same exact results.

It is unlikely that I will renew my membership and if I do it is probably more likely I will cancel it if it gets automatically. Also, please stop pushing the weather, the news and etc on me. I DO NOT CARE. There’s virtually infinitely other outlets I can get thst from.  That is not the purpose of this app. If anything give me the option to disable these “features”

Could be super excellent, but it’s not.

title: Great when iOS lets it work, breaks CarPlay
body: Two glaring issues with it. 1. The alarm will not sound audibly when my phone is in iOS 17’s standby mode. It shunted the alarm as vibrations to my watch. Net result: I overslept this morning. 2. While connected to a car via CarPlay, this app will change the audio source back to the iPhone. In my Honda CR-V with wireless CarPlay, this means that if I try to listen to SiriusXM, every 30 seconds to minute, the audio goes quiet for a few seconds while the source changes to the phone, then back to SXM. I have isolated it to this app: the problem will occur but then stop after force-quitting this app. So, I must quit the app before driving, and I must remember to launch it before bed each night, or the alarms won’t go off! Nonetheless, the features available in the alarms, like the missions and the checks to make sure I didn’t fall back asleep, are so useful that I will endure these glitches. I hope a fix can be found, at which point I will gladly update this review to the full five stars that it should be.

title: Great App, But Pricey Premium
body: This app is honestly fantastic. I love this app and although you don’t need the premium version to reap the benefits of the app, I would love to have some of the premium features. HOWEVER, I CANNOT see myself paying $59.99/year or $7.99/month. Repeatedly paying for an alarm clock is completely INSANE to me. Now if it were a One-Time fee, I’d happily pay, but it isn’t and that is just mind-boggling that they would continually charge for a premium alarm clock    -_- Overall, great app, well executed, easy to use and gets the job done but too pricey for premium.

title: this app made my day worse
body:
i don't usually write reviews but had such a bad experience i feel like I need to. if you're a person who likes keeping ur phone on silent mode or u have a phone with an old battery, THIS IS NOT THE APP FOR YOU. found that out the hard way today.

downloaded this app so i could have something to wake me up with custom sounds, without me needing to set anything up each night because i'm very forgetful. worked ok the first few nights, although the ads and calls to buy premium are a bit much.

then, this morning, no alarm went off. just my default gentle vibrate and a bunch of spam notifications. turns out (and to be fair, they say this on their faq) if ur on silent mode AND the app happens to reload in the background, NO alarm will play. so i just slept in lol can u keep the app from refreshing?? no!!!! it happens randomly due to ios. your only hope is to open the app EACH NIGHT before u sleep, according to the answers they're giving to reviews. bro. i have memory issues. i wanted your app to be something i DIDNT have to set every night.

alternately, u could turn off silent mode. but i need it during the day for school, so i'd have to remember to turn it off each night AND on again the next morning. that's not gonna happen bro.

so i'd decided to delete the app. then, tonight, i realized my battery these past few days has also been really bad? like, i do have an old phone, but it's been almost dead at the end of a day (and i'm not on it that much!!)

 i investigate in settings, and what do i see? this app is on in the background TWENTY FOUR SEVEN. like, ALL THE TIME. it keeps my phone from fully shutting off. NO other app on my phone does this. turn off the background refresh and the alarm DOESNT WORK. and it's leeching my battery as a result, which i don't have much of to begin with!!

the customer service for this app wants u to believe it's due to ios limitations that this stuff works how it does. idk, maybe. i'm not a tech expert. and i could see someone who's not me having an ok time here.

but this is just my advice: if you ARE like me, with a bad phone and adhd and a fondness for silent mode, find a different app. this one isn't worth it.

title: Great, but hate the subscription
body:
I used this app a lot around 2017ish when I could never wake up for school and loved it. I am an extremely heavy sleeper, and I have a bad habit of turning alarms off while still fully asleep. The alarms on this are loud and obnoxious, which is exactly what I need, and the tasks aren’t possible to do without waking up. When I first got this app, it was maybe $2 upfront with unlimited access to all the alarm settings. I stopped using it for a while, but I recently downloaded it again and was extremely disappointed to see the subscription pop up first thing. I’m glad the memory puzzle is still free as that is what I primarily used, but other options like the barcode, steps, or photos that require you to physically get up are no longer available without a subscription. I get that this app has much more features now, like sleep tracking, but those could be offered through subscription without including half the alarm types. This app is extremely helpful and it’s disappointing to see it stuck behind subscription, especially since the monthly price is three times more than the original one time price.

Edit- the developer reached out and helped and I’m grateful! I still stand by my first comment that an alarm app shouldn’t require a subscription, but their customer service was extremely helpful!

title: No Alarm Issue Resolved
body: To those who may be wondering why their alarm is not going off. In the top right corner of the screen in which the alarm is being activated there is a mute button to mute and unmute the alarm. If muted, it will stay muted for all future alarms until unmuted. The screen can ONLY be reached when the alarm is ACTUALLY GOING OFF, regardless of if you can hear it or not, the screen indicating the alarm is currently activated and going off, will appear in which you can actually unmute it. You may have to create an alarm that goes off in one minute from when you need to fix it so you can get to the screen and unmute it from there. Then you can delete the “one minute from now” alarm after you do that.

title: Sleep disorder
body: I have a severe sleep disorder and I’ve tried everything to get me up in the mornings. I’m not gonna say that this will be the fix for you but it definitely was for me. I had a sonic bomb alarm clock that would wake me up in the mornings with an extremely loud and obnoxious alarm but even putting it across my room I’d just sleepwalk and turn it off and lay back down. The problem was I wasn’t getting any brain activity so nothing was actually waking me up out of my sleep state. This app woke me up and forced me to do puzzles to shut off the alarm which got my brain going enough for me to be actually awake rather than in my usual sleep state that just shuts my alarm off and goes back to sleep without knowing it. I have never written a review before but I’ve only had this app for two weeks and it’s been an insane game changer so I just had to. I love the features of it, it has an initial alarm that you can set and you can choose the types of puzzles you want, how many, and their difficulty level that you need to complete before it shuts off the alarm. It has a time limit to each puzzle so if you fall back asleep and henceforth stop doing the puzzle the alarm goes off again. It has different alarms to choose from but personally I found it wasn’t even the loudness that makes me wake up I just really needed that brain activity. And additionally it has a silent notification that goes off ten minutes after you shut off the alarm and if you don't open the app with the notification within I believe two minutes the alarm goes off again. It is foolproof, it wakes you up, gets your brain going to keep you up, and goes off again if it for some reason didn’t work. title: THIS APP SAVED MY LIFE
body:
Here’s the short and long of it:

I have NEVER been able to wake up to an alarm in the morning, to the point it almost ruined my life. This app has allowed me to ACTUALLY wake up in the morning and GET OUT OF MY BED! It’s been a game changer.

Here’s the long version:

Since moving out, I’ve always had to have my parents call me and wake me up. Then, this summer I traveled to Europe for school. Because of the time difference, my parents couldn’t do that. I was able to get my roomies to help me - up until the last day, when we all had different flights traveling home. The ONE day no one woke me up, I missed my flight home. Needless to say, my parents were M.A.D. I spent a LONG time paying them back for the rescheduled flight. Then, I went back to classes back home, and I could STILL not wake up on my own. I can only imagine how frustrating that was for my parents 😭

Then, 2 months ago I tried this app. HOLY COW WHAT A DIFFERENCE. Requiring a photo match to get you up and out of the bed is GENIUS. My parents were so surprised when they called me and I was already awake. My depression got better because I didn’t have to feel guilty for inconveniencing others and constantly being late anymore. THANK YOU ALARMY!!!

title: Great alarm app! A+++
body:
Alarmy is a godsend if you’re a deep, heavy sleeper like me. It’s been saving me from the endless snoozes or sleeping through an alarm entirely. 

The app has tons of customizable options and features, personally I do a memory puzzle and then have the app make me walk downstairs to take a picture of my coffee maker in order to disable the alarm. I also have it set up to charge me $30 if I just delete the app instead of going through the process needed to disable the alarm. 

I’m glad that’s an option, because it takes away the temptation to bypass the alarm process to just stay in bed. Making yourself get up and think + walk around is the secret to properly fully waking up in the morning. Thanks, Alarmy! Now I’m no longer in danger of getting fired for being late all the time.
author: Duncan the donut man

title: It’s immediately obvious this is the answer
body:
I have used this for two days during the free trial. The mission that has you scan a barcode has gotten me out of bed these last two days at the time I actually wanted to be up. I have struggled through a bunch of other set ups but without a remote alarm clock (which I looked for and it doesn’t exist) if the thing making noise can be turned off in my bedroom I apparently cannot resist getting back into bed. It’s like my brain will make any excuse possible and when I’m sleepy it sounds reasonable so back into bed I go. I’ll update this after I’ve been using it but it’s going to be well worth the money if I can stop being late to work on work days and stop wasting my life away in bed on days off. Awesome feature: it lets you set any number of snoozes or none. I got out of bed on my day off and even did some housework instead of laying in bed most of the day.

If you are at wits end with yourself as I was because you just can’t get out of bed no matter what you try, this app will help you. title: Gets me out of bed!
body:
I don’t typically struggle with oversleeping but I have a hard time with laying in bed so long that my kids miss the bus or I’m late to work. Using Alarmy’s body movement mission forces me to get out of bed to shut the alarm off. I also love that one of the movement mission options doing squats, which means that selecting that mission not only gets me out of bed but it’s also a baby step towards getting into better shape. Other things I love are the sleep analysis, wake up analysis, and sleep sound/white noise options.

What I think could be done better is having more preset wake up music options (although this is slightly off set by the ability to record your own music or sync to Apple Music,) I don’t like having to leave the app running in the background in order for the alarm to sound, the steps body movement mission isn’t sensitive enough as I have to stomp and intentionally bounce while I walk for the app to count the steps, and lastly I wish there were other fitness choices in the movement missions so I could force myself to create a mini exercise routine that I have to complete before I can shut the alarm off. The app is also pretty pricey. While the app is a free download and includes a 7 day free trial, it’s $7 if you pay monthly or $59 a year. I’m able to afford that in my budget but many can’t and it’s a shame that those of us who most need apps like this to help get our lives together, likely due to to mental health struggles and/or neurodiversity, don’t have access to it because of financial barriers.

title: No more sleeping through alarms!
body:
Honestly a godsend. Alarmy has all sorts of features to wake you up and make sure you stay awake. You can set a series of ‘missions’ that you need to do to turn off your alarm that can require you to get up and move, do math problems, take a picture of a specific bar code, and more. You can also set the number of times you can hit snooze (including zero) and how long the alarm will snooze for. And critically, you can set the app to send you a push notification some amount of time after you complete your missions to ensure that you haven’t fallen asleep again. If you don’t respond within 2 minutes, your alarm will start back up from the beginning. 

If you’re sick of your wake-up plan being sabotaged by sleepy you, absolutely give this a try.

title: It’s not very good, but that’s not the dev’s fault.
body:
Perhaps my view is colored by the fact that I’ve used the far more reliable android app, but I don’t think this app is very good.

The android app is absolutely unstoppable, it won’t let you switch to another app, or close the app, or even turn off your phone. If you want to get that app to turn off without completing the mission, you have close it, open settings and uninstall it, while having it reopening itself constantly. Stopping the alarm without doing the missions is harder than the missions themself.

This app, on the other hand, is pitifully easy to circumvent, which for me defeats the entire purpose of it. In fact, it’s so easy to circumvent that I managed to do it completely accidentally, turning a 30 minute nap into a 2 hour nap and royally screwing up my day. Now, to be clear, I don’t think the devs are at fault for this. This just seems like a case of iOS being more difficult and restrictive to develop apps for.

I feel like working some shortcut automations in, at least as something optional, would make the app more reliable. Like have a way to create a shortcut that requires you to do a mission, and set it up linked to a default alarm.

$90/year for an alarm app?  Seriously?  

This app is a great example of the excesses of the subscription model.  Some developers deliver extraordinary software as a one-off purchase for this price. The notion of paying for this every month for eternity is a deal killer.  

Getting on the train of apps like this is an exercise in never building wealth and always being poor.  Stay away.

title: Suggestion for sentence typing feature :)
body:
I love this app. I used to set roughly 15 alarms every day, and I would still sleep through them. Alarmy changed my life. I recently went premium after using Alarmy for the past year or two, and it upgraded my experience to another level.
Before premium, I still had to set three alarms. Now, I just set one super charged alarm. I do two sentences, six easy math problems, and I scan two qr codes in my bathroom. 
This works amazingly for me, and it pushes me right into my morning routine. However, when I was setting up a new alarm just now, I went to enter new quotes/affirmations into the sentence typing feature and I realized that it could use some improvements.
Firstly, I would like the option to have folders underneath the custom tab. I would like the option to organize between my affirmations, my quotes, and my reminders/to-do lists.
Second, I would like the 'select all' button to be added inside each folder.
This would make setting my alarms the night before so very easy and I would get more intentional sentences tailored for the day. Just my thoughts! If you read this, thank you for your time and attention :)

title: Battery Life + 3rd Party Alarms
body:
- If you’ve noticed your battery draining at faster rates than normal, the Alarmy background process could be the reason. Turning off the app during the day is a decent workaround, but I’m guessing Alarmy has to work this way due to restrictions for 3rd party apps not being allowed to ring if it’s not running in the background.

- If Alarmy doesn’t ring randomly on certain days, it’s likely due to automatic software updates. These updates can cause the app to shutdown in the middle of the night, which in turn causes the ringer to not go off properly (at least for me, since I use Do Not Disturb and Silent mode frequently). Apple additionally does not allow you to prevent a single app from being updated automatically, which means that you’ll likely need to turn off automatic updates entirely which is annoying.

Overall, the functionality of the app is actually quite good - the puzzles have helped me wake up properly in the morning. However, due to limitations of the app (not even Alarmy’s fault, but rather due to iOS app restrictions), I’m switching to a manual digital alarm clock for reliability/battery life reasons.

title: Sadly, no longer reliable
body:

Unfortunately, something broke in the past few months, and it’s no longer reliable. Sometimes the alarm simply doesn’t go off. When I eventually wake up (late), I see the notification but there is no sound, until I unlock my phone and then it goes off. 

I’ve been using it for years, so I know all the rules to make sure it works. I’ve messaged support and they basically responded that they are looking into it. Unfortunately, for an alarm app, the only thing that matters is reliability. 

I’m so disappointed because this is one of my favorite, must have, apps. Until then, approach with caution.

title: Best Alarm App For Heavy Sleepers……Almost
body:
This is, handedly, the best third party alarm app for iOS; this is especially true for heavy sleepers that find themselves sleeping through alarms. It delivers what it claims and shows to near perfection, with one small issue in the idea and one large issue from what I suspect to be an iOS limitation.

But first, the good. Alarmy is very customizable when compared to the native clock app. You can change the look of the app with themes, backgrounds, color changes, and more. While I haven’t dug too much into this, for someone who has a specific aesthetic I imagine these features are appreciated.

The customization also applies to the alarm itself and its features. You can change the number of times you can snooze the alarm, how long the snooze interval is, how long the crescendo of volume is on the alarm (Side Note: some of the sounds are LOUD, much louder than the native alarm can get), if the alarm uses your phone speaker or a Bluetooth device, days of the week for your alarm, and missions with difficulty and round settings for each. 

This app delivers on its promise to assist users in waking up through “missions,” my favorite two being Memory and Math: Memory is a game of remembering where yellow tiles are on a grid - they are shown for a few seconds and then flipped over - of various size (5x5, 6x6, 7x7 - I.e. The difficulty setting - very easy, easy, medium, etc). Math is…well, math. You solve problems of selected difficulty from simple arithmetic to complex multiplication and division for a number of rounds. 

Now, the bad. The minor issue I have with the app is when I have multiple alarms set; sometimes I forget to turn off the later alarms only to be surprised when they go off and fumbling to grab my phone. For better and worse, this app is very strict in requiring the mission be completed to silence the alarm no matter what. This unfortunately has some drawbacks if someone has an alarm go off at a bad time, for example, while driving. This leaves the user with no choice but to delete the app as quickly as possible as the alarm crescendos to a blaring volume. I’m not sure if there’s a way to solve for this, as it will add exploitability in the alarm that heavy sleepers are known to take advantage of, but I feel it is important to mention for at least the angle of safety.

The second, more major issue is the fact that it sometimes will not go off at all. Don’t get me wrong, Alarmy is the only third-party app that is consistent enough that I trust it for my daily alarm clock. I’d estimate Alarmy rings ≈ 97% of the time, where the next best option is ≈ 70% of the time. I don’t know what causes the couple of times it doesn’t go off, I suspect it’s because it cannot ring if the iOS alarm is going off already (re-emphasis on heavy sleeper), but I don’t know for sure; I unfortunately cannot replicate the mornings it doesn’t ring.

Tl;dr - Best third-party alarm clock app I’ve used with few minor flaws. It’s the only one I’ve used reliable enough that I trust it in place of the iOS alarm. Additionally, the missions are great for heavy sleepers and very customizable. Highly recommended!

author: Hshajaja

title: Used for months now
body:
Look I’ll keep it simple. I’ve never had issues until this most recent update, for now I’m having to use a different app until something gets. I’ve done all the steps needed in ordered to make this work on my phone because all it’s doing is just sending notifications and not doing any type of sound. My ringer is on, DND is disabled. I understand that when you do an update for your phone some apps don’t work for some reason but that’s neither here nor there. 

Prior to this issue. I’ve loved this app. It genuinely wakes me, tracks my sleep, and my absolute favorite feature is that I’m able to play sound in the background ( and I can set the duration ) while I fall asleep. I love the heavy rain sound while falling asleep. 

I’m a heavy sleeper, so this app has been able to get me out of my sleep within the first alarm ( 9/10) which is better than the generic alarm on iPhone that I quite literally am never able to hear. 

If you read the other reviews about people complaining about the pricing, ignore them. You really don’t need to pay for anything to do what you need the app to do. Which is to wake up you. I have it set where I don’t have to do any missions, because like the other reviews say. It is annoying having to get through the games/missions in order to turn the alarm off. I was half awake barely able to look at my phone and that was the main reason I disabled the missions on my end. 

In all honesty, if the developers were to make it where while you’re doing the missions it’ll temporarily disable it for let’s say.. 30 seconds? Then in re consider the missions, because nothing frustrates me more than trying to do something while I’m being harassed by my alarm lol. 

Anyways. I would check the app out. If you love it, you love it, if you don’t then you don’t. Some of the negative I really don’t understand why y’all are even complaining. 

I’m keeping the 5 star review because more than likely the error for this app not working anymore is probably on my end. But if they’re any recommendations or possible solutions I’m all ears. For now I will be using another app until I can figure this out or else I’ll have to part ways.

title: Battery hog and won’t go off
body: I have to say, I love what this app does and how it works. I wake up much easier and faster which is exactly what it should do. However, the app is poorly built to a point that it is broken and unusable for me. Firstly: the app will not play sound during alarms if it’s not actively running in the background. You must have it previously opened on your phone or else it will only vibrate during the alarm process. This leads to the second problem, the app is a huge, massive battery hog when it’s open. Going in and looking at the battery measurements shows that Alarmy, which is only running in the background except for the 2-ish minutes it takes to turn my alarm off, is using comparable battery percentage as YouTube. That’s unacceptable. The idea behind the app is great, it desperately needs some behind the scenes tweaks.

title: an essential app but needs more flexibility
body:
I take a very sedative medication that makes it extremely hard to wake up in the morning and this app has completely changed the game for me. I use the QR code and it gets me up and in the kitchen where I can make coffee and start my day at a reasonable time which is something I have really struggled to do for years. 
That being said, there is a particular function on the QR code part of the app that’s been really frustrating. Every weekend or every other weekend I spend the night at my parents’ or boyfriend’s house which means I have to use a different QR for each place I stay at. That is usually ok because I will save a different QR code for each place I’m in. However, if I ever happen to forget to change the mission to the correct QR code, my alarm will go off in the morning for a QR code that I literally can’t scan because it’s in my apartment in another town. It doesn’t stop ringing if I turn off my photo or close the app or anything. The only way I can turn off the alarm is if I delete the app altogether which then deletes all my data on the app and then I have to re-enter all my previously saved QR codes and it’s really frustrating. I would suggest we either be able to choose a different QR code when the alarm is ringing if it’s set to the wrong one, or make it so that the app doesn’t completely erase all its data once the app is deleted.

title: Life changing app, 100x better than default alarm app
body:
To anyone looking for an amazing solution, look no further. Alarmy is hands down the best alarm clock I’ve ever used. At the time of this review there’s a free trial, it’s absolutely worth every penny after that. 

I never write reviews or rate apps, Alarmy is legitimately the best thing to ever happen to me regarding my sleep schedule. I have untreatable insomnia and the best I can do is sleep an hour before work and hope the iPhone alarm doesn’t shut off or activate silently. Alarmy gives me peace of mind and takes away the stress of not knowing if I’ll oversleep and be late for work. In the past two weeks since I’ve started using Alarmy I’ve woken up on time every single day for the first time in years, I was close to losing my job before I found Alarmy. 

Thank you guys so much, words cannot describe how grateful I am for Alarmy.

title: Battery HOG
body:
The following review comes after 2 years of using this app:

I used to love this app because doing a few math problems in the morning to shut my alarm off has proven an effective tool for making sure I don’t sleep past the time I’m supposed to get up to work. Lately however I’ve noticed an insane amount of battery drain for an app that only runs in the background and maybe gets 15 min a week of actual screen time. Spotify and Instagram comparatively get 7-10 hours on screen a week total and yet Alarmy takes up more battery than both of them. 

What is it doing in the background that makes it so inefficient?? 

After noticing an increase in my phone overheating, along with having to charge my phone periodically throughout the day, I’m making the tough choice to delete this app and will purchase a new alarm clock so I don’t have to have something running 168 hours a week in the background on my phone. If the battery drain wasn’t an issue this app would easily be 5 stars but because of it I can no longer recommend this app.

title: It was a great app
body:
I used Alarmy for years and I can’t understate just how valuable of an alarm it was for me. It was absolutely a game changer if you struggled to get out of bed in the morning. 

Now though, it’s a bloated mess. Currently about once a week it will randomly not make an audible sound which has caused me on more than one occasion to be late for meetings/appointments. I’ve done all the trouble shooting steps but I believe it’s caused by the too frequent updates being pushed and restarting the app in the middle of the night. 

Outside of this it has been bogged down by too many useless features. Before deleting the app, it was taking up to 40% of my battery life a day caused by background activity. Why does an alarm app take up that much background activity? Beats me, either it’s unoptimized or it is making unnecessary calls for data. 

Either way, I would recommend you stay clear of this app.

For instance, the app does not allow your alarm to go off if the app is closed the app also doesn’t allow your alarm to go off if you are using your phone for anything at all, I am unsure how this makes for a five star alarm app, if the app only works when you’re doing absolutely nothing with your device, but people who use their cell phones, use their cell phones for things prior to falling sleep that might make it where this app does not work for them I have only had a handful of times where the app successfully went off at the specified time it was supposed to. title: I swear by this app
body:
This is the most effective alarm app I have EVER used, and I’ve used an awful lot. The missions work and the dev team put a huge amount of effort into making sure the alarm WILL go off no matter what. Headphones: no problem. Minimize the app: no problem. Close the app entirely: SOME problem, but it still tries. The missions really do force me out of bed, and make it really hard to delay or dodge. The “skip alarm” feature is great since it allows me to make a REALLY UNPLEASANT last resort alarm that I’m able to skip if I wake up in time. 

I had to reach out to support once, and the issue was resolved the next day and never seen again. And in a couple months of using the app I’ve already seen other improvements and features added. Overall; a very solid alarm and clearly a good team behind it. I happily paid for a premium yearly subscription.

body:
App does not integrate well with iOS. You have to always have the app open in order for it to work properly, and even still you have to unlock your phone in order to snooze or turn of the alarm. 

When the app is on all the time it drains the battery for some reason. Looking in my phones battery settings I can see it takes up 65% of my battery power throughout the day, with “background processes.” For what though? I don’t know. 

When the app is not open, but one of the alarms is active, when it’s time for the alarm, the app sends a constant stream of push notifications, with no sound, which totally bombard the OS blocking all other notifications until you open the app and turn off the alarm. 

Very annoying. Very power consumptive. And not well integrated with iOS. I finally deleted the app today. No thanks.

Modifying notifications, of course, renders the app useless. 
     You get what you pay for, and the free version isn’t worth the “cost.” The monthly cost for the premium version is steep when you consider the cost of a real alarm clock at Walmart.

title: DO NOT USE! UNRELIABLE!
body:
An alarm clock app needs to go off EVERY TIME. If you set an alarm, it can’t have errors and not work one day otherwise it defeats the purpose of the app. 
I nearly missed my presentation this morning because the alarm didn’t go off. Let me clarify. The alarm screen showed that it was going off but there was no sound. 

Yes, I triple checked the settings and the volume was turned all the way up. 
No, it was not connected to any Bluetooth device that would channel the sound away from the phone speakers.
Yes, my phone speakers work perfect.
Yes, it has worked all other times that I have set the alarm and have not altered any of the settings past this time. It simply did not make any sound this time, which of course was the worst possible day it could have done this.

I’ve deleted the app and will strongly suggest anyone using this app, if you’re waking up for something important, DO NOT rely on this app. Use your normal phone alarm or another alarm app.

title: Unreliable
body:
Unfortunately, this alarm app has failed me and made me miss important work events too many times. I can no longer trust it to be my primary alarm and must rely on something else. It makes me sad, because when it works, it is the most effective alarm I have found. But recently, I have woken up naturally an hour or two after I scheduled an alarm to ring, missing the start of work. When I look at my phone to figure out why the alarm didn’t work, it’s on the snooze screen, but no task was required nor sound played. The whole app was frozen. When I force quit and reload the app, it plays the alarm and requires the task immediately, even though it is already 2 hours late and I’m already awake. This had happened twice for me, heavily impacting my life and job.

I have been an alarmy user for years, and this is not the first time it has just broken for me. It did the same a couple year ago, prompting 
me to cancel my premium subscription then. But, I got a new job and figured I’d give the app another shot for those early morning commitments. It worked well at first, but about a month later, I’ve missed the start of work twice now. When you run an alarm app, it needs to always actually sound the alarm. People rely on the alarms to wake up for important things in their lives. An alarm failing has real world consequences for your customers.

So I’m cancelling the premium subcription yet again and looking for a different primary alarm solution.

title: This app is saving my GPA
body:
About a month ago I had a change in my medication that was greatly beneficial for me, but I quickly went from a very light sleeper to a VERY heavy one. I would set an alarm with the default alarm app, only to wake up hours later with it still ringing- I just wouldn't hear it. I was missing classes, due dates, and appointments, no matter how many alarms I set. My grades were dropping and I was in constant fear of missing work and getting fired. I downloaded this app last week without much hope of it actually working. I expected that I would just have to change my meds back to the ones I had before, despite how much physically better I felt. 

 In this past week, I have woken up on time every single morning and from every nap! This alarm is LOUD, even without choosing a "loud" sound (I really like the picnic sound). I also have it set to make me do math problems, which really helps me "actually" wake up. I haven't missed a single class this week and it's taken an huge amount of stress and guilt off my shoulders, especially as the end of the college semester is getting close. I am so thankful for this app- I don't even need any of the premium features, but might buy the subscription anyway because the value it's given me is worth so much. If you're in doubt, try this app!! I'm so glad I did!!

title: Life saver
body: Hello, I neverrr write reviews but this app has seriously saved my life. I have always been know to be a chronic deep sleeper, and I’ve had trouble waking up my entire life. I’ve had multiple occurrences where friends and family became seriously concerned at the level of unconsciousness I experience when they try to wake me up. Since this problem has been so long-lasting I’ve gotten used to setting a million alarms because I’m so scared that I won’t wake up for school. I’m still using multiple alarms with this app out of habit and fear but week by week I’m trying to decrease the amount and I’ve still been able to get up! I’ve found that personally the only activity that pulls my brain out of my near coma lol is the math questions. I put them on medium difficulty so they aren’t too hard to where I go to my calculator or turn off my phone and I do 3 problems per alarm. I have the premium because I find the power ups super useful- increasing loudness the longer the alarm is going off, wake up checks- anywhere from 1-10 min after u shut off the alarm, and you can put labels on the alarms that it reads out loud at a high volume!! This is not only the first time I’ve been able to be pulled out of such a deep sleep so effectively but the first time in my life that I’m not constantly missing things or late at that. Personally I stick with one type of activity for my alarms due to comfortability but I would definitely recommend rotating them so that you’re mind doesn’t get used to them. I would rate this app a 1000/10 if I could!! Seriously something that has solved a huge problem in my life and I’m so grateful to have found this app:))))

title: Narcolepsy
body:
This app has changed my life. As somebody with narcolepsy type 2, I have never been able to wake up to alarms. I would press snooze over and over, possibly 50 times. And no, not an overstatement. I often, if I allow myself, will sleep for 28-40+ hours at a time, half waking up to pee or take a bite of the chips I have next to me on my bed at all times. I have never felt what it was truly like to feel awake. But this alarm, has allowed me to conquer me snoozing my alarms without remembering. When I had the multi alarms, it would allow me to actually get up and take my adderall, fall asleep for 10 minutes, then wake up from both the alarm and adderall mix. I never had to worry about missing my college classes again. 
Even though I’m unable to subscribe to the full version anymore due to college, I would like to add a suggestion! The snooze button is unlimited :(. And I can do the check to see if awake, but snooze is easier on my brain when trying to get the wake hormones to work. But, with unlimited snooze, I found myself pressing snooze throughout the entirety of the day, as I can sleep on adderall aswell. Narcolepsy is unforgiving ahah. Maybe there could be an option to only be allowed to snooze once or twice or unlimited 😅. It would help severely.
author: tay702702702

title: I can’t praise it enough…
body:
Quite honestly, this app has changed my life. I often stay up too late, I’ve never been a morning person, and I’m an EXTREMELY deep sleeper. One time, lightning struck my dog’s electric fence and caused a small explosion outside of my window, and I remained sound asleep.

Despite these seemingly insurmountable issues, Alarmy has never, EVER failed me. I used to use Apple’s built in alarms, and they would randomly fail to go off, causing me to sleep through all sorts of important obligations. This has never happened with Alarmy, provided I follow their instructions (which they make very clear) before I go to bed every night.

Alarmy alarms reliably go off at the scheduled time, every time. Not only are they reliable, they are effective. The sounds they have crafted for this application are so incredibly infuriating to hear that there’s no sleeping through them.

Another issue I faced with all other alarm clocks is the fact that I would shut them off while I was asleep. Alarmy saved me from myself yet again by providing the wake up missions, which would be incredibly difficult to do while asleep (although, as I have proved, not impossible). 

After I completed the missions in my sleep the first time, I immediately bought premium for the wake-up check feature and have never looked back. It’s worth every penny, especially since I would probably be fired from my job without it. There are some drawbacks to the wake-up check, but they are completely my fault, because most days I will forget that the wake-up check is coming, and while I’m in the shower, my alarm will start going off again which makes for an unpleasant experience. But again, totally my fault.

If this app can get a person like me to wake up on time, it can get literally ANYBODY to wake up on time. My only concern is that this app is so good that Apple will try to buy it out and ruin it like they do with every other app they incorporate into their OS. So, I beg of you Alarmy devs, don’t ever sell out to Apple, you are perfect!! Bravo, bravo, 5 stars.

title: Overall Helpful Alarm
body:
For the most part, I think this app is great. As someone who chronically hits snooze, It’s been the best at waking me up so far if I don’t allow it to give me the option to hit snooze. I find that the math and the memory games are the ones that I can consistently use without my brain finding a work around or getting irritated by it. 

A couple things though, the main motivator for writing this review is that I really hate that the wake up check in feature that goes off sometime after you’ve turned off the alarm, doesn’t make any sound. VERY OFTEN, I am up and moving going about my morning routine & will forget about that feature until my alarm starts going off again & I have to stop what I’m doing, which sometimes is impossible or just irritatingly inconvenient, and go through my entire alarm process AGAIN. It’s the most frustrating thing. It doesn’t make any sound, just vibrates once so if I’m busy doing something & don’t have my phone in my hand looking at it, I have no idea the reminder popped up. A little reminder alert ding is literally all that it would need. I get so mad every time I have to stop what I’m doing and go through my entire alarm process after I’m already awake.  

Another small thing is that I tend to find that I also wake up easier when an alarm tracks your sleep and goes off during the most optimal time in your sleep cycle so I wish that feature was built into this app as well & I didn’t have to use a separate alarm app for that. 

Other than the few odd times the alarms have glitched in some way and made me so angry I’ve had to delete it off my phone, it works pretty well.

title: Alarmy, my dearly beloved

Alarmy and I have been through so much together. During my freshman year of high school, I desired a new and more efficient way to wake up. Ever since that magical moment, Alarmy and I have been in an on-again-off-again relationship. We mostly engage on the week days, when I need to be somewhere in the morning, but I also often use her when I don’t want to sleep too much.
Alarmy has brought a good share of goodness into my life. She usually gets me up, but sometimes I’ll feel cheeky and remove her from my phone because I can’t be asked to solve my 10 easy math problems. Yet she also has encouraged me to learn more about healthy sleeping habits, and taught me what type of sleeper I am, how long I like to sleep, what gets me up the most affectively.
I love the Alarmy app so much. It is an essential part of my morning routine, I highly recommend this app to anyone who has trouble getting up and wants to wake up on time.

title: Love the app, but I have some suggestions
body:
This app is the perfect way to actually carry out your plans to wake up early! Serial snooze buttoner, hereby reformed. Three suggestions: 

1) It would be nice if the wake up check (which is an awesome feature) had a longer time limit before it times out, given that it’s a silent notification. A little annoying to have to stop my morning groove to repeat my alarm step if I miss the check. I end up staying in bed looking at dumb stuff on my phone just so I’ll see the wake up check notification. Maybe adding a vibrate function or an extremely quiet sound specifically for the wake up check would be helpful. 

 2) This is nitpicky but the motivational quotes in the typing challenge are almost unbearable. I’m not sure if it’s a copyright thing preventing the developers from using better options but the quotes feel pretty lackluster, sometimes to the point of questioning if the quote was put in the wrong category by mistake. Also a lot of them are negatively-focused, in the vein of “I know things are bad, but keep going, because eventually they will get better.” I personally prefer more positive, insightful quotes, especially early in the morning to start my day off right. 

 3) Finally, when I’m half asleep, I’m really good at tricking the steps challenge by shaking my phone in my hand while I’m in bed. If there were maybe an option to add a gps tracker or something to confirm you are actually leaving a 10 foot radius, it would probably help circumvent the motives of my sleepy self, who will stop at nothing to sabotage the plans I make when I’m fully alert.

title: Don’t have your phone on silent
body:
As a notoriously heavy sleeper who always needs to set 10 alarms to get to work, Alarmy has saved my mornings. You’ll be amazed how hard simple tasks are for your groggy brain, and Alarmy will force you to keep doing it until you get it right unless you want to keep hearing the ringing. I always set a memorization task and then a harder math task 30 minutes later to ensure I don’t fall back asleep. Not only does it help me actually wake up, I think it’s somewhat improved my math skill. However, I do have one problem with this system - if my phone is on silent, Alarmy will not ring. I can certainly understand that a third party app probably doesn’t have the ability to bypass silent mode, this is just a warning to potential users to set a reminder to take your phone off silent or set an extra normal alarm as insurance, as this has made me late to work a couple times. 

Overall - great app, easy to use, plenty of stuff that you have access to without paying, and you will actually wake up.

title: The alarm you think you don’t need.
body:
iOS…now the clock has failed me about 3 times. Those 3 times have been extremely detrimental for work, the alarm is actively going off, but it doesn’t make a sound. If you have your phone set on vibrate, sometimes the alarm doesn’t override it. If you have your alarm set on low, for some reason the sound is capped on a lower tier. These aren’t constant problems but they’re frequent. iOS also is just an alarm clock. Easy to turn off, snooze, what have you. It’s also not very loud as a default.

This app has never once failed me the many years of use. It is extremely loud, it’ll blast your phone on any setting you have it at. If you accidentally close the app, it’ll tell you you forgot. It’s almost impossible to snooze with an automatic back up alarm that will kick in 5 mins after your alarm. It’ll ask you first if you’re awake. The why you’ll wake up is the exercises they can make you do if you choose to. Anywhere from math problems, to physical activity, photos of locations. I am a fan of the shake activity. You simply shake your phone x amount of times (mine is at 30). It doesn’t sound too hard to just cheese and go back to sleep, but you can adjust the intensity required to count as a shake. I have mine set at medium high, and I really have to shake this phone like a crazy person. I assume at max intensity, you’ll create enough power to bring a rocket into space. It also has convenient weather, horoscopes, news, and other tiny bites of info that might be good to start your day with. It also tracks your sleep patterns if you want it to. All of this is optional.

Oh yeah, all of these exercises are timed. If you don’t complete it in time, it starts all over with the loud alarm. It’s amazing and is absolutely free. I don’t really know what the paid version offers, but it’s completely great as a free app.

title: Goodbye to an old friend
body:
I’ve been using this app for months and loved it! The way it has you do tasks to wake up is the only thing I’ve found that prevents me from hitting snooze!

Upon downloading this app, I did did find it odd that the app had to be “open” or “your alarm may not ring”. But I figured, no worries, I’ll let it do it’s thing. 

My phone is over a year old now, so it wasn’t surprising that my battery felt like
It was starting to go downhill. My usage hadn’t changed, so I figured there was no way that any of my apps, let alone my alarm app, could be connected to these issues. For this reason, I had never checked my battery usage data. 

That is, until today, when my phone died mid-day when I was at work and not even using it. I finally checked my battery health and It clocked in at a respectably healthy 90%. I then checked my battery usage data and was horrified by what I saw. 

My beloved alarm app, the literal only reason I get up in the morning, was responsible for 15% of ALL my battery usage over the last 10 days. By comparison, I watch a lot of YouTube. An average of 3 hours per day to be exact, and it used 19% over that same span. 

If I had written this review yesterday, I would have given 5 stars. It really does wake me up like nothing else. But I have to do something, and I have to be honest with myself. I’m not watching any less YouTube anytime soon. So it is with immense sadness that today is the day I say goodbye to Alarmy.

Roughly once a month the alarm will fail to sound, meaning that you’re never 100% sure when you go to sleep that the alarm is going to wake you up. For a long time, I’ve kept using it and trying to figure out if I’m doing something to cause this (especially since I don’t see many other comments about this). I even leave the app running in the background all the time like they ask you to (which is bizarre and annoying).  In my mind, the most basic function of an alarm clock is to sound the alarm at the time you tell it to, and if it can’t do that there is no reason to use it
