author: ESCape183

title: No More Being Late to Work
body:
First, I’ve never left a review on an app in my life. But this may well have changed my life today. The past few months I’ve become that girl that has no less than 10 alarms every morning, wakes up to half and quickly falls right back to sleep until I just run out of alarms and wake up 2 hours later than I should have and have to rush to work only to still be an hour late. Every single day. 
WELL, not anymore. 
Today I used this alarm for the first time. Just ONE alarm & I’m awake THREE hours before I’m supposed to go to work, and I mean actually awake. 
I used the step method - basically take a minimum of 15 steps to turn off the alarm. I mixed it with a memorization one to wake up my brain a little too.
I’m not kidding, I even tried to hit snooze at first but I guess I didn’t set that up right in the settings - which is good - so I had to get out of bed instead of snoozing all morning. 

If you’re thinking about getting this app, it’s worth a try. Just pick something that you know will make you stay awake. I knew I could solve math problems all morning half asleep and never actually get up. Being forced to get up to shut off the most annoying sounds ever? I doubt I’ll be late to work again for a long time.

title: Nothing worked… then I found Alarmy
body:
I bought a shocking wake-up alarm (Pavlok) for under $300 to wake me up, I mostly used the vibrate setting after awhile. But it was annoying to have to take it off my wrist all the time and I eventually lost it - you couldn’t wear it during the day either unless I wanted to short circuit your laptop - I didn’t feel comfortable using it. 

I got a sleep wake up light for under $300 and it worked pretty well, but it’s not portable and I began traveling a lot for work which made it impossible to use. 

By some miracle, while searching for a vibrating alarm app for a different purpose, I discovered Alarmy in an add. I fell in love with it the second I saw it - amazing! Works successfully more frequently (almost without fail) than my shock watch, completely portable, and cheaper…

Well yes and no, there doesn’t seem to be a one-time purchase fee, instead it’s monthly. If I had to pay $300 for lifetime access - I probably would, maybe I will try to contact the team and work something out…

title: Life Changer
body:
This alarm straight up changed my life. I used to have a really hard time waking up and staying up. I would have to set 7 different alarms because I would keep turning them off and falling back asleep.

Now that I downloaded this app, I only have 2 alarms! I set the first one with a mission that engages my brain, like a math question, to help me start to wake up slowly. Then 5 minutes later, my second alarm makes me get out of bed and take a picture of my doorknob to shut it off. Ever since I started using this app I haven’t slept through an alarm once!!

The app does have a couple of weird quirks. Since most apps can’t make noise if they’re not open, Alarmy always has to be open in the background of your phone in order to go off. This really bugs me so I just set a reminder on my phone to open the app before I go to bed.

Another weird thing is that every time you close the app, Alarmy will send you literally dozens of banner notifications warning you to open it back up. This is incredibly annoying, so I disabled notifications altogether. When I did, I got a warning that my alarms would stop going off if I disabled notifications. So far this hasn’t happened and my alarms have worked every time, so I’m not turning them back on.

Anyway, it’s a great app. Alarmy’s noises start out soft and quiet, and slowly get louder until you disable it. It has a bunch of missions you can set to disable alarms, which focus on stimulating your brain or getting your body moving. If you’re sleeping through your alarms or falling back asleep after they go off, this is the solution.

title: Alarm does what it says with some big payoffs
body:
Downloaded this app because I’ve been having to get up for work at 3:30am and I have a tendency to turn my alarm off, go back to sleep and then forget to reset it. I set this app to memory and squats before it will turn off and so far it’s done what it says. After the squats, I feel awake enough that I don’t have the desire to get back in bed. 

But be warned, this app wants to stay in the background and tells you that it needs in order for the alarm to ring. Not sure why and seems a little shady imo. Also, with it in the background, it drains the battery super fast. I usually end a 8 hour work day with minimal usage at around 60-70%. Yesterday and today I ended with about 30%. These two things make it hard to recommend as a real solution. If the app can run without draining the battery I’ll consider changing my review.

title: Costly over time
body: Let me first say that I love this app! It is feature rich, works great, and even alerts you if you close the app so that you won’t risk your alarm not going off just because you accidentally swiped close the app. The feature that works best for me is the “time pressure” feature. This feature is a premium feature—which means paying a monthly or yearly subscription fee. I’ve had the app for over a year now and have been paying a monthly subscription fee. However, I really just cannot justify spending that much on an app I will use for an indefinite period of time.  I think asking people to pay $50-$60+ a year, depending on the subscription plan, is a bit steep—especially for an app. Maybe not for some people, but it definitely is for me as a student. I’d even happily pay a one time $50 payment to have the app and be done with it; or even have to deal with ads. I just wish there was a more cost effective option for students, and others with fixed incomes, that would like to access the premium features. This is why I am only able to give the app 4 stars instead of 5.

title: CAUTION: It will overheat your phone and kill your battery
body: I LOVE Alarmy. It works so well.. but, they want you to keep it open all day in the background so you don’t forget to set it at night. And it requires access to do everything in the background so it will actually ring I. The morning. The problem is: while running in the background they have it running some sort of processes, who knows what.. but it KILLS your battery. Literally uses more battery than my screen.. since I got up this morning it has used 25% of my battery, which means it is tracking a lot of SOMETHING in the background.. and there is no way to stop it unless you remember to physically swipe up and force close the app every morning. My battery life has cut in half since this started. Also, it makes my phone REALLY hot constantly to where the phone dims the screen and the back of my phone is hot to the touch. After Force closing the app, this all stops. (EDIT: just looked through the tracking data, and while the app is open it literally tracks ALL of your usage data such as: search history, what apps you use, location data, etc. and sells it to advertisers.. that’s why it kills the phone battery.. also.. why am I being charged a monthly subscription when they are making money selling my personal info?)

And the app works great 80% of the time. But the other 20% of the time, the alarm goes off silently for no readily apparent reason. title: I loved it until this week…
body:
This new update is terrible, and I get the feeling it’ll get worse. Two stars for now, going to one if it gets any worse. I’ve been using Alarmy for several years. It’s almost impossible for me to wake up through phone speakers. They just aren’t loud enough to do it. Before even starting to use Alarmy,I had come up with a beautiful workaround. I bought a sound bar off Amazon. I connect to Bluetooth. Then the alarm plays at full volume through the soundbar. THAT’ll wake you up. This worked great, but to keep the soundbar on, I had to play music or a tv show throughout the night. No problem, I can fall asleep to that. But sometimes a season would end, or the provider would pop up and ask me if I was still watching, etc and it would turn off once sound stopped going through it for like 20 minutes. Enter Alarmy. The simple white noise fireplace allows me to set my alarms and activate the white noise before I’m anywhere close to going to sleep. It’s much quieter than whatever I’m watching before bed. It stays on throughout the night, unless the phone updates or something, but I have that turned off. There were some other perks. When I was living in an apartment, I wanted to use the lowest volume that was needed to wake me up. So I’d use the crescendo feature. Again…worked beautifully. Yada yada. All great, loved it. This new interface is seriously overcomplicated and totally useless. Not being able to leave the classics screen in the app? Come on. Bring back an Alarmy Classic and have it just be the old version from before all this cluttered garbage was added. I’d happily pay to have it back.

UPDATE: 9/22/22
They released an update that at least allows you to use the classic, built in sounds without it turning off when you leave the screen. I would still take an Alarmy Classic to get me back to the older, less cluttered up version, but at least this is a mild improvement to the user experience. Up to 4 stars now.

title: Not worth it in iOS 16
body:
I’ve used Alarmy for years and have been incredibly satisfied with it. However, as of iOS 16, the app has only crashed my phone and caused me trouble.

One morning, I received my alarm notification, as usual. However, when I ended the alarm in the app, the notifications kept coming. In fact, so many notifications were sent that my phone began to overheat, and eventually to begin a cycle of restarting.

In between one of these restarts, I was able to delete Alarmy, but the notifications didn’t stop coming! This phantom of Alarmy continued to crash my phone until I was able to turn off notifications (for an app that was no longer on my phone).

My phone is still hot and very slow after this escapade, and I am now hesitant to re-download Alarmy, despite the years of usage without issue. 

In summary (tl;dr): the app will damage your phone in iOS 16. Use with caution.

title: Not a fan of the new update
body:
This has been my favorite alarm for the longest. Literally would not be able to wake up on time without it. The scheduling system is amazing. The challenges have been so helpful, and having my rain music come directly from the app has been fantastic. I’ve always loved this app. 

Unfortunately, last night I experienced a major disappointment with the app. The rain noise section was updated to showcase YouTube videos instead, and the ability to set how long the rain noise would last for disappeared. To make things worse, for the YouTube videos to play, my screen would need to stay on the entire time. The new sleep mode timer is very confusing and wouldn’t let me adjust the time. 

Literally loved the fact that I could play rain noises from this app while the screen was off, which made me completely stop using YouTube rain in the past. The fact that y’all integrated it and now I have to keep my screen is pretty frustrating. At least bring back the ability to schedule when the rain should end so my phone doesn’t have to be on all night. I don’t want to keep my phone on the charger all night. 

I rarely write reviews, but this was a major pain point for me. Please fix it soon. I need my rain noises. And the specific sound choices you had before were perfect to me. I miss those. I’m sorry to be so picky about this, but it was a major part of my sleep routine. 

Thank you for hearing my concerns.

title: The Update is a MESS
body:
This app used to have a decent sized set of sleep sounds accessible by one tap. Now, that screen is a long, scrolling list of YOUTUBE videos within Alarmy. Not even original content from the developers, just recycled YouTube videos, thumbnails and all.

I’ve listened to the stock Alarmy thunderstorm sound every night for years now, it’s a concrete part of what makes me fall asleep each night. Before the update it was easily accessible with one tap. Now, you have to tap, scroll down, load, scroll down more, load, scroll, scroll, scroll, until you get to the bottom, tap again, and THERE you’ll find the sounds. It’s ridiculous. Every scroll just irritates me knowing that the developer of this app is taking advantage of others’ YouTube content for their own app, and cheaply implementing it. You can’t even turn your phone off with these sounds, so what’s the point? Might as well just use the YouTube app. 

I’m completely disgusted by this new update and I hope the developer reversed what they’ve done. This isn’t helpful WHATSOEVER and it’s borderline immoral. You charge for this app, don’t take people’s content and profit from it, all while making the app LESS usable.

title: Amazing
body:

One downside: you have to have Background App Refresh on in order for the app to work, so I suggest turning it on (if you have it off) and ticking off every app except Alarmy. Since enabling Background App Refresh it automatically gives permission for every app to use it, you must manually go into the setting every time you download a new app and tick the option off for that app. However, I think this is a fault of Apple themselves for not including an “Exceptions” option in their settings. I know the app needs Background App Refresh to work properly, so this isn’t in any way the developers’ fault.

There’s a few feature you have to pay for but the picture-turn-off feature is free and that’s all that matters. The only thing is you have to pay for the “wake up check it” that makes sure you didn’t go back to bed but if you have to take a picture of your sink you turn the alarm off; then all you have to do is fight the urge to lay back down after you up. title: Beginning to regret buying
body:
So firstly this app has a really good idea and a lot of really cool features, if they worked right. 

My first complaint is that it doesn’t show up as an alarm when the alarm goes off. Instead, it goes off. And then I have to dig through my phone, find the app, and then dismiss the alarm. Which is just so obnoxious and really dumb for an alarm to not act like an alarm would. But I chalked it up to just another step to help me wake up. 

But then the features stopped working like they should. I had to get up super early for an appointment and so I decided to use the photo option. Guess what decided not to work at 5:00 am. That’s right, the photo option. So my alarm is going off and I cannot get it to stop. It finally timed itself out and I thought “well that was a weird one time thing.” Nope! I had the are you awake check in set. It asks if I’m up, I’m washing my face and didn’t hear, see, or feel anything to indicate that it did the awake check. So my alarm starts going off again requesting I take a picture. But I still can’t use the photo function. 

And finally this morning. Rather than the photo function, I had the phrase function on. Because at least I should be able to do that without it malfunctioning. Wrong. Rather than using the 2 phrases I typed up as reminders for the day, it gave me 3 inspirational quotes to type out. I even double checked after I finished typing it all out, and it was DEFINITELY set to 2 phrases of my choosing as the settings. 

So, moral of the story. If you enjoy waking up in a hot rage because your alarm clock is hanky panky lemon janky. Then this alarm is for you. I personally am mad that I spent $60 on an app that makes me murderous first thing in the morning. Especially since I have put a lot of work into creating a calm and peaceful wake-up routine. Only to have it blown before it begins by majorly malfunctioning tech. It does wake me up though. Just in all the wrong ways.

title: Worked at first
body:
I am and was looking for an app that would make an alarm strong enough and stubborn enough to match my sleep-hazed terribly irritated and proud self in the morning. I wake up wayyy early to do the pre-dawn Islamic prayer, and often times end up going to bed late, which makes it harder to take me out of the sleep cycle. You understand that I need something good to do this. I’m not upset this app can’t help me anymore, because it probably can someone else.

At first, the alarm was absolutely terrifying, and absolutely perfect. As a joke, I set the most horrifying sound I could find for free on there, completely forgetting I’d be the one to deal with it later, and faced that wrath. The adrenaline of waking up and thinking death was upon me DEFINITELY woke me up. However, the first problem happened here, for me.

In all my terror, I completely forgot to do the little memory game or whatever it was, and just decided to completely shut off my phone. Of course, I was still awake, but this knowledge stuck with me as a sort of “I survived” thing; my brain needed that out. 

So now, no matter what I do, I’ll just end up completely shutting off the phone when it wakes me up, thinking ‘naw I’m awake, I’m just gonna close my eyes against the lamp light’, and boom I completely miss my plans. 

It may work for you. It probably will. I’m just absolutely difficult to please. Enjoy.

It also tells you how long (x hours x minutes) you have until your alarm is set to go off, which is helpful. You also can make it so you have to do a certain task (take a certain picture or solve a puzzle, for example) before the alarm shuts off. I have the free version, and the ads really aren’t bad at all. Premium has several extra features (like more alarm sounds, the option to record your own, more tasks you have to do to dismiss the alarm, etc), but you’re not really missing anything either way.

to avoid this nonsense you have put your phone in do not disturb with “all calls blocked” while in do not disturb mode. this allows for the app to function normally and incoming phone calls do not cause the bug to occur. title: Pretty Great Solution
body:
By far the best alarm app I’ve used. I’ve always had trouble waking up and staying awake since I started using my phone as my main morning alarm clock. 

I’ve come up with my own solution with Alarmy by printing out a QR code and sticking it up in my bathroom. So I HAVE to get up and walk into some intense fluorescent lighting to turn it off by scanning the code. 9/10 times it works like a charm(old habits die hard, that’s my own fault lol.) 

The app is easy to use, has plenty of great options for different needs and the UI is attractive and easy to understand. I think the extras are more than worth paying for and I’m honestly glad I gave it a shot. 

There aren’t really any cons for me. The alarm sounds are good, it does what it says effectively and consistently and the developers genuinely seem to care about users. I’d recommend this to anyone who wants more from an alarm clock for whatever reason. Seriously happy with this app and I’ll be using it for the foreseeable future!

Before I had to use multiple alarms with a low chance of waking up on time, but with Alarmy I am instantly awake with just one. 

It can even wake the very heavy sleepers-capable of sleeping during a rough plane landing-in my family in seconds!

title: It doesn’t work like it used to.
body: This app was great when I first used it years ago. But now it doesn’t work. Something about the iOS restrictions: Alarmy is aware and released a statement and a workaround. The work around requires you to keep the app active in the background and you can’t use Do Not Disturb. Keeping it active in the background is cool but I receive calls and text from multiple time zones and my sleep would be interrupted if I didn’t use DND. If you follow the work arounds the alarm will work. But here’s the kicker. The best part of this app WAS how freaking persistent the tasks were. You really had to complete the task to disarm it. Or go crazy. There was no way around it. But not anymore, remember the alarm doesn’t work unless it’s active in the background. So if your alarm goes off at 5am and your super groggy and not in your right mind cuz you’re half asleep, and you quit the app instead of completing the task, it shuts the alarm off. Which means you don’t have to complete any of the task. Completing the task is what woke you up; they require brainpower and a certain level of consciousness. Before the iOS issues, if you quit the app the alarm would continue to go off until you completed the task. So now this app is just another basic alarm not unlike the one on your iPhone. So glad I didn’t pay for premium.

title: My Morning Savior
body: I sleep very deeply, especially in the early morning so it’s very hard for me to wake up. With regular alarms, I would somehow turn them off in my sleepy state and not remember turning them off at. Setting multiple alarms didn’t help me either. I even got an alarm clock and put it across the room so I had to get out of bed, but somehow I’d end up back in bed sleeping for too long. It got to a point where I was late to school every singe day in one week. I decided to google good alarms and I found Alarmy! I will never go back to using regular alarms. The math problem and memory games didn’t help me much, even on a difficult level because I would stay in bed, do what I had to and then go back to sleep. I decided to try the picture feature and it’s been a huge blessing for me! It’s infuriating when I’m laying in bed half asleep and there is no way to get it to turn off without getting up, but I wake up. Even though it’s the same thing as putting my alarm across the room, I think it takes more mental energy to be able to line the picture up with the previous set picture. I’ve set it to my bathroom sink since I need to go there in the morning anyways! I haven’t slept late at all since getting this app! By the time I get the picture line up correctly, I’m awake enough that I can think clearly and not allow myself to get back in bed. I also have a habit of taking really long naps. They usually are around 3 hours, so it’s a problem when I have something to do and can’t take my usual long nap. Alarmy has helped me get to work on time many times! I seriously wouldn’t wake up if it weren’t for it. This app is great and it really works!! I would 12/10 recommended! Edit: only thing is, I’ve learned how to trick the alarm into not making noise, in my sleep! So I’ll turn it off while sleeping and not wake up :/ no I just put it across the room and that works

title: Battery Issue!
body:
I love this app, but the battery drain from it is so significant that I’m looking for something to replace Alarmy. I have an iPhone 11 Pro Max, so it’s not old by any means. This is the only app I’ve downloaded in several weeks or change I’ve made with my phone usage in months. I have always had multiple weather apps run on background, for example, while receiving alerts. I have several social media and news apps that run on background that send multiple notifications throughout the day. Shopping apps, banking apps, email apps, all are being frequently used (way more than Alarmy) and they all are running on background and sending notifications. Yet the night I downloaded and used this app is when I started having battery drain. Yes I have tried turning off background run once I’m awake and turning it back on just before I go to bed. I can’t imagine how much worse it would be if I left it run on background all the time. 

When exactly is this going to be fixed? Why does it need to run on background anyway? Is this problem only on the free version?

TLDR. Pros: it’s simple, easy to use, has lots of free options for both the alarm and the shut off method. 1 con that negates all pros: going from 24-48 to BARELY 12 hour battery life on a 2 year old phone.

title: Game changer for the hearing disabled
body:
I don’t normally write reviews but this alarm literally saved my job.  I lost over half my hearing as an adult 10 years ago and tried all sorts of alarms that were loud and made my bed vibrate and I was waking up initially, only to quickly turn off the alarm and go back to sleep.

I had begun contemplate the cost of bedsheets and er visits for burns because an alarm that might set my bed on fire appeared to be my last hope for getting work on time.

Luckily I found this app that does not require self- immolation to work.

I have now been on time to work every single day since I started using it for 3+months.  Seriously.  My boss is not just off my back but has all but forgotten my earlier troubles.

After a few days of using it, I got the very reasonable premium subscription and the 90 second wake up check saved me from screening myself a dozen times.   Nice to be able to mix up the sounds a bit at random so I don’t tune the same one out.

If you have hearing loss, hate mornings, or just have trouble getting from sleep to awake you definitely need to try this out.

It’s definitely the most annoying app in my phone that I can’t live without.

title: Time to find a new app
body:
I love this app as it’s MUCH better than than stock iPhone alarm app. However, the recent updates prevents the app from ringing the second consecutive alarm. Let me explain in detail. 

I set two alarms with 15 minutes interval. The first rings perfectly; I hit the blue dismiss icon at the bottom and everything works fine. However, the second one never rings. The reason behind is that after you hit the blue dismiss icon, you’ve to press that small ‘x’ on top right corner to exit the “today’s panel”. Once you’ve done that, that’s when the second alarm will ring. I found out in the settings you can disable this, after having paid $59.99 for the year. 

So disappointed in the company. Guess it’s time to find another app to replace this.

title: No Customer Support
body:
I am mainly giving this app low stars because I sent Customer Support two messages 3 weeks ago and I still have not gotten a response. My issues may be fixable but I'll never know because no one will get back to me. I will address my concerns here. If their support responds I may update my review.

I would like more than one mission to be able to sequence with my alarm. For example, I want to start with squats to get the blood flowing, then do typing to engage my brain, then go take a picture to ensure I start a pot of coffee. I can't figure out how to assign more than one mission. It only allows me to select one. I have tried setting several missions up at the same alarm time and even one minute after another but it rarely works past the first mission. Not sure what happens or why the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, etc. alarms will not activate.

Also, I used this app many years ago and I feel like it was better then than it is now. I remember being able to have a sequence of several missions before the alarm would turn off and I was able to do this without having to set multiple alarms, I could do it with just one and it wouldn't be complete until they were all completed (ex: I could do math problems followed by memory game followed by taking a picture).

Additionally, I was playing around with the subscription options because it listed so
many different version/levels/price tiers to see if any of them unlocked different features that would allow me to assign multiple missions on one alarm. As far as I could see none of them did this. However, I got charged immediately (and seemingly multiple times! I got multiple emails) and it looks like now I did not get to enjoy the free trial. This needs to be fixed.

body: My phone usually ends the day at around 60-70%. I started using alarms because I needed a stronger commitment mechanism for waking up. The math problems were brilliant in this regard. I look at the battery usage and low and behold half the battery bar at EVERY SINGLE HOUR is spent on this app. “Background processes” apparently. There’s no reason for an alarm clock app to be taking up this much battery. I specifically even turned off background app refresh and it still drained my phone! I ended up removing the app and my battery usage is normal now. Either the app is really poorly optimized or there’s some sketchy ad service or mining operation being run in the background.

title: Wouldn’t stop
body:
Update after 3 weeks of use:
I switched from photo to scanning a barcode of something in the kitchen and that has been more effective. I’m taking off one star only because you cannot use the phones flashlight while the barcode scanner is open, meaning I have to find a light source. Rather than blind myself with the bright kitchen lights, I grab the salt and hunch down next to the little night light by the cat food to get it to work. Other apps with barcode scanners have a way to turn your light on - that would be really useful at 5am. And yet, for the FIRST time in my 30 years, I am up on time every single day. 

Original review:
I set this to take a photo of my coffee pot. Alarm went off as expected (extremely loudly I may add, as I fumbled with my phone trying o silence it while running from the bedroom so as to not wake up my husband). I get downstairs and take a photo of the coffee pot. Photo doesn’t match. Tried again. Photo doesn’t match. Tried at least 10 times. Lined it up as perfectly as I could. Doesn’t match doesn’t match doesn’t match. I quit the app, alarm wouldn’t stop. I turned off my phone but when I turned it back on the alarm just kept going. I ultimately made it stop by deleting the app but I feel like if I redownload it will start going again. There really needs to be some kind of “emergency shutoff.” On the plus side, I’m definitely awake.

title: Used to be my favorite. Till I discovered something terrible
body:
I. CAN'T. TURN. IT. OFF. ANYMORE!

Maybe some people like the idea of it being impossible to force stop an alarm that is ringing without doing the missions, but I do not like that I HAVE to do the missions JUST TO GET BACK TO THE NORMAL ALARM LIST!

I had chosen a very difficult and time consuming mission (3 sets of memorizing at maximum size) and it started going off like it was supposed to.

But  was not in a situation where I could stare at the screen that long, so all I could do was snooze.

OVER AND OVER.

It kept me on the alarm's screen and never let me go back to the alarm list. Only by dismissing and doing ALL the missions could I stop it.

Restarted phone. Nope, still ringing, still stuck on dismiss prompt. No button to go back.

Closed the app. It immediately started ringing again.

Turned on "do not disturb". Nope. Didn't shut up.

Restarted again with app closed and do not disturb. Nope. I get spammed with that alarm when I turn it on.

NEVER ONCE given the option to EVEN EDIT ANOTHER ALARM.

Searched desperately on the internet for help. Guess what? Plenty of articles BUT THEY'RE ALL ABOUT THE ANDROID VERSION!

Every google search hack I tried to force it to show only iphone articles, and all I got was either stuff about the STOCK alarm app or JUST A BUNCH OF TOP TEN ALARM APPS FOR IPHONE ARTICLES. Not ONE helpful article or reddit post or anything about how to force stop a SINGLE alarm in Alarmy for iphone.

The ONLY WAY was COMPLETELY uninstalling the app. I used this all the time and now I've lost all the alarms I had.

I am NOT reinstalling this, though, till that gets fixed. It used to have an option to go back, but no more. The distraction and frustration that caused could've been ****LIFE-THREATENING**** if I was in the wrong situation such as driving or some kind of emergency.

I don't like it when apps I install to help EMPOWER me end up making me feel so POWERLESS.

Now all those alarms are gone and I have to find and LEARN a whole new app with equal possibility of keeping me from sleeping in but also not making me ****crash into traffic.***

title: This app is changing my life
body:
When I first got this app I was frustrated for 3 reasons: the user interface is busy and ugly, instructions were unclear, and the paid version is very expensive. I quickly came to realize that none of those things mattered because this app works and is making me a better person. And you don’t need the paid version for every function I’m about to mention. I had to watch a YouTube video on how to utilize it best, but as someone who either doesn’t hear alarms or hits snooze without a second thought, here is what I do:
Set 1 alarm to go off every weekday at the same time. Set the alarm sound to “random” so that my brain doesn’t get “used to” one particular sound and tune it out. Set my “mission” to the bar code scanner and scan the code on my shampoo bottle. This requires me to scan my shampoo every single morning to turn my alarm off. And at that point I’m out of bed and halfway into the shower. In other words, I’m ACTUALLY up! No other alarm has gotten me to do that. And now I’m on time for things and not rushing. Life changing. I don’t care if it’s clunky and confusing, it’s AMAZING.

It’s safe to say, I will not be renewing another year. I don’t think it’s worth $60.

title: no more setting 10 alarms to only *maybe* wake up
body: I absolutely love this app. I cannot remember a time in my life where I would actually wake up and stay up. I opted to pay for the very reasonable premium subscription after I tested out the free trial. The physical challenges force me to wake up and get out of bed, in addition to starting my day off with some nice exercise. Potentially my favorite feature, amongst all the great options and settings, is the ability to select your alarm tone to ‘random.’ If I hear the same alarm every morning, my brain will eventually tune it out, and it won’t wake me up anymore. Even the most obnoxious alarm tone Apple offers (you know the one) will not do anything. But with the random option, a different alarm tone will play every morning, and will only get louder and louder. If you decide to go for premium, a great feature is the ‘wake up check’ where they will prompt you to make sure you’re still awake, and you have to select ‘yes’ within a certain amount of time, otherwise you have to do your whole wake up mission again. There’s also great alarm ‘power ups’ that you can choose from if you need extra motivation to get up in the morning. I never thought I would see the day where one alarm wakes me up, but I’m glad to finally be here. If you’re a chronic late sleeper, there’s not an app or alarm I can recommend more.

title: Useless unless you pay $60 for a stupid alarm app
body:
This app locks so many of its features down unless you pay $60 a year for premium, and that for the annual. the month by month is $7.50 ($90 a year) 

Like I’m fine with devs getting paid for their work but to make people pay that much for simple things like wake up check. Or a single loud sound backup is ridiculous. That’s like charging someone money to change the resolution it should be default.

The price tag is more outrageous when you look at how many features it doesn’t have, compared to other apps. It offers no randomized sound playlist. It doesn’t have auto snooze so you can’t get used to the audio.

 It doesn’t open on the Home Screen so every morning you will need to sign in your phone and navigate to the app (iOS doesn’t let apps do show one the Home Screen. Only the apple clock can) I bring this up cause the challenge settings for the app make it kinda useless when it’s a challenge to open any 3rd party alarm app. 

The music they have isn’t even complete songs it’s small clips. Just like a lot of this app it’s lazy

Theres alot more stuff missing or behind an outrageous pay wall.
look at any other alarm app it will probably have more features. Alarm options and not cost anything for features.
Alarm apps should charge for more sounds. Or remove ads. Or even just a support us purchase. Which is a one time payment.

If you find a good app you should support the devs but support them with a responsible amount. alarms are easy to program. A $5 one time purchase is more then enough to say thanks for an app that plays a sound at a specific time. But $60 a year is just greedy cause they are the first app you see when searching alarms.

title: Simply the best
body:
This is THE alarm clock app. If you’re looking for an alarm clock app, stop. Download this one.

Like many people here I’ve had issues waking up to my alarm, which sent me down the path of finding a different alarm clock app. Enter Alarmy. 

The app has multiple different actions, some that come with the free versions and some with the paid version. For example, I use the barcode action (free) so that I have to scan a barcode in the kitchen in order to shut my alarm off. This works well for me, as I have to get up out of bed and walk down the hallway. Since I’m up, I don’t go back to sleep. If this wouldn’t work for you, there are others to choose from. 

The customization (disable snooze, etc.), and the alarm sounds are great. 

My only critique of this app and not enough to take any stars off would be the pro version pricing model. The price of $60/year or $7.50 a month seems pretty steep for the features. I would gladly pay a lifetime fee for the pro version, or maybe $20-25/year, but not $60 or more with the premium.

If I manage to wake up, it’s like I’m a different person for the first 10 minutes of my day, and I WILL go back to bed, despite my best interest. Most alarms stop ringing after 5-10 minutes, impossible for mere mortals to sleep through, however no issue for me some days. This app conquers all those problems.

 I am a sleepy person. I will sleep ALL DAY if you let me. I have tried every whacky alarm on the market. Light up your room alarms, vibrating bed alarms, my Alexa even wakes me up with morning affirmations. None of those helped, but this app has me up and at ‘em on time. It is the ONLY REASON I am a functioning member of society. Just download it.

title: Subpar and unreliable
body:
Like a lot of the five star reviews, I do have positive things to say about the app. It’s louder than a lot of apps I heard and for a while was more reliable than the alarm my phone came with. 

That being said, it’s become really unreliable. If I set an alarm for five hours later, for the most part it will go off. But if I set one for an hour, it consistently goes off silently. I triple check that the alarm is open, my volume is up, my phone isn’t silenced, and it’s plugged into the charger. So why have I woken up multiple times to it ringing completely silently? This has also been a problem with multiple phones now, so I know it’s not my phone. 

It’s so crazy that alarm apps will randomly not perform their only function. I set alarms to go off across three different apps, each set to go off several minutes after the other. The fact that Alarmy tries to charges $60 ANNUALLY is insane on its own, but factoring in that it’s hit or miss with going off makes it that much more ridiculous.  

Lastly, there’s a horoscope feature you can add to the “today’s panel” and most of the time it has normal messages. But several times it’s given me messages about losing weight or saying to not overeat? Wth is that?? This was several months ago, I stopped reading them so I don’t know if they fixed them. But that message is especially irritating if you struggle with your body image. 

Would love if the developers responded to at least acknowledge that the alarms sometimes don’t go off and it’s not just user error. But given that I mentioned the $60 charge I highly doubt they’d want to respond since they seem to be avoiding addressing that.

author: Wanda s. B

title: This app helps solve a problem I’ve had for YEARS
body:
I have narcolepsy. Luckily I have medicine that will keep me awake - but only if I actually TAKE it. You would be shocked, SHOCKED, at how difficult it is for me to wake up just long enough to grab a pill bottle, get a pill out, and swallow it. I tried everything I could think and everything the Internet suggested to me. None of it worked. I bought a vibrating alarm clock to shake my bed (slept through it). I slept with the pill bottle under my pillow (it kept falling off the bed and getting lost). I put the bottle all the way on the other side of the room so I’d have to physically stand up to get it (I just rolled over and went back to sleep). I put my alarm clock next to the bottle on the other side of the room (wake up, smash snooze button, crawl back in bed without ever touching the bottle). I was at my wit’s end. 

Another narcoleptic recommended this app to me and HOLY CRAP IT WORKS. I use the “mission” where you scan a bar code. I have to get up, grab my meds, and scan the code on my medicine bottle to make my phone stop screeching at me. That finally did it. I’m up and taking my medicine like I’m supposed to now!

 I really love that you have the option to set the alarm tone to shuffle randomly, so you never get used to hearing the same sound and learn to sleep through it! I’ve been using Alarmy for months now and haven’t gotten used to any of the alarm tones. They have a good range of tones - some of them are pleasant, some are mildly irritating, and some make you wanna yeet your phone into the nearest garbage disposal. The tones, combined with the utter stubbornness of the app (you really cannot trick it, you HAVE to complete your “mission” like you’re supposed to), makes this app super effective. 

It worked so well that my spouse also uses it now, even though he doesn’t have a sleep disorder (thank god). He likes the math problem missions because they wake up his brain.

Some of the better missions are locked behind a paywall but honestly I think they’re more than worthy the money. This is a beautifully and thoughtfully designed app and I am happy to support the developers!

author: Rebecca - Personal Experience

title: Great Idea / Mostly Dependable / Too Much $$
body: I’ve been using the free version of this app. When it works, it’s extremely helpful. Problems: Unfortunately, if the app is not open and recently used it will only go off silently - I believe it will vibrate if you have vibration activated on your phone for notifications. I have vibration deactivated on my phone for reasons related to my job, so it just silently pushes notifications while I sleep away. What’s frustrating is that this can happen even if you’ve left alarmy on in the background but you’ve used too many other apps since then. The only way to be confident it will work is to close out your other apps and make sure alarmy was the last app you used before going to bed. When doing that, it’s only had an issue once in about a year and I don’t know what went wrong that time. I think having to do all that extra work to know my alarm will go off is very annoying and borderline too much trouble, but since the app has helped me as well, I’m still putting up with those issues for now. Strengths: The missions are extremely helpful for waking me up. I’ve found that the shake mission works well personally for me. I do 150 shakes with the difficulty set on hard and it gets my blood flowing enough to wake me. When waking up in time is extremely important, setting a series of missions is really helpful. Like starting with shaking and then setting a second one soon after with barcode scan so I have to get up and go somewhere to turn it off. Combos like that work well. I’m interested in some of the other missions in the paid version, but cannot justify the price for premium. Price: I’m grateful for the free version. If there was not a free version or if it was a lot more limited than it is now, I wouldn’t be using this app. I want to use the premium version, because I really like the idea of typing motivational or custom phrases to help with things I want to memorize, but I just can’t justify the expense. The seemingly permanent “sale” of $59.99 is way too high for this kind of an app. I guess somebody out there is paying for it, but I’m sorry, I’m not willing to pay for $60 every year for an alarm that I don’t even get to keep if I don’t keep paying $60 a year for it. How is that a good idea? That’s way more expensive in the long run than physical alarms and this one doesn’t even have any material or manufacturing costs. Only R&D and software development costs that a physical alarm also has. So as much as I want to use the premium version and would consider paying around a $40 one-time cost or a much lower monthly subscription, the current price just doesn’t seem right. Especially when I have to jump through so many hurdles just to make sure the alarm will go off when I need it to. Hope this review helps somebody out there. I’m still using the free version of this app at the moment. Just doing the annoying routine of refreshing it every night and setting other native and physical alarms anytime waking up on time for something is extra important/risky.

title: It works.
body:
I got this app when I started working night shifts and kept sleeping through my day classes. A lot of people say they’re a heavy sleeper, and I’m no different. I’ve slept through at least 4 fire alarms while I lived in dorms. This is the only app I trust to wake me up if I’m taking a 90 minute nap or only getting 3 hours of sleep. It’s highly customizable and it really has a lot of features with the free edition. I’ve been using it for 5 years for free, today I got the paid version because anything you use daily for five years ought to be good. Over those five years I did have ads but there were no pop ups, and the couple banner ads that are there aren’t intrusive at all.

I would highly recommend this app for anyone that struggles to wake up. The games you can say to dismiss the alarm offer flexibility. I’m barely able to do 16x13 in my head fully awake, much less with a blaring alarm screaming at me after sleeping for 6 holes. The only reason you shouldn’t try this app is if you don’t struggle waking up at all like some kind of sleep hating psychopath. But if that were you, you wouldn’t be reading this review.

title: Extremely Helpful, but One Problem…
body:
I have some sleep disorders, so waking up is extremely difficult for me. Alarmy has made such a huge difference - it forces my brain to start working. I set the alarms so that they progressively get harder - first I do the ones where you shake the phone, then 5x5 memory, and then a few math problems. Then I set larger memory problems and harder math problems. It’s helped tremendously. 

You want to make sure that you turn off the alarms when you don’t need them (like if you have to go to work early; you don’t want one of these ringing while you’re trying to have a meeting with your boss), and also to leave this app open and in the foreground when you put your phone down. 

My biggest complaint is the news section that comes up after you turn off an alarm. I understand that they want to present news articles that will appeal to a variety of folks. However, Fox News? Seriously? And even worse, it’s often these fear-mongering headlines about COVID vaccines. We are living in the middle of a pandemic and the only way out of it is vaccination. Meanwhile, every morning people have to see these headlines about “Scary new thing linked to the vaccines,” which are clearly misleading and ignoring the facts about COVID and the risks associated with the virus (guess what - you’re at risk of those problems if you get the virus, and the risk is much higher!!). Alarmy showing these deliberately misleading and false headlines is harmful. If Alarmy is going to show news articles, then they need to show unbiased, credible reporting - The AP, BBC, PBS, NPR, Reuters, NYTimes, The Washington Post, etc. Spreading the propaganda that Alarmy shows is dangerous at best. They either need to show responsible, accurate, non-biased news reporting, or show none at all.

title: Best alarm out there, you can stop your search now!!
body:
This is not just the only alarm, but the only THING I have found that actually gets me up. And it does it consistently and well every morning, being forced to take a picture of the shower every morning since I can’t sleep with the alarm sound works so perfect for me. 

To be able to turn the alarm off, you have some options. You can set it to have to take a picture of whatever you choose (you set a picture beforehand and the picture you take has to match), you can do math problems, you can type out sentences, you can shake your phone, and you can scan a barcode. (I think all those are free) they also have some other options for premium! 

The alarm sound variety isn’t great, I like a super soft wake up that slowly gets louder and they only have one sound that does something close to that (and not a lot of options overall, you can only choose from so many if you use it free). However, I decided to pay for premium since I’m starting my first year of college so now I can record my own sounds! Even if you pay for premium though, ($60/year) you can’t set a song to be your alarm unless it’s DRM free, which is more complicated to do. 

Without premium, you get: 
1. Five ish options for turning the alarm off
2. Can turn on the snooze button 
3. Label your alarms  
4. As many alarms as you want
5. Set your alarms to repeat any day or combo of days of the week
6. Choose the volume and vibration intensity 
7. Can choose from some sleep music/nature sounds to play 
8. News feature 

With premium, you also get: 
1. ‘Wake up check’ feature 
2. Three ‘Power ups’ (1 reads out the time every minute while ringing, 1 does the same but with the label you set on the alarm, and 1 blares a really loud alarm after no response from you for 40 seconds) 
3. More alarm sound options 
4. You can record your own sound to wake up to
5. I think 3 more missions to be able to turn off the alarm 
6. Ad-free

Thanks Alarmy, you have changed my mornings to be 1000% better! :)

Whoever created this app really put some thought into it.There are so many features in this app. You can set alarms for power naps, early morning alarms, as well as alarms for things you need to accomplish. While there are some premium features, it can still be used for free. For every alarm you set, you have the option of doing a mission or whether you want your phone to vibrate or not.(These are examples of some of the missions available: squats, steps, memory games, math, etc.) You can set how loud your alarms are. You can turn snooze on or off. You can label your alarm and choose from a variety of sounds. After you wake up and complete the mission (optional), you will see the date and receive a daily fortune. You can read some news articles and then start your day. And for all those who have difficulty sleeping, there is sleeping music available on the app. (You don’t have to download any of the sleeping music in order to listen to it) This long review can be summarized by saying that Alarmy is a fascinating app and I would recommend downloading it.

title: Must have in everyday life
body:
I’ve always found it hard to wake up. All I used to do was press snooze, and then proceed to wake up 20-30 minutes later. This was a big problem.

I think I watched a video or something on this app and said, “heck, it’s free! I’ll give it a try.”

The feature I’ve found most helpful is the QR scanner. It’s so valuable because I live in a loft bed and anything that scares me enough to force me down the ladder is awesome.
For some reason every time I hear the sound of the rooster I jump out of bed and start running down the hall to scan my mouthwash before it gets too loud.

If you’re on the fence GET IT. I think that the math equations and memory game could benefit different people in different situations.

Happy sleeping- er waking up!

Update: I decided to add a little more to my review now that I’ve used it for about 9 months.
First of all, most of the different options get me up easily. For perspective, if I do the math one I will do very hard for 10 questions. If you aren’t as good at math, normal for 5 will probably accommodate your needs.
Shaking works pretty well, though I have to do a lot to make me stay up. Usually I will do 100 and it works for the days I’m not waking up very early but still am in danger of falling back asleep.
Finally, memory works similar to math where you have to activate your brain to do it. I usually do 5 times 5 and it works even better than math and is less frustrating. I found that using memory also made me more likely to get out of bed immediately and less likely to just open social media and scroll. It is what I now use about 1/3 of the time during night and always for naps. (I use QR scanning most of the time)
I appreciate that there is a pro version, and though I haven’t personally tried it (tight budget!) it might be helpful for the deepest of sleepers.

To the creators, thank you from the bottom of my heart. And to the people reading this, I hope you benefit from Alarmy as much as I have.

title: Great alarm, but sketchy usage of our Privacy
body:
Like most apps, this one also collects our privacy data to sell to others. What’s weirder is this being an alarm app they give a GPS feature for “Weather” when they more so want it for our Geolocation. 

When I first downloaded the app I never closed it for 2 weeks because it sent a notification claiming the alarm wouldn’t activate. I later accidentally closed it and since then the alarm has kept working as intended. Showing me that having the app open at all times allowed for them to track your Geolocation and other privacy stuff while it was open in the background. And the alarm still worker while closed.

With the new iPhone update, we now have a cool “Request app tracking” feature. It forces apps to request our consent to track our privacy data instead of them taking it without our permission/knowledge. 
But this app is the first app that does NOT give you an option to opt out of tracking. You only get an “OK” option, so be warned.

All in all, the app is good. But be prepared for the “Spyware” type of tracking it does.

title: Great app, one request
body:
Hello! I’ve been using Alarmy for months now and so far good results! I’ve been using the sleep sounds to fall asleep since I have trouble falling asleep and they’ve helped me so much. Overall, the features are great and useful.

However, I do have one complaint//request. And that is the option for emergency dismiss. The reason I request this is the other day I was in class and a random alarm went off that i didn’t realize I set and I couldn’t dismiss it since it was a barcode and I no longer had that barcode. Since I had no way to disable it I had to power my phone off for the rest of the school day. Though it is my fault the alarm was set in the first place, an emergency dismiss without a task would be very helpful in any situation. 

In conclusion I recommend this app to heavy sleepers, unable to fall asleep sleepers and anyone in between

Thanks for reading 💕💕

title: Wake-up the Right Way
body:
Alarmy is seriously the best thing to happen to me. 

In the past, I would sleep through my alarm, or actually turn it off IN MY SLEEP. I was habitually late, and my job was in jeopardy. This app has been a complete game changer. There are so many options, including just a basic alarm. It’s literally impossible to turn this thing off unless I complete the tasks I set. Not only that, it still sounds even when the phone is on silent mode. I can’t tell you how many times I forgot my phone was on silent from work, went to bed, and the alarm wouldn’t sound. Alarmy makes sure it’s heard! 
AND to top it all off, this app also provides news headlines, weather, and my horoscope (which is eerily accurate). It’s completely customizable and all around my favorite app of all time.

title: This app is wonderful but still not enough for me
body:
I love this app, there’s nothing wrong with it, it’s perfect for what it’s intended to do. 

However my sleepy self is willing to do anything to keep from waking up, so instead of fully waking up and doing my mission, I’d just delete the app then go back to sleep. I realized this after waking up late, going to check the app to see what was wrong with it, and realizing that it wasn’t on my phone anymore. 

Next step was parental restrictions. I turned off the “delete apps from device” option in the Screentime settings, thinking there’s no way I could get past that. I was wrong though—I started waking up to a phone that had been turned off, presumably when the alarm went off and couldn’t be quickly silenced.

So to everyone out there thinking that this app will be the solution to your problems—it might be, or you might just find yourself fighting a more intense wake-up war.

title: It’s helped me after a few attempts.
body: I have insomnia and depression, so getting up in the morning can be exceptionally difficult somedays. It got to the point where I was turning off alarms with zero memory of doing so. I downloaded this app in hopes of compating that, but ran into some difficulties at first. I started deleting the app without memory of doing so each morning, waking up late and wondering where the app went on my phone. title: Great for non morning people
body:
I absolutely hate waking in the morning but of course see the benefits (like not being late). I try to wake up so I have time to actually get ready but it never works. I’ve gotten into the habit of just turning of my alarm and going back to bed. Even if I put my phone across the room, I still go directly back to bed. What people always tell me is that I have terrible self discipline and need to work to get it up. But I already know that and I’m working on it. But building up self discipline takes time and when I need start getting up earlier now, I don’t have that time. 
But with Alarmy, I start getting up earlier and it’s a little bit easier. Trust me, I still hate getting up in the morning but Alarmy forces my butt out of bed and out of my room. It really helped when I had video calls. I wasn’t waking up 2 minutes before the call anymore. I use the barcode one primarily but I’ve tried all of them and enjoy them all. (I also like how you don’t have to have a mission on) The barcode one is amazing because it forces me to get out of my room. I have it set for something in my bathroom because I usually brush my teeth first and it helps kickstart my routine. Plus, it’s a lot easier to convince me not to go back to my comfy bed when I’m in my not so comfy bathroom. I actually have time to get fully ready and I’m not doing stuff in the car. Which is amazing! I can do a fully face of makeup and I’m not in a bumpy car rushing. It’s awesome. 
Thank you so much Alarmy for helping actually get up in the morning. I can’t wait to actually have time to get ready for school.

author: cheetopickle

title: I don’t usually write reviews
body:
So when I do, I think the app is a big deal. I used to use the iOS stock alarm clock and I was late for work about twice a year - unacceptable. My problem is that I would acknowledge the alarms, turn them off, and go back to sleep. 
Alarmy mitigates this by forcing you to engage with the app and wake your brain up. and it is LOUD. And if you force-close the app it will re open and send you constant notifications until you re-open the app and complete the puzzle. For some this might be a bit much- but for people like me this is perfect.
The best part is that the free app gives you everything you need, and the ads are not obtrusive. Some “free” apps will hide their useful features behind a paywall, but Alarmy gives you everything you need off the bat, and offers even more compelling upgrades if you wish to pay. This is how it should be - well done!

title: MUST USE
body:
I'm a student with morning classes (since they aren’t offered later) and I tend to continue studying until late at night because my major is quite demanding. I was recommended this by a friend and it's a lifesaver. I sleep like a rock. I can fall asleep on command but I won't wake up. My regular alarm wasn't doing it and I'm pretty sure my first class teachers wondered what happened to me in the mornings because it wasn't pretty. I would go to my first class looking all disheveled and fix myself during the break period.
Now with Alarmy, I get up and stay up. I am forced to start moving and wake myself uo with the Shake function since I leave my phone on my night stand and I can’t just reach and click snooze. Then I actually have time to get ready for school and sometimes I even have left over time to scroll through my SNS. My last one is to take a picture of my (packed) bag so I'm actually ready to leave the dorms (without running)
I also have startle epilepsy, so seizures that can be caused by sudden noises/surprises. A past alarm I tried was too sudden and caused me to have a few episodes but Alarmy has been working great. Your alarm will gradually get louder but not alarmingly (no pun intended) loud. Just loud enough to wake up a rock :)
Thank you Alarmy~~♡

title: Love this app
body: ALARMY has changed my life.  I was literally the guy that set 6 alarms every 10 minutes an hour before I actually needed to get up.  My wife LOVED that! Then I tried the shake method, and realized I can shake my phone REALLY hard for a long time and still fall back asleep. Finally I picked the photo one, I have to get up and walk all the way across my house and take a picture perfectly. This was perfect.   By the time I do that, I’m AWAKE. Fast forward a couple years, now I’m up and out of bed within 5 seconds of my alarm going off. Don’t even wake the wife most days.  Pretty sure I could switch to any old alarm clock now, I’ve been conditioned.  But I just keep using the app, for now.

title: It’s Worth Paying the Monthly Subscription!
body:
I have bought every kind of alarm clock you you can think of. 

The kind with the light that, “slowly, naturally wakes you.”

My daughter bought me the type that has the target and you shoot it with the laser gun to get the alarm to go off. That was amazingly loud and irritating until it went berserk at 3AM and I had to put it out of its misery (cheap product - but it was fun!)

So many different kinds of alarms - simple ones, tech ones... I’d sleep through them all, or keep on hitting snooze.

I’m one of those who is a horrible sleeper and is already a natural night owl. Combine that, and I toss/turn until 3/4AM every day & by the time 6:30AM rolls around - I am finally ZONKED out from exhaustion.

I still oversleep, because I can hit snooze and go right back to sleep, but it’s not the alarm - it’s me. I wake up from it 95% of the time, I just snore right back to sleep. And that’s even doing the shake or math method. 

I’m going to try a harder math level and maybe that will help. I’m so very thankful my bosses understand my sleep issues and are okay with me being late probably 1X a week by 20M.

(We won’t mention the 2X when they all had to call for about 2HRS to finally get me to wake up 🙄🤦‍♀️🙄)

But again - that’s not the alarm, that’s me. Alarm is great.

ESPECIALLY #7 and use the label enhancement. You can have a voice say WHATEVER YOU WANT. I also have it call my dogs and stuff.

Choo-Choo come give Mommy kisses.
Diva, go kiss Momma.
(my hubby) Frank!! Wake up your f*cking lazy a** wife! (There’s one that says that and others MUCH WORSE😆😆)

title: The Best Alarm and the only alarm that can Wake anyone up
body:
This app is so sensibly designed. It has so many options that can be used to really get over the habit of snoozing. This app has melodious nature tunes that sounds so natural in the early morning rather than annoying loud common tunes. The idea of selecting appropriate game based on how much work you would like to give your brain the first thing in the morning takes away the stress of dismissing alarm and can be used by even young kids of 7+ years. The setting of rounds helps you to be completely awake before you unconsciously doze off again. Fun part is it is smart too, it starts over from 1 if you happen to sleep in between completing all the rounds. 
I am surprised by the idea that is put into building this app and the way logic is set up to actually serve the purpose. No wonder all YouTubers talking about waking up early is mentioning about this. This is totally a worth it app to download by default.
Kuddos to all the people behind this app, you have made waking up early a nice experience to even deep sleepers and snoozers.

Thank you!

title: 5-star App
body:
This is a 5-star app! Yes, I gave it a four, but that’s only because I wish more of their features were free. I did the free-trial when I first downloaded it and it was amazing but I can’t afford to continue paying for them. 
Even without those extra features, this is still a great alarm to use. I haven’t used any other kind of alarm app (besides the one that came on my iPhone) but I don’t imagine you can get better than this Alarmy app! 
I am the type of person who literally sets 50 alarms all within a few minutes apart so that I can wake up. I have tried numerous alarm clocks and even bought an Alexa and plugged it in across the room (which still didn’t work as I just get on the app and turn it off real quick). 
With this app I am able to wake up at the time I set it for ONCE because it makes you! Having to do 10 math problems just to shut it off, really works! They also have shaking it x amount of times with a sensitivity setting, or walking so many steps. 
My favorite was on the paid features; you can have it tell you whatever you want. I used “Wake the F up Lisa, or your kids will be late for school and be failures and you will fail as a mother and in life!”, along with some other funny ones cursing myself to get up! ;) 
Then, the other (paid for feat.) was the “Are you up yet?” setting, which is like a bada** snooze. It waits 3 minutes (or whatever time you choose) and asks if you’re up yet; then you must do more tasks to prove that you are. So if for some reason the first alarm didn’t work the snooze sure will! 
Again, even without the paid-for features, this app is still amazing and worth downloading! Whether you’re a heavy sleeper or not, or go back to sleep every time like I do, this app will get you up! 
The alarms are very loud compared to the one included on your phone (which makes no sense on how they do that) but it is! Then the free wake up features still do a great job! 
My husband hates it but I love it! 
He can wake up to any sound and has to listen to it until I finally grab it and take ten minutes trying to do math in the mornings! ;) 

If you’re struggling, look no further! 
If you can afford it, I highly suggest paying for the additional features! They do have the free-trial so you can try before you buy, which is always great! 
Alarmy, y’all did a great job! 👏
My family thanks you too! ;)

title: Monthly fee for an alarm???
body:
I love the function of this alarm, but really struggle with it practically. I literally only use it for the function where you can only quiet the alarm by scanning a barcode. Without this, I do not get up on time and my day is completely different. However, in order for it to play, you have to be sure it’s running at least in background, and that your volume is not on silent (this one’s a kicker, as someone who often gets texts in the middle of the night), and I’ve had issues where the alarm doesn’t go off because of this, but I think that’s just how all apps have to work with iOS.
Still, by far the worst thing about this app is that it is over saturated with ads and many of the functions are behind a paywall of $5/month. I would gladly pay to upgrade the app once, but that repeating price tag makes me laugh, who can pay every single month for an alarm that isn’t even perfectly reliable?
It’s all I can do to hope someone else develops a barcode alarm that I can afford to use without so many ads, but so far this is the only app that does it.

title: This app is TOO effective. Worth the subscription
body:
I really hate this app, but that’s a good thing. I’m a middle aged woman and up to now have never found a way to wake up early. At first. I was skeptical that the alarm tones weren’t loud or annoying enough. When the alarm actually went off -OMG- I hate that sound so much! It sounds like a drill for a nuclear attack and my body goes into flight or fight mode. I wake up as quickly as possible to make it end as quickly as possible! 

After reading other reviews, I was afraid there were bugs that would allow me to outsmart it.  I have tried turning my phone off, turning down the volume, exiting out of the app before the alarm rings.  None works and only makes things worse for my cheating self.  I thought I had outsmarted it when I found I could get it to count steps by shaking my phone, but then after about 15 steps it warned me I was cheating and then added the steps back on. I have not been desperate enough to try deleting the app when it’s alarming. At some point, it’s about free will. 

You have to be REALLY certain you want to wake up the night before when you activate it because there’s no going back.  I learned this the hard way one Sunday I had wanted to sleep in.

title: UPDATED: I wish I could give this 5 stars...
body:
UPDATE #2: Unfortunately, there's another bug that's popped up, where one of my QR code alarms doesn't always go off at the scheduled time (12:03 am), but instead sometimes goes off at precisely 5:33 am... waking me up in the middle of the night. I'll groggily open the alarm, and then Alarmy will tell me it's turned off the "stale alarm" because it's more than three hours after the alarm time. I tried many times to send feedback about this and got a "Failed to sent feedback" message several times, so hopefully the Alarmy team received it. 

I really want to give this app five stars - the QR feature alone is worth it, and has helped me so much to wake me up in the morning and keep me on time! - but if it wakes me up in the middle of the night, I can't give it five stars. :(

UPDATE: The Alarmy team fixed the original bugs so quickly: I can name all my alarms again, and the QR code problem has been fixed! +Many stars for that!

ORIGINAL: So Alarmy has some brilliant ideas, especially the QR code alarm. But there are some pretty big bugs. Sometimes when I exit the QR scan photo screen several times in a row when doing the QR scan mission, Alarmy does not allow me to go back to the photo QR scan and I cannot complete the mission, and I have to force quit the app. Also, after trying a subscription and canceling because of this bug, I can not give names to any of my alarms! (It does not save the name.) I would report these bugs, but... the in-app bug report (leave feedback) form is buggy. The keyboard covers the "Send" button so you cannot send any feedback whatsoever. Please fix and I can give this app the five stars it deserves!

title: Good alarm app
body: This is a great alarm, although beware to make sure you set the picture right otherwise you will be in for a fun surprise in the morning. The first night I used this I accidentally set the picture to the picture of a waterfall I’d taken, during a trip to Yellowstone, instead of the intended kitchen sink. I woke up the next morning to see the picture, and realized it was gonna be quite the long day. I got in the car, drove the entire day until I finally arrived at the waterfall. But, in my stupidity, I’d set the sensitivity to high, which meant I had to wait till the sun was fully out to get the lighting right. After the alarm was finally turned off, I traveled home to find that my wife had left me along with the kids. She left me a note, saying that she hoped I was happy with whoever I ran off with, since I was clearly not happy with her. I tried to call and explain, but my phone had died from constantly ringing for the last 24 hours. So in the end, it’s a great app, but be careful or you might lose everything you ever loved. 5 out of 5 stars.

body: Okay, I NEVER write reviews. It’s not really my ‘thing’ and very few apps affect me enough to even think about reviewing it. Alarmy however, is truly life-changing. I started college this year and was terrified of the thought of missing a class that costed thousands of dollars just because I ‘couldn’t wake up’. I downloaded alarmy and let me tell you... I finished my first semester and wasn’t late to one single class. I start off with one alarm with shake, then a second with math, and a third with memory. If you have issues waking up or even just need some mental stimulation when you wake up, alarmy is the way to go, I swear. I will be using this until the day I die.

title: Phenomenal
body:
I downloaded this app because I never like waking up in the morning for any reason. My wife is a morning person til the end and I’m more of a stay up late guy. She always asks me to wake up early with her and start our day together but I apparently shut my alarms off in my sleep (I’m on strike and don’t have to be up for work).  So I downloaded this without telling her, and the first day that it went off she sat straight up in bed and didn’t know what was going on (all new sounds that aren’t like the ones on IOS). Then she seen me doing math problems and taking pictures of her while she was still in bed. So I explained it to her and she laughed of course but she was highly impressed that A) I woke up to an alarm for the first time in over a year and B) that I actually took initiative to do something she asked me to do lol.  
The math problem missions definitely throw you for a loop first thing in the morning and the picture mission is hard to get used to, but it’s def effective, it took me 4 tries to get the picture right, but I don’t mind because I got to take pictures of my wife first thing in the morning (every guys dream).

So all in all, this alarm works.  I woke up easily, not abruptly. My wife is happy that I can wake up without her assistance, and our intimate life has changed already (she promised if I woke up early with her that I would be rewarded every time).

Many thanks to all of the developers and managers who seen this project through until the end. It was much worth it and it is very much appreciated.

You get a morning exercise to get your brain going and start your day which you get to determine the difficulty of, and you can change all sorts of alarms, all of them loud. The only thing I didn’t like is that you have to completely enter the app to dismiss it. Also, the only reason I got the premium was bc of the free trial and I feel that it is super cool, you get more exercises to choose from, you can submit a recording to wake you up, and if you struggle with falling back asleep, the premium allows you to add an alarm where, if you don’t turn it off in a certain number of minutes immediately, you have to start over again. title: Perfect for Hypersomniacs!
body:
This app is perfect for people with sleep disorders. I have Idiopathic Hypersomnia which means I’m always tired no matter how much sleep I get. I have to take medicine to keep me awake, and waking up to take it in the morning was borderline impossible until I found this app. I would either sleep through alarms or turn them off without realizing it and immediately go back to sleep. With this app, I love that it just gets louder so you can’t ignore it, and that I have to do a challenge to shut it up. I like the “shake” challenge, I set it to where I have to shake it really hard 30 times, which requires me to move, which makes it easier to actually fully wake up.

Long story short, this app is a game changer for anyone with hypersomnia, narcolepsy, shift sleep disorder, or the like. Two thumbs up!!

title: Should’ve left the old quick alarm widget
body:
The biggest selling point for this app was the quick alarm widget. I was glad to see that widget was updated at first. Then I realized that you removed some of the Jerry features that made it unique.

1) Micro intervals - The smaller 1/5/10/30 min increments were a HUGE selling point. Something for short naps or a quick alarm if I put something on the stove. If I need to set an alarm 6 or 8 hours from now I’ll open the actual app, not use the widget.

2) The old widget allowed you to add those intervals together to get a precise alarm. You didn’t need 8 different interval options when you could add the smaller increments until you hit a total you liked. Now each quick alarm sets an individual alarm, no totaling, and you go from 5 to 10 min to 1/6/8 hours.

3) The widget’s stark white background is brutal on the eyes, especially when the rest of your phone is in night mode.

So if you’re going to all but kill one of your defining features, there is no reason to keep an app that charges a monthly subscription fee to get access to features that a number of other apps do as good or better and don’t charge for.
