title: Struggle to Wake up? Keep getting back in bed? Use this app.
body:
I am a very tired person. Often, I like to stay up late, making it very hard to get up on time the next day. I found myself either wasting hours of each day just struggling to get up and stay up - neither truly resting nor being productive - or being late to whatever morning appointment or obligation I had to get to.

Then, I found Alarmy. Alarmy is a different sort of alarm than anything I’ve used before.
Alarmy knows my struggle. It knows my pain. So, Alarmy works hard to wake me up and doesn’t let me get away with getting back in bed.

Alarmy has innovative features that make it hard to ignore. For instance, I currently have it set that my alarm won’t turn off until I scan the barcode on my morning cup of coffee, which I make immediately. Alarmy gets me there, the caffeine helps me stay up long enough to truly be awake.

The alarm may not sound nice (depending on which one you need. I definitely need the harsher one). But, for hard or long tasks (such as the barcode scanning), the alarm will pause for 30 seconds or so while you try to do the thing it requires.

There’s other modes too, like math problems with customizable difficulty and number of problems, or shaking the phone itself a customizable number of times at a customizable strength.
I can tell the developers put a lot of thought into each method and how it might help someone wake up.
The math problems make sure you’re mentally awake and thinking; not half-asleep. The barcode can ensure you get to a task or area where the barcode is at. The shaking task makes sure you have enough physical movement, if physical activity is what wakes you up. And there’s many more alarm types in there.

Best of all, I can tell the developers listen to feedback. A long time ago, I think when the app was fairly new, I sent feedback requesting a new alarm type of having to type a phrase. Lo and behold, this is now a feature! Granted, I haven’t tried it yet because it’s a pro feature, but I was excited to see it nonetheless.

There’s a couple limitations of the app, which are absolutely just limitations of iOS in the first place. For instance, Alarmy can’t sound the alarm if the app is not running in the background of your phone, due to the way iOS works. Alarmy warns you of this when you set an alarm, so you know not to close the app.
However, sometimes my phone dies, which can itself terminate the app. I may not remember to open the app once I plug in my phone, and so the alarm can’t sound. It’s a bit of a disappointment knowing that Apple limits the app in this way.
That said, Alarmy still does its best to wake you up with constant push notifications, which I have set to vibrate my phone (which I keep on silent). And on the few occasions where this happened, I usually woke up enough to see the notification, and tap it (sometimes reluctantly) which allows the alarm to sound!

Even if you’re really, really hard to convince to wake up, Alarmy makes it hard to ignore. I once deleted the app because school was cancelled and I didn’t want to get up. Of course I had to redownload it later - because Alarmy does it’s job well.

I think I could’ve been fired for being late without Alarmy. And so for that reason alone I am happy to give it 5 stars and a thumbs up! 🥰
author: AustinS136

title: Forget you wanna snooze!
body:
Before Alarmy I’d usually wake up with an alarm and immediately begin to analyze the pros and cons of staying out of bed vs snoozing. Or I’d wake up pondering the dream I was pulled out of feeling like it’s only common courtesy to go back to sleep and finish the dream. Both ended up with me back in bed quicker than you can say breakfast and coffee! Then I’d go and hate myself for sleeping in which killed my mood and kept me in bed even longer. Vicious cycle. 

With Alarmy I have math problems as the first alarm and they’re just enough to engage my analytical brain and begin to actually wake up enough to kill the incredible pull of the bed in the morning without making me think f this math crap. Second alarm follows 5 minutes after which requires a picture of my bathroom to turn off giving me just enough time to put on my workout clothes, make my bed, drink some water, and head to the bath to wash up. Very effective overall!

I feel like the software processes could be simplified and I’ve had some weird glitches when my phone was on silent, but I’m no software engineer so maybe they’ve done everything possible with what Apple allows. Regardless, because of the consistent success I’ve had with Alarmy it’s definitely a 5/5 would recommend from me!

title: Great Free features, but not worth subscription
body:
I’ll split this into pros and cons, but ultimately, the companies greed guarantees I won’t be spending money on this product.

Pros:
-This app is ANNOYING in the best way that you can hope for in an alarm clock. It is ceaseless and efficient at getting a lazy sack like me out of bed.
-the ads on free aren’t horrible.
-it has a few good options for waking up. My favorite is math and the pattern, but the photo has been great for making sure I actually leave the bed.

CONS:
-This BIGGEST con of this app is the greed of the developer. The developer is charging a monthly fee to unlock the same features that have been in the app for months. If their ever changing missions, or other catered content that requires extra overhead would be unlocked permanently with that months subscription, then it would be worth it. But giving a rotating feature mission and removing ads for $3.50-$5 a month is just not worth it. I would much prefer a smaller ad removal purchase that’s one time, then each month an option to try the new missions with the option of buying. I would love to support the developer cause I use the app everyday, but I would want to get something permanent in return instead of just 1 month of features, then they go away.

TLDR- Not a fan of the subscription model, and it isn’t worth its cost compared to just using free features.

title: Only using this app to wake up ever!
body:
I never ever write reviews, so this shows how amazing this app is. I’m a lover for the snooze button and my apple alarms never wake me up like they used to. I’ve tried every trick in the book but to no avail. I randomly came across this app and was hesitant to try out the 7-day free trial, because it would imply I had to pay in the future should I go past the 7 days. However, best $5 ever spent. Since using it, I’ve been able to make every early morning meeting regardless of the time. 

I’m not a fan of the blaring alarm noises, so I love how the “morning” sounds are soothing enough to not put me in a panic but loud and consistent enough to wake me up and get me going. I love how you can customize each alarm to have easy or challenging missions, because—let’s face it—in the past, I’ve slept through alarms with the phone directly next to my ear so I need every complicated problem possible to even consider me waking up. 

I set my alarms to “no snooze” so I have to manually go into the app to dismiss the alarm (and it’s made me realize how instinctually I press the side buttons on my iPhone to mute). All-in-all, this is hands down the best alarm system I’ve used to wake me up successfully each morning without having a mini heart attack from blaring alarms.

title: Great alarm
body:
I’m a super heavy sleeper, and I almost always turn off alarms without even waking up; I love the morning (and get depressed if I wake up late), but my body sure doesn’t. I’ve even managed to do some of the easier puzzles and such without waking up enough to even try and keep myself awake (and if they’re too hard then I’ll just turn off the phone, also without waking up 😫). Setting multiple alarms usually means I I wake up to find I turned off the other alarms once the first goes off.

Alarmy’s wake up checks and QR code puzzle together with the wake up checks is the best thing I found to combat this. Putting a QR code in the opposite side of my apartment is enough that I’ll wake up like half way to do the puzzle, but not too much that I’ll just turn off the phone. The wake up check takes the place of setting multiple alarms, since I can’t just turn it off immediately or treat it like an alarm by itself (since usually if I have multiple alarms, and I’m lucky enough to wake up to one, it was the last alarm that really mattered). 

One alarm and a wake up check can almost always get me up!

title: Best app ever
body:
I have been using Alarmy for 60 days exactly as of 1;06am tonight, as I drink with friends I get a notification and now I’m here. It’s by far the best alarm app you can use, I will wake up tomorrow at 5:30 am regardless of the time, why? Because of each different task Alarmy gives you.

I will say that by far the picture one is the useful, you can customize it, for example I have a white board and I will take a picture of a designn and erase, so regardless of the day(5:30am) I have to wake up and sketch out the original design. Before you know it you are up. 

Another option is just taking a picture of a todo list, and I have used it when waking up, and take a copy of the task and read what I have for that day.

I will say that the math one is useful, but it’s easy enough to multiple it especially if you have any intentions of staying in bed. The memory one is great! But I have gotten to the point where I have a 7x7 and I can do it with one eye close. And then I end of passing back out especially if I only have x hours of sleep. If they expressed the difficulty or allowed you to customize the amount to a max of 10 or using 2 groups in swift and having it so it goes up to 20x20 that would be awesome, otherwise even with having 3 alarms back to back I end up turning then off.

The QR Code is brilliant, if you read books or want to read books, get a book holder custom QR code by just printing it on a small best of thick paper, and while you are reading in the morning, leave the book park where you left off and set the book in a spot outside the room in you sleep in; so when you wake up you go to that page and can read x pages (10-20) and then leave it back. It’s a great way to build successful habits, especially if you are a entrepreneur.

I haven’t used any other options other than those 4, but the photo or the QRCode one is by far the best, especially because you have to get out of bed.

Best of luck everyone and thanks Alarmy for this awesome app! 

From a fellow software engineer.

title: A Huge Quality of Life Improvement
body:
I don’t want to use cliches too often, but I sincerely mean it when I say that Alarmy had been life-changing for me. Alarms always used to be more like minor statistical improvements to waking up on time, which frequently made me late to things and more unreliable. The best way to be up on time was to go to bed early, but I often have problems getting to sleep at night, so that’s a toss-up too.
This alarm can force me to get up and move across the apartment to scan a barcode in my bathroom to turn it off, it never stops until I complete my task (and I can stop worrying about endlessly snoozing it), and the volume seems louder than other apps I’ve tried. 
Half-Awake Me is a selfish, self-destructive monster who can justify any amount of extra minutes sleeping, so it’s nice to find an app to take as much power away from her as possible. I recommend this to people all the time, and therapists I know have started recommending it to clients with sleeping issues. This has been a major part of improving my life lately, so thank you sincerely to the developers.

title: Good, but occasionally bad
body:
Overall, it’s a good app. It generally does what I want. When I used to have an Android phone, I had the best alarm app ever (I cant wake up was the name), which was the most customizable alarm app I had ever used and was truly inspirational. This doesn’t even come close to that app, but it still offers good features and I’ve used it for over a year now. 

What prompted me to give it two stars was that I picked up my phone at the end of work today after not touching it all afternoon and was surprised to see my battery at 16% even tho it was close to full this morning. My phone was noticeably warm even tho it had been sitting idle for the last few hours. I opened the settings app, went to the battery section, and saw that Alarmy had used 44% of my battery in background mode. This is rare, but it’s not the first time it’s happened. So here I am giving it a very mixed review. Really, all I want is an iPhone version of the app I used to use on my android phone.

title: USE CAUTION
body: Unquestionably, this app is aesthetically and functionally very well designed. However, the manner in which it manipulated the device volume is potentially very dangerous. It appears that just before the alarm is sounded, it programmatically maximizes the volume, which affects all running applications across all connections, including Bluetooth. Additionally, every alert (roughly one every five seconds) is handled by the app as a separate event, so even if you manage to reduce the volume quickly, it’s jacked right back up immediately. I often stream a popular music app over Bluetooth to my home theater sound system. When this alarm sounds, it cranks the volume, which in turn cranks my home theater volume to 100%. This once happened while I had run to the store and left my phone at home. I got back to a bunch of very angry neighbors that, as it turns out, are not fans of my music selection. Just use caution.

title: Saved attendance record
body:
I have a recurring issue of waking up to my alarm in such a haze that I reflexively turn it off without even comprehending it. I would frequently wake up hours past my alarm to find that it had mysteriously turned off. At first, I thought it was a bug, but I eventually figured out that I was shutting it off myself in the morning half-asleep. 

I tried everything from 20+ subsequent alarms to an alarm timed to your stages of sleep to an alarm that made you scan a barcode of something to silence it (in my case, the barcode of my coffee tin). None of them worked for more than a week before I had presumably figured out how to cheat them and would, once again, wake up to a turned-off alarm. 

This app has been the first one to consistently wake me up on time without me feeling groggy.

I use the math option, so I usually have to really get my brain going to silence the alarm (as a bonus, I get lots of practice with arithmetic which lord knows I could use considering the fact that I wrote 2x1=3 on a calculus exam). I especially like that you can opt to require solving a certain number in a row before it turns off. This makes sure that by the time I silence it, I’m fully alive, awake, alert and enthusiastic. The app also has the option to follow up with you after to make sure you’re really awake, erasing any doubt that I’ll ever shut off my alarm in my sleep again. 

My only request would be to amp up the math even more. If you were to add a scratchpad feature, you could add an option to make the problems algebraic equations. I mean while we’re at it, why not push the envelope even further and add derivatives and integration—I can promise you that will make sure that I’m up. 

In all seriousness, theres a lot of expansion that could be made with the concept of an alarm based on cognitive engagement. Check out how Quizlet is able to take manually entered information and generate quizzes, learning games, and flash cards. Having a user-generated quiz would be a great way to wake up, especially for students looking to get up for classes (I’m gonna go out on a limb here and say that a lot of the user-base is made up of students who oversleep)

Overall, the app is fantastic and adding even more cognitive skill based alarm features could be a great way to appeal to attendance-office frequent flyers like myself (before downloading this app, of course)

title: Perfect for INCREDIBLY deep sleepers
body:
I have been trying different features on this app for a couple of weeks and absolutely love it. I am someone who has difficulty getting out of bed and I generally will turn off alarms half asleep and have to panic-get-ready at the last second.

Having ADHD, autism, an undiagnosed physical disability, and insomnia, I have really struggled finding an alarm system that works for me.

I started off using the barcode feature by having to scan the shampoo in my bathroom so it would pressure me to wake up from the bright lights and the fact I was able to get up and out of bed. While this was often successful, I did end up falling back asleep quite a bit. The shaker is nice because I have some circulation issues and it helps me feel more alert to get my blood flowing but since it doesn’t force me out of bed I normally only use it in addition to other alarms.

The memory and math ones don’t help me too much because I can generally solve them while still very tired and go back to bed but I haven’t tried the higher difficulty settings which might be better.

My favorite however, and the only one which I suspect will have me awake every time is the photo feature, specifically because it is excruciatingly hard to line the photos up. And I mean this in a good way. I used a photo of the calendar in the hallway this morning and it helped me so much. Having to line up the dates, getting frustrated, I had to try it quite a few times to line up the angle right before I got it to shut off (it’s a relatively big calendar in a very narrow hallway so angles are key).

I have been using the sound Orkney specifically because I find it to be the most annoying which makes me happy. All of the iPhone alarm sounds are too standard and easy to listen to for me to wake up from them. I suspect I will probably have to switch alarm sounds over time (I get used to the sound and won’t wake up from it), but I love the sound options.

This app really was made with neurodivergent and insomniac people in mind. I am so glad an app like this exists. I may try premium at some point because I suspect options like the steps setting could be very useful for my specific difficulties. I also am very excited about the fact there is a power nap setting because I end up having to take these quite frequently. I haven’t used it yet but I can’t wait!

Thank you to the app developers and the team (I know this makes my review seem fake) but I genuinely am just amazed and really thankful for how this app is set up!

title: Game. Changer.
body:

As a math teacher, I can often do the math problems in my sleep (though I have seriously improved on my double digit multiplication), but having to take that picture forced me up. It drives me nuts but I’m not late because of my alarm clock anymore. 
I have been forced to delete a couple times because no matter how hard I tried to match the picture, the alarm would not turn off. Props to the app not having an “out” that I could learn in my sleep, but the only way I could go on with my day was to delete the app mid-alarm. Now, I always have to use pictures that are very easy to match, and after moving, I have been having difficulty finding a good spot. So, 4 stars only because I wish the app was slightly more lenient on those pictures because I do have trouble getting the phone in the exact position to match the original picture.

**edit: using the app for the first time since March (teacher during Covid lol) and noticing a barcode option which seems much more reliable than the photo!! Back to 5 stars!!!

title: Battery Usage Issues
body:
So first off, this app is fantastic from a purely functional perspective. If you absolutely need to wake up for something, this is going to be your best bet.

Seemingly randomly, some days this happens and others not, if the app is running in the background it will absolutely drain my phone battery. I have no way to predict when this will happen, so I automatically close the app after I wake up from the alarm. I have to remember I did so or the alarm won’t sound if the phone is in silent mode (the app warns you as such when you force close it).

Today, it used up 28% of my battery after the phone was unused and it was running in the background for 3 hours or so. Really weird stuff. And before you ask, yes I’ve uninstalled and reinstalled, and I’ve restarted my phone several times to see if that would prevent the issue. It seems to happen quite randomly despite my actions.

Like I said, otherwise this app is practically perfect. I would love to support it with the premium version if it didn’t have this battery issue.

body:
Look, I like my bed. I’m warm, my blankets are super soft, my pillow is a literal giant stuffed unicorn I got on Black Friday, and I’m usually coming out of a dream that leaves me desperate to return to that wonderful world. (My dreams don’t have Covid-19, okay?)
When I wake up, I never want to move. But I am also a responsible near-adult who has responsibilities. And I HATE it. When I just used my ordinary alarm app, I had fifteen alarms. All with snooze. But I just turned off each alarm as they rang and went back to sleep. I got a special vibrating disc to put under my pillow (before the unicorn) in hopes it would jolt me awake. The first morning I hurled it across my room and have yet to find it. It was like I was fighting a constant battle with my morning-self: constantly trying to find ways of luring her out of bed. 
Absolutely no self control or willpower to listen to all my alarms. Who cares if I’m late to school? Not morning-me. 
Then this app came along. Ooooh boy. Oh boy oh boy do I hate this app. Not only is the noise so deafening I woke up the first day thinking a friggin bomb alarm was going off, but the thing won’t shut up until I take a picture of my bathroom sink, then begin my day in the bathroom. I know I set these settings. I know. And boy do I hate myself for it. This app is so great that it drags a reluctant, sleep deprived teenager out of bed every morning when all I want to do is sleep the day away. I have three alarms everyday. The first is set for the picture. The second is math problems to make sure I’m actually starting my day and hadn’t just gone back to sleep. The third is just shaking it. 
However, the one, tiny, slight problem I have is that it can be deleted. Apparently morning-me figured out a way to shut the thing up without leaving bed: just delete it. Yep. This is my fifteenth time re-downloading the app. I just keep deleting it. 
But that’s more like a me problem, and it’s not like the app-creators can fix that, so I digress.
If you hate mornings with all the wrath of all nine levels of hell like me, then this is the app for you. You will hate it, but its mandatory. Ya know, if you don’t delete it every morning like I do.  
So download it. Do it. You know you have to.

Some of these option are mentally waking you up, like through math problems; and others are more physical, like asking you to shake the device. All of these are completely customizable as well! The most clever one though is the barcode feature. You take a photo of the barcode on an item in your house (i.e. chip bags, tooth paste, deodorant), and then place it far away from your bed. The next morning, in order to turn off the alarm, you must get up and go to the objet and scan it which forces you to move. Overall, awesome features and effective!

author: ur mom is trash

title: Actually fun!!
body:
Alarmy is so different from any other alarm wake up app I have ever used. I love that you have to take a picture of something. It really gets you up and moving and you have to match up angles sometimes. They also have math problems and other things to help your mind do an activity to wake up. I like a good adventure/activity, so finding the right angle and getting the picture fits both of those. (For some added adventure, move the object around so you have to “hunt” for it) 
My only complaint is that Alarmy won’t let you use any picture you want. The first time I used it I took a picture of a small lighthouse statue... the next morning when my alarm sounded I went over to go take the picture and it said, “no picture found” So I was stuck for several minutes with an alarm that wouldn’t go off. After some trial and error I found that you still can take pictures, but they almost have to have significant points or not too much going on. 
So I started using a bag of Folgers 1850 coffee as my picture, and that works great! (It’s good coffee too). Alarmy likes that it has numbers, isn’t too busy, and has a simple design. So saying all this... and to end my now Thesis Statement (sorry about it being so long) the only thing I would change is the ability to use almost any picture I take. This cuts down on being frustrated right out of bed that day because you can’t turn your alarm off for several minutes. Other than that, I highly recommend this app. It has truly helped me to ACTUALLY get up in the mornings!

body: I’ve been using Alarmy for over one-hundred days now and it has never failed to wake me up! I felt as if the least I could do is write an honest review. My favorite features would have to be the different creative missions you can complete in order to shut the alarm off, and the “Quick Alarm” which allows you to create a one time alarm ranging from one minute, to one hour (you can select multiple increments in order to set your ideal time), I use the Quick Alarm feature mainly for a laundry timer, but also for the occasional thirty-minute nap! body:
Overall, the app is good for using as a general alarm but I don’t recommend using the photo option. I’m not sure if this was something purposely implemented by the creators, but whenever I take a picture and it doesn’t match up completely, the camera would sometimes flip around and make it incredibly difficult to take the picture. At other times, the picture is (istg) exactly the same as the previous but it wouldn’t go through. My alarm kept notifying me for about an hour while I was doing other things and I had to reinstall the app to turn it off. Again, I’m not sure if the creators did his to intensify the difficulty, but when it’s early in the morning, I don’t want to spend my first five minutes trying to take the picture.

OTHERWISE, this app isn’t bad for its other features. I really like having the weather right when I wake up and the features for maths and memorization DO work (personally, only if the difficulty is higher). So overall, a pretty effective system; maybe just a few changes here and there.

author: PerrieRocky

title: Woke up and stayed up
body:
This is truly a powerful alarm. For the first time ever this morning, I woke up when I planned to wake up and I didn’t even press snooze once. 
I’ve become a pro at the snooze button. I own THREE alarm clocks, all placed in different locations in my bedroom, plus the six iPhone alarms I used to set every morning. I am NOT a morning person. It’s bad to the point that I can hit snooze on all those alarms in a sleepwalking state and wake up hours later, late and unable to recall how I managed to walk around the room while still asleep and turn off the alarms.
I actually stumbled on this app looking for an app that would sound off my favorite songs in the morning so that I wouldn’t be so quick to hit snooze on my favorite artists, but I downloaded this as my backup. Lo-and-behold, I slept through all six music alarms this morning and the only one that actually worked was the single, annoyingly persistent math alarm set by Alarmy. The noise itself made me jump awake thinking my work was trying to video chat me (exact same ringtone—weird but effective), but what kept me awake was the replacement of a snooze button with math problems. Can a groggy me add large sums first thing in the morning as easily as I can sleepwalk to turn off my alarms? No, definitely not, it took me at least 5 minutes of nonstop alarm to crack it. But the reward of Alarmy telling me good morning and giving me weather reports and the news was well worth it—it’s actually the first time ever that I’ve had enough time in the morning to sit with my coffee and read the news. This app is the secret to mornings.

Update: Weirdly, with time, the Math alarms stopped being effective. I got so good at doing math in a half asleep state that I would fall right back asleep, or I’d get so annoyed with the mental math that I’d delete the app—but with my sleep history that’s probably to be expected.
I sprung for the membership so that I could use the walking alarm. I don’t regret it—you really cannot cheat that alarm, it knows what a person walking with their phone in hand should feel like. The only issue is that the alarm is still sounding while I walk the 30 steps around my apartment, so I have to use it sparingly so that I don’t wake my room mates. On the other hand, the typing alarm is wonderful. Successfully annoying, and it helps me get excited for the day with the motivational phrases it makes me write.

For any other heavy sleepers out there—if you use this alarm, make sure to change it up every now and then, or you *will* get used to it and ignore it. Changing the challenges up every other day helps. There is also a random setting for the alarm noise that will wake you with a new sound or melody every morning. Just be aware that one of the sounds is a rooster. A very loud rooster who will definitely startle and confuse your room mates when it goes off.

I found this app, and use the Math option for every alarm. And it works. The thing won't turn off until I figure out the 3 problems. More often than not, I doze back off when I'm solving them, and it beeps back at me again. Granted, that makes me so mad (when it resets), but then I am actually awake and get up for the day. 

All in all. Been using this for over a year. Amazing app. I appreciate that it is free to use, simple, and effective.

title: An Alarm that Hasn’t Failed Me
body:
I have a shifted sleep schedule, am very stubborn and so have difficulties waking up at a reasonable hour. It’s at the point that I’m able to get out of bed to silence a hidden alarm and go back to sleep. 
This is the first alarm I’ve had that I haven’t been able to silence in my sleep or just sleep through. It’s reliable, easy to use and offers plenty of customization even with the free version. I would not recommend this for people that wake up to a regular alarm because the point of this is to frustrate you into getting up, but it’s PERFECT for people like me that struggle. 
My only complaint is that the Math option is pretty unfeasible at the higher difficulties - multiplying two four digit numbers mentally and in the span of 30 seconds is a bit much to ask when I’m not half asleep. Even so, that’s a great choice for VERY stubborn sleepers like myself. It’s the perfect fallback as long as you’re ok cursing at an angry alarm. Just be sure to increase the time to solve before it resets. 
I would also advise against using vibration or a peaceful alarm that wouldn’t scare you awake. The alarm is VERY insistent and if it’s not something that would immediately jolt me awake, I’ve noticed it working into my dreams and making some pretty awful nightmares.

title: The best you could possibly want
body:

From shaking the phone to answering a math problem to turn off your alarm, this app has all the choices you’ll need to ensure you wake up. 

The best part? There’s so much customization available. You can set your alarms once and be set for the year. Want to set alarms for weekdays? You can do it. Want different times for each day? You can do it. Want some alarms to give you challenges to silence them while others you just tap your screen? You can do it.

This is the best alarm app I’ve found. Used it for several years now and I don’t plan on stopping!

title: AMAZING
body: I started using this app because I was having a really difficult time waking up once I started taking my prescription sleeping pills at night. I was late to work and missing class and nothing I did seem to work. I tried putting my alarm clock on the other side of the room, I tried leaving my curtains open for the sun, nothing did the trick. This alarm is the most amazing thing- nothing, absolutely nothing, can beat it in terms of functionality. There is no way not to wake up when you set this alarm. I use the math function and, when I want a less alarming wake up, the shake function and they have never failed me. I’ve been using it for almost 2 years now and, unlike most other alarms, I have not gotten used to this one. I love it because there is absolutely no way to turn off the alarm except to follow its instructions. You can’t close out of the app, you can’t turn your phone volume down. If it wants you to wake up, you will wake up. I’m so glad I tried this app before I did something more extreme, like getting one of those alarms that shakes the bed and sounds like a fire alarm. If you’re looking for a sign, let this be it: this thing works.

title: An absolute LIFE SAVER
body:
I downloaded this app as a last stitch effort to getting up in the morning. I am an incredibly heavy sleeper, and my only priority when first waking up is going back to sleep. I can snooze a regular alarm 15 times without even knowing it. I’ve actually done that. 

This alarm app stands out because of all the different features, which you can tweak until it’s perfect for you. 

Personally, I use alarm sounds from the loudest pack. I have them set to get louder as time goes on. My snoozes are 5 minutes long and I get 2 of them. At one point, I had begun to do the math problems in my sleep (lol), bit was able to increase the difficulty so I had no choice. You can also adjust the power of the vibrate option. 

One fallback though is that if the app is not running in the background (aka if it is closed/ X’ed out) the alarm has no sound, just vibrates. Running the app in the background requires a good amount of data/ battery life.  The times i forgot to open it before I slept, I usually slept through the faint vibration.

title: Broke this chronic snoozer!
body:
This is the only alarm I’ve ever had that has worked for me. I was recommended it by a friend and I can’t thank them enough. I am a chronic hitter of the snooze button and I used to have to set at least 6 alarms per sleep. I would snooze ALL of them and take around an hour to wake up. I haven’t looked back since getting this app. 

I use the 3 math problems setting on hard difficulty I think (whatever starts to use parentheses) and it makes me use my brain hard enough that it just gets me up every time. Also, with the added panic of the timer, I know that I absolutely can’t close my eyes or the loud sounds will start again. Genius. Also, once I “win” and get all the math problems right, I love that my short little horoscope pops up so that my interest is piqued and attention is kept long enough that I start having some coherent thoughts and get up! 

I have not overslept in the last two years because of this app. The only time I have is because I either forgot about an appointment or never set the alarm in the first place, never because it wasn’t able to wake me. THANK YOU, ALARMY!

One of the best parts about the alarm functions is there are multiple different settings to ensure the difficulty level is the right one for you. The app also houses a wide variety of sounds including typical alarm ones and even ones I would never think of. I always use the music selection one, but the options are nice. The difference I’ve seen between this app’s alarm clocks and any other is the choice to solve a puzzle, take a picture, or do some other task to stop the alarm from going off. It’s simply helpful because the alarm won’t stop sounding unless the given task is completed. This stops me from turning off the alarm and just going to bed immediately after. 

This app also has many different sounding alarms. My favorite one overall is the Loud Alarm 7. As the name suggests, it’s very loud and has never failed to wake me up. 

This app has many different features and is good for deep sleepers, I’d definitely recommend this to anyone who is a deep sleeper like myself.

title: Annoyingly Effective! It works!
body:
I am terrible morning person and often sleep through multiple alarms. This alarm app gets me up! I use two timers on this app and still use two others as backup, but this is my primary. 

I use the math equation option. I keep it simple enough to do quickly but steps up from 2+2. One alarm is set on the rooster sound to get me moving. The next is a very loud warning sound for which I must do the math the shut off. 

One thing that is sort of annoying is that there’s not always a pop up notification to access the app to do said equation. I wind up scrolling through the phone for the app. Even upon opening it, I just sort of stab at it until it give me the numbers. It’s really frustrating but maybe that’s the point and why it wakes me.  The only reason it lost a star is because they place an ad smack in the middle of the screen which is unpleasant to look at, easier to hit by mistake when setting alarms or when stabbing at the app, as previously mentioned, you can’t help but hit it. Ads (on the edges or pop up) are annoying as it is but I find the placement of their add takes that last star off.

author: Sophiuhm

title: COLLEGE STUDENT NECESSITY
body:
I’ve struggled with diagnosed narcolepsy since I was a little kid, and I’ve never been able to wake myself up on my own, because I always simply wake up, turn the alarm off, and immediately go back to sleep. 

I discovered Alarmy my first semester of freshman year in college, desperate to find something that would help me get to classes without sleeping through them. I had downloaded and tried every single alarm app you could possibly imagine. Alarmy was the best one I found. It was a lifesaver, and honestly I don’t know if I would’ve succeeded through college without this app. 

I’m a big fan of the math section- I think it’s great for me to be awake-awake and I really love that I can make several alarms with different actions in case one doesn’t work the first time. Although Alarmy isn’t the only app with that feature, it’s the only one that’s as easy to use and effective that I have found. 

While there’s no better option than this one, I think that it would be really great if they extended their actions (shake, math, etc.) to the timer part too, because I have the same problem with naps, and it would be a great help to keep me from sleeping over. 

Other than that, this app is perfect for me and anyone struggling with sleep (whether it be oversleeping or not enough sleep) as well as college students.

title: Where Have You Been All My Life?
body:
Morning is easily the most dangerous part of my day. Specifically, those first waking moments when most people get out of bed, put on some slippers, and hop to the kitchen for coffee. How lovely. Not me. While most people are buttering their toast, I am busy sabotaging my life in bed. I can have alarms blasting away on my watch, on my phone, on my nightstand, AND in the bathroom and still manage to turn them all off and wind up back on my pillow. I would say it’s almost like sleepwalking, but I don’t actually know what sleepwalking is like. A doctor once told me it had to do with my ADHD. Whatever the *bleep* it has to do with, wake-up time has been the bane of my existence from 4th grade straight through my 40s.

Then I found Alarmy. Now I am CEO of a Fortune 500 corporation with a golf handicap of 3. Or, not quite that, but I am definitely a happier person who is now infinitely less likely to wreck my day before it even begins. By setting up a cognitively or physically challenging task which must be completed promptly in order to silence the alarm, I am able to put a lot more distance between myself and Sleepytown. Alarmy then checks to make sure I have followed through and that I am still awake after a set number of minutes. Sure, there are times when I get angry at Alarmy for being so disruptive and relentless. But this is just another way of saying that Alarmy is totally great at what it does. I forgive it. I love it. I need it. Thank you, Alarmy! You have quickly become one of my very best friends👍🏻!

title: Force close
body:
I really don’t like to complain especially about technology. I know how it is. My husband and I have had this app for about a year now and still have the same issue. Yes it wakes me up and I love it for that. However, it says if you force close the app, the alarms will not go off. So if you have your alarms set every day because your off days are always different. You should just be able to force close the app the night before, so the alarms won’t go off that next morning, no biggie, right? Wrong. As long as the alarms are turned on, they go off. Whether the app is force closed or not. This becomes soooo aggravating, especially after a year of this stupid crap. 
So basically, you have to remember to turn the alarms off on your days off and turn them on, on days you work. Which is ridiculous when I should be able to always have them on, and force close the app when I don’t want to use them. It’s not like I’m asking something, that you all can’t do. It’s already suppose to be able to do this. I’m not asking you to read my mind and know what days I’m off. 
Fix your software!!!! It’s so frustrating!!!

title: Love the vibrate to sound options
body: I tried this app to stop waking up a housemate with my previous alarms; I wake up at 3:00am and everything is very quiet so I needed something that was strong enough to wake me but not strong enough to wake people around me in the same room.  I only get between 4-5 hours sleep so my alarm is what makes or breaks the start of my day being on time. I needed something with heavy vibration and a softer sound that ascends slowly, this app has that!!!!!  I think it it’s a great app and has various combos and sounds you can use. I found some that are positive, feel-good musics and ascend slowly yet have major vibrations from the start. I don’t use the mental stimulations because once it goes off I’m typically quick to rise. On the contrary I do wish I could turn it off easier.  I believe that’s a main point of this app, to not be able to just hit snooze, but there are some moments I would like to just lay there and easily in the dark hit “no sound” or “off” quickly; I only have that short bit of ascension before the sound grows to where my roommates are waken. Still this is an amazing app! Gem of a find!

title: The only thing that has worked!
body:

I don’t sleep the best so I need a good routine and sleeping in always ruins any progress I have made, but even if I put my phone on my dresser and make myself get out of bed, I immediately just go back. The picture feature has been a game changer.

All the other options would have either frustrated me and gave me anxiety (like math lol) or just kept me in bed where I would lay back down. Sometimes even if I’m up I’ll just lay there forever on my phone poking around and I want to stop that habit.

Anyways, I set the picture as my bathroom sink, and to my joy and sleepy dismay, it works! I changed the settings to give me the most time to get up because I’m fighting with my brain. But it’s the 5th day and I’ve gotten out of bed and stayed up each time! I’m so happy!

title: What the heck?!
body: This app is literally magic. I’m not gonna lie, I was very skeptical of this app even with all the great reviews I had read. It’s now 8am and even though I went to sleep at 3am (that’s never gonna change) I am awake and don’t feel crappy the way I usually do when I wake up so early. I used the barcode scanner and scanned a book on the other side of my room that was under a large stack of books. I also experimented with the app a bit and tried to swipe out of it completely. The alarm kept going! I honestly think the only way to turn the alarm off would be to shut my phone down but since I don’t see myself doing that, I think this app is finally the alarm that will work for me. My sleep schedule is still horrendous but at least I know I can actually wake up before 9am without feeling awful. Thank you Alarmy!

title: Outstanding alarm app for a heavy sleeper -- with lots of options!
body:

I can choose to have my alarm be loud and persistent until I complete a task (lately it's been lengthy math problems so I have to get out of bed and use my calculator). 

This has been an excellent tool, and since downloading it, I have used it every single night. The user interface is very intuitive, and the built-in content has plenty of options and variety. I also love the positive messages displayed after I a set an alarm and minimize the app.

Very great service. A must-have for heavy sleepers who just won't wake up to regular alarms (or for those who need a bit more motivation to wake up in the morning).

title: MORE THAN AN ALARM
body:
Honestly you already know how great of an alarm is from reading all the other reviews ... but it’s SO MUCH MORE THAN THAT because of all the options it offers!

I’ve been using this to wake up - severe insomnia + a demanding job means I’m always working and always sleep deprived. This gets me up no matter WHAT. But look at all the other things it does ... 

PILL REMINDER: I’ve been using this as a reminders app. I take vitamins in the morning and meds at night and I’m very inconsistent with them. By setting an alarm that makes me take a barcode of the pill bottles, I’ve been consistently taking my meds for months now! 

EXERCISE MOTIVATOR: I took a photo of a sign at my local park and set an alarm that requires a photo of this sign to turn it off. Along with that I set a once hourly alarm to take 100 steps and am walking a ton more. I’ve been getting so much more fresh air and exercise! 

GUITAR PRACTICE: I use the photo function again to take a photo of my guitar practice setup and have been able to more consistently practice! 

SKINCARE: Been getting really into skincare recently ... I set an alarm to scan the barcode of my face wash and because I’ve been so consistent with it, my skin is literally glowing ...

I’m naturally a hot mess but I’m becoming a healthier person thanks to this app. From the bottom of my heart thank you for changing my life with a simple alarm!

title: Amazing!! But picture mode is terrible
body: I loved this alarm ! Stuff like the remembering game and the math equations were amazing ways to wake me up and it should be able to wake everyone up in the morning no doubt. It would always be the only alarm to wake me up, however my issue began to be staying up, as I found that afterwards I began to just get sleepy again and fall back asleep. I found that forcing me to get up and stand was the best way to keep me awake. So I decided to use the picture mode for my alarm. Suddenly, everything went downhill. Even after changing the settings (extending the time, making sure the quality of the retake was low), retaking the picture was always way too hard, and I’d be there for 20 minutes trying to turn the alarm off.  I’ve had to delete and re-download the app multiple times to shut it off now, and now that I’ve done that the alarm has suddenly become far too low and quiet to even wake me up, even at max volume and everything. This alarm is the only I know of that can wake me up, and I’ll be sure to keep at it and try to fix it, but a future reminder to future users: the picture mode is hard to work with, and may become more of a strain on your day then a help.

title: Works through three neuro meds!
body:
My sleeping patterns have gone rogue from
My body’s preferred cycle to twelve hours of deep sleep due to my medication adjustment. This was causing severe migraines that weren’t responding to my normal medication and a general screw up to my day. So I downloaded Alarmy.

Perfect. When Alarmy wakes me, I choose to perform the pattern recognization and it forces my brain to stay alert. I’m awake. I’m actually awake and staying awake instead of disabling my regular alarm in the middle of the night!

If it wasn’t for Alarmy I was going to start, no kidding, playing the sounds of babies crying because that’s the only thing that can wake me otherwise! Just a simple “memorize these patterns” and flipping them can motivate me to wake up easier. I’m a little slow due to the neurological problems so I’m not being assaulted with the alarm as I’m trying to flip the boxes over, so I’m very happy about that design. It’s very forgiving for tricky fingers. 

A much easier start to my day and keeps me on my medication schedule better. A life saver. Thank you for creating this app.

title: The Best Alarm Ever!
body: I’m so happy I found this app! I’m not a morning person and I always hit the snooze button. I realized that I needed to make some changes first starting with getting up earlier to be able to complete tasks before the kids wake up. I tried this before but it never stuck since I loved hitting the snooze button. I found Alarmy and it changed my life. I started with the memory game just because I struggle with remembering things at times so I thought that would be helpful for me. When I tell you, no matter what time I went to sleep, once Alarmy went off and I completed my memory mission, I was wide awake and ready to start my day. I felt good about myself and started seeing a difference in my life in general. I make sure I go to be at a decent hour because I can now count on Alarmy to wake me and my brain up. I now use the math mission and it works just as well. I also set it up on my 1st grade son’s tablet because he struggles with math at times. He loves it! I let him pick the tone and I hear when he wakes up counting aloud and actually completing the problems. He even asked if I could make the problems a little more difficult! Sorry for the long review but I love this app and not just for the alarm but also the sleep music option. I used to use you tube for sleep meditation music but now I don’t have to. The creator of this app is a genius. Thanks so much!

title: I love it, only one problem
body:
I’ve used this app for quite a long time now and I would love to continue using it. It’s just become... frustrating.
I’m a heavy sleeper but this app had sounds and alarms that could wake me up in an instant, now no matter what I do either in the app or my phone settings all I get is a vibration. Kinda hard to wake up to that when I can’t even wake up to dubstep. Like I said I’ve used this app for a long time. Long enough they’ve given me free lifetime premium. These problems only started happening when I got my iPhone X. And for some reason it only makes sound if I look at it then quickly shut it off and close the app then reopen it and put the phone to sleep. Kinda defeats the purpose of the alarm if you can only hear it when you preform an exorcism on it. Don’t take this review with the idea that this app won’t work for you. I’m only writing this out to try to find some help(google returns nothing). This app works. title: Life-changing
body:
I don’t typically write reviews, but I had to for this app. All my life I’ve had an incredibly difficult time waking up in the morning. I would unconsciously shut off all of my alarms and would have full conversations with people and not even be awake enough to realize I was doing it. It got to a point where I was contemplating whether or not to go to a sleep doctor to figure out if there was some sort of medical reason that I was having so much difficulty waking up in the mornings. I started using this app as a last result and have found incredible success. Since using this app, I’ve been able to create a sleep schedule (which has been nearly impossible for years), and wake up feeling rested for the first time in a long while. I love that there are so many features to use so that you can truly find whatever works best for you. My personal favorite it the picture function. It requires me to get up and moving and to focus to make sure the picture is just right.

I’ve already been recommending this app to friends and family :)

I would absolutely recommend!!

title: Good variety of tasks, but unreliable (UPDATED)
body:
I’m so upset right now. This app has normally done a good job of giving me tasks that get me out of bed, despite it being a bit of an ordeal to even open the app. I have to go to the app via my notifications as it doesn’t open in the forefront (?) as most alarm apps do. (I don’t know technological lingo, I apologize.)  

If I try to close the app in the background, Alarmy gives a message that it needs to be running in the background to work on silent mode. Annoying, but I deal. Yet today with my phone on silent mode and Alarmy in the background, it did not go off. I have to be at work by 6:30, 6:45 at the latest. I woke up at 6:55. I saw notifications that it had been going off, but I heard nothing. The sound should be getting progressively louder as I have set it to do.

Giving it 3 stars as the tasks are pretty good and this is the first time anything like this has happened in the 6 months I’ve had the app, but it should never happen. 

I also set a mellow, positive song to wake me up a little later on the weekends. It plays a loud annoying sound and doesn’t play the song I chose until I pick it up and do the memory game to turn off the app.

////UPDATE////

The alarm now sounds in silent mode with it running in the background. Not sure about my weekend song as I have turned it off. I will update again after testing. Still docking a star because it’s hard to get into the app as it’s going off. It should really pop forward as most alarms do.

title: No More Snooze
body:
My entire adult life I have been a chronic snoozer. I was snoozing for about 20-40 minutes each day. I got Alarmy as a last ditched effort to save my morning routine. I started off with the “Take a Picture” mission and it’s okay, but way too sensitive and a little buggy. I switched over to the barcode/QR scanner and it’s amazing. It recognizes the QR code I put on my bathroom mirror immediately, without fail. Since I started using this alarm mission a month ago I have not snoozed once. My mornings are infinitely less stressful. I am able to wake up earlier while simultaneously feeling less tired, thanks to Alarmy. 

Shout out: Magic Light Bulbs

Suggestions: 

- Location tracking to distinguish different alarms if you sleep at different locations.

- “Take a Picture” mission is way too sensitive even on the lowest setting.

title: This alarm wakes me up better than an earthquake
body:
10/10 I definitely recommend this app. I use a custom MP3 of my favorite vine and the math mission setting.

A little backstory, I’ve never been able to get up in the mornings. I’m always such a deep sleeper that my parents eventually started using water and my brain got used to that and I would roll over and go back to sleep without even remembering it.

My mom eventually bought me the Sonic Boom alarm clock when I was 16 which shakes the bed and makes a horrendously loud noise, so loud it would wake my parents up on the main floor before me in the basement. I had that for years and it did diddly.

Now I’ve had this app pretty much since Google Play Pass launched on the Google Play Store and this app was on there. I thought ‘why not’ and it has changed my life. 

I wake up every morning around 10-11 and have only overslept this alarm a couple of times. I always curse it out in the mornings sure, but who wouldn’t with 6 math problems and dyscalculia 😂

TLDR- If nothing has worked for you, try this.

title: Genius Idea/Why don’t all alarms have this?!
body:
I am a student with morning classes and A morning job. I have always had trouble getting up in the morning because I am a deep sleeper, and I both sleep walk and talk so whoever is waking me up doesn’t know if I am actually awake or not. I have tried everything, and alarmy is the thing that helped me most.

I sleep through the majority of alarms because they are simply not loud enough or shut off after only a few rings. That is why alarmy is genius because it allows you to alter the way you want to be woken up, and gives you multiple different tasks to chose from. This allows you to not only hear the alarm (unlike most clocks) but also have multiple different tasks to make sure you are truly awake. And if you get used to one task and stop needing to be fully awake to do it (like I do), you can change it or do a task like math.

Alarmy has helped me to finally be able to function in the morning, and helped me keep my job! :). I wish all alarms worked this way, it seems so obvious and that is why it’s genius. So thank you to the developers at alarmy! Hope I see more genius products like this soon.

title: Pretty good alarm!
body:
I have struggled to wake up FOREVER. When the time came when I headed off to college, my parents were worried I’d oversleep all my classes. So, I tried searching for alarm apps that would hopefully help me wake up in the morning.

This one has proved the most successful. I usually use math problems to wake me up before setting a second alarm about 15 minutes later just to make sure I woke up. It’s worked about 95% of the time, which is really good for me! I like the variance of options for sounds and extra settings.

The only complaint I have is that the photo option is a bit frustrating. I tried it out once by taking a picture of a sign hanging in my dormitory lounge. The next morning, I went and took a picture of it but the app told me it wasn’t accurate and just kept on ringing. This went on for about fifteen minutes until finally I decided to just delete and reinstall the app. Probably not going to use that function again, lol! I’ll just stick to my math and memory game.

Thanks for the cool app! Would (mostly) recommend to heavy sleepers!

title: Best Alarm Ever
body:
I am AWFUL at waking up. I’ll set 4 alarms a few minutes apart and will shut some off, then snooze the rest for over an hour. This alarm is a total game changer for me. I typically set 3 different types about 10 minutes apart. 

The first is the math, followed by shake, ending with the barcode scan of my face-wash in the bathroom! The last one forces me to get out of bed which is necessary. 

The one thing that I wish was different is to have the sound not stop until AFTER the task is completed. I, in my drool-induced haze, have figured out if I keep pressing ‘scan’ or enter random numbers, the alarm will pause for some time. Even if it’s a few seconds, I’ll do it for a while if I’m tired enough. 🥴 

All in all- I LOVE THIS APP. Download it NOW if you’re always late/a heavy sleeper/super lazy & never want go get out of bed.

title: I finally get up to my alarm
body:

App. I made the mistake of not taking off the snooze button the first time but now I took that option away and I literally can’t turn my alarm off without getting out of bed. This week I’ve been awake on time and having coffee and not rushing. It’s taken so much stress out of my days. 

The app also isn’t bogged down with ads and has a beautiful design. I like all the options for waking up but I use the barcode scanner to scan something in my bathroom each morning. 

The only “flaw” that occurred was if you have do not disturb on, the app can’t override that and won’t go off. I didn’t think about how the iPhone bedtime alarm has that feature so it didn’t work that day. Not the apps fault but something to be aware of. 

Thanks Alarmy! 😴

 The only problem I have with the app is that when your phone  goes off, you have to try to unlock your phone, find the app and then dismiss the alarm before you can turn it off. This is not good at all for someone trying to use it with others in the house or especially in the same room. It also is not very nice for a sleeping person to be fully awake and have a blaring alarm in their face when they are trying to get it turned off. 

One tip I also have for people is that they they want more then one mission, they can set more then one alarm a minute or two apart with a different mission

It’s worked fine. But it’s still running nonstop in the background. 

My battery report shows in the last 24 hours, Alarmy has accounted for 14% of my battery use with only 2 minutes active and nearly 16 hours running in the background.

title: Great, but could be better Suggestions incl.
body:
This app is packed with simple but easy to use features.

The pros:
- There's a neat feature
that shows how much time till the next alarm rings

- There's widget support to set a quick alarm right from the Notification Center(for situations like cooking something for a few min. (I think the time limit is more than a few min))

- AccuWeather is included- when you dismiss the alarm you can choose to see the weather for the day

- There are background noises such as a coffee shop, rain, beta soundwave, etc, and these can be played for a specific amount of time, I think

- If you keep the app running in the background, you can have your device set to one volume, and the alarm will still reach its max (at least it seems so)

- You can have backgrounds in the app

- Really simple and intuitive

- Can name each alarm, and the name shows up in the alarm notification

- Differnt options to dismiss the alarm, such as doing a math problem or a few. Along with this there's a preview mode that allows you to test the alarm volume and "mission" (the way to dismiss the alarm)

- Ads make the app free, and they don't seem to make the app bugy/ laggy

Cons/ Suggestions:

- App is currently more than 200 mb in size (not too bad, but is a little space consumptive for an alarm app)

- Sometimes it's easy to forget to keep the app running in the background, and if your device volume isn't high enough, you may not hear the alarm (I think the OS limits it so that the app has to work this way, and it can be annoying.)

- Once the app rings, you have to open the actual app to dismiss the alarm, and if your device is locked, the time while you're unlocking, it will keep ringing (unlike an alarm by the default iOS clock app which you can dismiss right from the lockscreen. More time to wake up though.)

- If your device is locked, the way the alarm notifies you is through notifications,  each new ring: a new notification (if it rings 20 times you got 20 notifications), but once you unlock they go away like regular notifications (just kind of annoying and probably coukd be improved)

- If the app has to be open in the background, it'd be nice if there was a feature that made it so the screen would fully turn off, similar to the device locking, and when the alarm rings you just tap the screen to turn the screen on. This could provide easier access to dismiss the alarm while also not having to keep the device unlocked and the screen on.

- Alarm will ring until your device runs out of battery, probably unless charging. Then if your device literally powers off, and you turn it back on all the notifications kind of lag the device, but not too much.

title: Alarm app that actually works
body:
I don’t really write a review for an app, but this app is just amazing. 
At first, I set up the mission to shake the phone100 times and then to take a picture of something in the room 10 minutes later (because I knew I would not leave the bed after the shaking), but I ended up going back to bed after those missions. 
If you’re like me, I highly recommend to take a picture/scan whatever is in the bathroom, forcing yourself to take a shower. when your hair is wet, you wouldn’t want to go back to bed, and your mind becomes more clear after taking shower. 
It’s amazing how taking actual action makes everything easier than lying on a bed thinking about doing it dreadfully. You don’t have to be a morning person, but hitting snooze and waking up late despite of all the motivation I had at night was kind of unhealthy for me. it’s like a little failure that eats you up slowly because you’re basically starting your day with a small failure. I used to wake up and would think, “eh, i’m like that. I didn’t believe I would succeed anyway,” and all the planning for the day would go to trash. This app not only helped me to wake up on time, but made me think that even I could succeed at something small - and it becomes a momentum to do something I planned to do.

title: Good app but WAAAAAY overpriced.
body:
I had thought about writing an app that did exactly what this app does. Force heavy snooze button user to wake up by having them perform physical tasks, like math, walking a set number of steps or taking photos in another room in the house. Since I figured I couldn’t be the first person to think of this I searched the App Store and found that there is at least this one (and probably more). The app, so far, is good. It does all that I would have wanted my app to do, and more. The only negative of the application is that for full functionality it needs to be running in the background. However that is an iOS limitation and not a flaw in their work. 

But at $4.99 a month or $139 lifetime purchase price it is ridiculous. Highly engineered gaming software with multi-million dollar production budgets often cost $59 for new releases and quickly go into the bargain bin for $29.  This is a product that could be written in a number of weeks, tops with a software engineer or two. While I am happy to pay for products I will be a free user under this business/pricing model.

title: Perfect for the “morning challenged”!
body:
I am a night person who lives in a morning-person world. I often shut off standard alarms without even realizing it. Theses developers have thought of everything, there are so my options, anyone can find an alarm that works, and works well!

Alarmy has so many unique options - tones, songs, annoying sounds - but it’s the “get the alarm to stop going off” options that are amazing. Right now I am using the math option (which has easy to difficult ranges) and I’m actually discovering my “in your head” math skills are significantly improving!

Alarm choices: Vibrations, tones, songs, increasing loudness - the alarm options have something for everyone, (including the Deaf and Hard of Hearing, which I love)! 

But WAKING you is only one part of the puzzle. People like me, who fight against their natural sleep cycle — we need to STAY awake. And that’s where this app STANDS OUT. 

Shut off choices: Math problems of varying degrees (easy to difficult) and varying in how many I am required to do!

In lieu of math, I can choose a barcode in my house that I have to get up and go scan!  This app has thought of everything. I LOVE IT. 

And my family is happy because they don’t have to hear me “snooze” an old fashioned alarm for an hour (all in my sleep, mind you)!  They are even pleased by my sound choices and knowing the FIRST TIME it goes off that “mom’s awake now.”

LIFE CHANGING.

title: There’s some other way to turn it off
body:
My super power is learning to disable alarms without waking up. Normally it takes me a few months, but I’ve always found a way. I tried this app for the first time (or maybe the first time in several years, I didn’t think I’d had it before) and I set a ton of alarms. Some with the math mission, some with the memory mission, and one with the barcode mission for my toothpaste in the other room. I think I set 7 alarms, all with different sounds too. And it didn’t wake me up. While I could maybe see myself being able to do the math and memory, there’s no way I got out of bed and scanned my toothpaste in my sleep. 

I’m not sure what it is, but there’s some sort of loophole to turning it off. My phone was still on so it wasn’t that. I think maybe if you double press home and close it that way it’ll turn it off? It’s just a guess. I have no idea how I did it. But there’s another way and I missed my shift. 

2 stars because the concept of the app is great, but please fix whatever back door sleeping me found

title: Rocks!! By far the best if you’re a hard sleeper
body: I connect this through my sound bar via Bluetooth, and put my iPhone in “do not disturb” mode, make sure the Alarmy notifications are set to “persistent” and also set to “by app”, then I make sure (after I’ve set the alarm time) to go to the settings icon in upper right corner of the app...which is on the screen you see “after” you set your alarm and push “done”....to vibrate off (because I use a wireless charging pad but a power cord works just as good) and then you must make sure that you disable the “disable in dismiss mode” (otherwise it won’t go off if you have “do not disturb” turned on. Then I lock it, set my sound bar volume super high (depending on when I have to get up and how tired I think I’ll be) “so pretty loud usually” and set my iPhone 8 on the charging pad and I can sleep almost anywhere through most noises if I’m tired enough, but set it on the loud ringer 1 alarm sound setting and....it wakes me up no matter what condition I feel asleep in. Lol. I’ve tried probably 8 other alarm apps and now I seriously “only use Alarmy” (this app).  You can set it to wake up to pleasant sounds if you’re a light sleeper...or the loudest most annoying sounds or music that when it goes off...(if you’re sleeping nicely) it’s upsetting to say the least lol but if you “have to get up” for whatever whenever and can’t chance not hearing your normal alarm...put this (if it’s connected to blue tooth speakers)....far enough away that you have to get out of bed to turn it off. It even has a setting I enable that fires up the alarm 10 mins after I’ve disabled it...just in case I accidentally lay back down on my bed and accidentally fall asleep again. Whoever designed this app is a awesome! Thank you to whoever designed and built this app.  Saves me every time. 👍🙌😎

author: MrsT1998

title: Heavy sleepers life saver!
body:
I could sleep through an earthquake. Literally, I have slept through a magnitude 3 earthquake...😳 So, as you can imagine I’ve had some serious difficulties waking up by an alarm alone. Just as some other reviewers have stated, my parents would have to come wake me because I would turn my alarms off in my sleep and have no recollection of it in the morning. Angry parents and reprimands from my employer forced me to find a solution. 
At first, I tried the famed Screamin’ Meanie. If you, or any of your friends are truck drivers, you know what I’m talking about. A device that boasts a 120 decibel alarm. That’s equivalent to a chainsaw running beside your bed and almost as loud as a military jet aircraft taking off beside your head. Needless to say, I most definitely did not sleep through this alarm. But neither did my chihuahua who sleeps soundly beside me. The first morning of use, I could see the discomfort and panic in my poor pooches eyes as I scrambled to turn the contraption off (which isn’t easy or user-friendly, may I add.) I knew this hearing-damaging alarm wasn’t for me immediately.
That’s when I searched and came across my beloved Alarmy. I will forever sing it’s praises as it has saved my career, education, and sanity many times. With its variable loudness settings I can assure that it’s loud enough to wake me but not so loud that my dog goes deaf. I prefer the easy math equation task; difficult enough to force me into thinking clearly, but not so difficult that I’m frantically trying to use my calculator while an alarm is blaring in my ear. For a free app, this guy has all the best features and settings anyone could desire out of an alarm clock. I mean, come on, what all do you really want to customize about an alarm? 😂 Oh, and did I mention that there’s no annoying ads that most free apps unfortunately have? Well, it doesn’t and I appreciate that aspect because who wants a thirty second ad popping up while trying to turn an alarm off at the crack of dawn! 
So all-in-all, I highly recommend this app and hope the creators never change the format or functions. If you’re a heavy sleeper like I am, you must give Alarmy a try! 😊

title: Fell down the stairs and got out of work
body: This app is amazing! I set it up so I had to take a picture in order to stop the alarm. I figured I’d give a big middle finger to morning me and make myself go downstairs to take a picture of the coffee maker in order for the alarm to stop. Smart idea right? Then I can just turn on the coffee maker and get my day started. Well the alarm started going off and for some reason I chose the siren at full blast so I went full panic mode. My wife started yelling at me to turn it off and my baby in the next room over woke up and started crying. In my frantic half asleep panic I jumped out of bed faster than I have in years. I started rushing downstairs and ended up slipping and falling down the last 10 or so stairs and busting my nose on the railing. No time for self care. Gotta snap a pic of coffee maker. I finally get the picture and turn off the deafening alarm to find my face and shirt covered in blood. I figured I’d take a pic of that as well and text it to my boss. She said to take the day off so I washed up and went back to bed. The results were better than I ever could have dreamed. Here’s to hoping it works just as well tomorrow! Thanks for an amazing app

title: Needs an alternative option for deactivating alarms
body:
I’ve been using the very loud alarms, that’s been getting me up in the morning better than anything else and because of the picture taking mission it’s also made me actually get out of bed so I stay awake. The only problem with that is this morning, it wasn’t accepting the same picture I always took.

I had set it to be the bathroom vent fan that’s on the ceiling because it’s reasonably far away from my bed and also unlikely to ever change enough to not be accepted, but apparently not. This morning it just wouldn’t stop, which is inconvenient when the room is also next to another bedroom with sleeping people inside.

I had to momentarily delete the app to get it to stop because the alarms also force the volume to always be at max so you can’t quiet it down. I don’t know why it wasn’t accepting the image as it did every other morning since I got the app about two or three weeks ago, but I’ve had to reset all the settings after redownloading. I think that there should be the ability to choose secondary challenges so that you aren’t just stuck whenever there’s some error for whatever reason and have to delete the app.

Other than this mornings issues, the app has been great. I used to not wake up very well regardless of what alarm sound I was using, but that’s not an option now. It’s enabled me to get a job after an extended unemployment after being laid off because I just couldn’t get to sleep until 3 AM at minimum because I couldn’t wake up until noon. Great app, just needs a secondary option for turning off alarms that isn’t hidden behind a paywall

title: Best Alarm I’ve Ever Had
body:
I am almost 30 and I’m the absolute worst at waking up in the morning. Growing up, I used to drive my mom crazy because I have some sort of magically ability to go back to sleep no matter how many times she tried to wake me up. Now that I’ve started a career, I’ve struggled with the same problem and nothing seemed to help. I found this app one night hoping it would work and it has seriously changed my life. I no longer worry about accidentally sleeping through all my alarms because it is impossibly with Alarmy. 

The barcode scanner makes you scan an item’s barcode. For me, it’s my deodorant in the bathroom. It makes me get up. I actually forgot to bring the item with me on a work trip that I set up to scan and I had to delete the app! It wouldn’t stop going off! That may sound crazy but it is exactly the type of alarm I need! You can’t just close this app, even in the background and make it go off. It just keeps going until you get up. 

I love it.

title: Fantastic when it works! Until it doesn't.
body:
I've been using Alarmy for months. I love the options for missions, and I've found that using the barcode scanner to make me scan a lotion bottle in my bathroom has really made a difference in forcing me to get up and stay up, something no alarm before has ever managed to reliably do for me. 

Until this morning. Last night I set the same alarms in the same way I always do. I turned up the volume and ringer on my phone as usual. Yet this morning I woke up three hours late. Best I can tell, Alarmy enabled some sort of mute function, so the alarms went off, but silently. Not sure what use a silent alarm app has. If I want a gentle reminder alarm, I'll use the built in Apple alarm. 

I love Alarmy and want to continue using it, but I can only do that if I can trust that it won't enable this mute mode again.

title: Best decision for more stress-free mornings
body: This alarm clock has changed my mornings! I have always struggled with waking up, setting AT LEAST 4 alarm clocks which would all be dismissed. When finally I’d wake up, I struggled to make myself get out of bed, especially in the winter. I’d do math in my head of how much longer I could lay there and ultimately end up rushing each day to get to work. My brother told me about this alarm and it’s changed everything! I use a barcode on my refrigerator so that I have to get out of bed to scan it. Once I’m out of bed, I have no problem staying awake! No more stressful rushing to leave! The only time it did not work was when I accidentally closed out of the app while my phone was on do not disturb. The alarm didn’t make any sound until 8 am (3 hours after I had scheduled it) when do not disturb automatically shut off. The app does warn, however, that it needs to run in the background to work. I would highly recommend this app to everyone!!

title: This app changed my life!
body:
I take medication at night that makes me wake up feeling super tired. I used to set 10-15 alarms just to make sure I got out of bed. I’ve tried so many different ways to get myself out of bed, but tired morning me always finds a way to get around waking up. My brain ended up getting used to hearing the alarm and started to associate it with hitting the snooze button, instead of associating it with actually waking up. 

Now, as soon as I pick up my phone to turn off my alarm I am forced to use my brain by doing very basic tasks that seem impossible when you’re tired and lazy. My two favorite “missions” to complete are the memorize game and the barcode scanner. With the scanner l like to make the mission to scan an item in my kitchen, so I literally have to get out of bed. Also, the ringtones are 10/10. I’ve been using the app for a few weeks and the first few notes of “Orkney” bring me out of my precious slumber every time without fail.

Amazing app. Thanks to the people who dreamed this app into existence (I had to).
